articles.title: Art Programs in Lebanon Bring Beauty to Midst of Crisis
articles.summary: With Lebanon currently being impacted by war, a refugee crisis, and more, stories of beauty can be hard to come across. For ministries active in Lebanon, meeting the spiritual, physical...
articles.summary_zh: 黎巴嫩目前受到战争、难民危机等影响, 对活跃在黎巴嫩的各部来说,满足一个国家的精神、身体和情感需求,只是为了生存而努力,这可能会造成损失。 Horizons International的Pierre Houssney说,尽管由于人类在罪恶世界中的堕落,国家仍然面临创伤,但上帝仍然创造了一个包含美丽的世界。 “我认为,美丽对人们的心来说是关于上帝的,特别是当它不仅仅是为美丽着想,而是以基督为名的美丽时,”Houssney说。 “在创伤中,在贫困中,我们试图给那些拥有艺术天赋的信徒机会,通过他们的艺术向社会发出先知的声音,以便在危机中呼唤基督。
articles.title_zh: 黎巴嫩的艺术项目将美丽带入危机
articles.content: With Lebanon currently being impacted by war, a refugee crisis, and more, stories of beauty can be hard to come across. For ministries active in Lebanon, meeting the spiritual, physical and emotional needs of a country just trying to survive can take its toll. Horizons International’s Pierre Houssney said that despite the trauma the country faces due to the fallenness of man in a sinful world, God has still created a world that contains beauty. “And I think that beauty speaks to people’s hearts about God, especially when it’s not just beauty, you know, for beauty’s sake, but when it’s beauty in the name of Christ,” Houssney said. “In the midst of the trauma, in the midst of the poverty, we’re trying to give opportunities for believers, who have artistic gifts, to have a prophetic voice through their art to the society, so that we can be calling out for Christ in the midst of the crisis.” Some of these opportunities for creating beauty are fine art classes offered by Horizons International. Horizons International has had up to 35 students at one time participating in these classes revolving around painting or drawing. Students in visual arts classes had the opportunity to participate in an exhibition in Beirut called “His Touch.” People from the community were invited to see the work of beginner students as well as 10 different Christian artists. Graphic design classes offer a more practical element, allowing students to learn a skill they could use in their everyday lives. On the worship side of things, music theory and classes in instruments are helping raise up worship leaders for local churches. One unit teaching guitar, piano, and drums to beginners looking to lead worship at their church had 70 people participate. “And so this new generation needs training, and they need, you know, they need mentoring, and they need to have those skills so that they can, they can lead their congregations in worship,” Houssney said. Though some may have more trouble connecting visual arts directly with ministry, Houssney says social media helps make that connection more clear. Beautiful videos that contain scripture messages alongside visual art tend to get a higher viewership. When posts like that get more views, they can potentially bring more people to Christ. “And so it needs to be beautiful. It needs to be excellent, it needs to be well done. And that’s what our Lord deserves,” Houssney said. “That’s not just what social media deserves.” Currently, Horizons International has to spread resources between humanitarian aid like food and medicine and projects that glorify God through the arts. In the midst of the crisis in Lebanon, pray for God to provide the resources for canvases, studio spaces, art instructors and more. Houssney also says what an organization like Horizons International is here for is to see God open more and more hearts to the Gospel. “So I’m not praying that the church would have less hardship. I’m not praying for you know, for less, you know, political chaos. What I’m praying for is that, through it all, people would continue to open their hearts, and that God will be glorified.” Learn more about the work of Horizons International in Lebanon by visiting https://www.horizonsinternational.org/lebanon-crisis .
articles.content_zh: 黎巴嫩目前受到战争、难民危机等影响, 对活跃在黎巴嫩的各部来说,满足一个国家的精神、身体和情感需求,只是为了生存而努力,这可能会造成损失。 Horizons International的Pierre Houssney说,尽管由于人类在罪恶世界中的堕落,国家仍然面临创伤,但上帝仍然创造了一个包含美丽的世界。 “我认为,美丽对人们的心来说是关于上帝的,特别是当它不仅仅是为美丽着想,而是以基督为名的美丽时,”Houssney说。 “在创伤中,在贫困中,我们试图给那些拥有艺术天赋的信徒机会,通过他们的艺术向社会发出先知的声音,以便在危机中呼唤基督。” 其中一些创造美貌的机会是地平线国际提供的精美艺术课. 地平线国际曾经有多达35名学生参加这些围绕绘画或绘画而旋转的课. 视觉艺术课的学生有机会在贝鲁特参加一个名为“他的触摸”的展览。 社区人士被邀请观看初学者和10名不同的基督教艺术家的作品. 图形设计课程提供了更实用的元素,让学生学习在日常生活中可以使用的技能. 在事物的崇拜方面,乐器中的音乐理论和课程正在帮助培养地方教会的崇拜领袖. 一个教吉他,钢琴,和鼓的单位在他们的教堂里为初学者寻找引领崇拜,有70人参加. “因此,这新一代需要培训,他们需要,你知道,他们需要指导,他们需要这些技能,以便他们能够领导他们的教会进行礼拜。” 虽然有些人可能更难直接将视觉艺术与部委联系起来, 包含经文信息与视觉艺术的美丽视频往往获得更高的收视率. 当这样的帖子获得更多的观点时,它们有可能将更多的人带入基督. “因此,它必须是美丽的。 它需要出色,需要做得很好。 这才是我们的主应得的。 这不仅仅是社交媒体应得的。 目前,地平线国际必须在食品和医药等人道主义援助和通过艺术来赞美上帝的项目之间分配资源。 在黎巴嫩危机中,祈求上帝为画布、工作室空间、艺术教员等提供资源。 霍斯尼还说,像地平线国际这样的组织在这里是为了看到上帝对"福音"越来越开放的心. 我并不祈祷教会会减少困难。 我并不是为你们祈祷, 我所祈祷的是,通过这一切,人们将继续敞开心扉,而上帝将受到赞美。” 透过访问https://www.horisonsinternational.org/lebanon-crisis,

articles.title_zh: v.容忍
articles.content: This incident took place over 15 years ago, and yet, I remember it clearly.  In the buzz of daily life, it is easy to get caught up in the carelessness of the checklists, and forget the intentionality of abiding in Him. I remember how frantic I was once at or late deadline and how frustrated I was at all the problems we were having in getting the program together.  We’d all kinds of equipment failure throughout the day and I was going to have to drive the program across town to get it uploaded to the satellite.  It was already 7 pm and the babysitter was calling me every 10 minutes. Then, I got a call from a lady with a gentle Creole accent. She told me, “I felt led to call you and pray with you.”  I SO didn’t want to talk to this lady, wasn’t interested in being prayed over, and really just wanted to leave to get this program fed and pick my 2-year old up.  I was impatient when I responded to her.  Rather than take insult from what was probably a curt rebuff,  she just said , “Wow. You REALLY need the peace of our heavenly Father on your heart right now.” And…she burst out in song.   Now I’m wondering why I’m on the phone with this crazy lady, and then she prayed through the worship song and then rolled right into praying for me, for my distress, for the things I thought I needed to do…and prayed that I would be still and listen, that my heart would be quiet long enough to remember the awe of God, and that the joy would come back to my heart as we produced MNN… The more she prayed, the more convicted I grew and I realized I was caught up in the ‘do’ and not the ‘be’…and THEN she pulled out the big guns: the story of Mary and Martha. Luke 10:38-42 New International Version (NIV) At the Home of Martha and Mary 38 As Jesus and his disciples were on their way, he came to a village where a woman named Martha opened her home to him. 39 She had a sister called Mary, who sat at the Lord’s feet listening to what he said. 40 But Martha was distracted by all the preparations that had to be made. She came to him and asked, “Lord, don’t you care that my sister has left me to do the work by myself? Tell her to help me!” 41 “Martha, Martha,” the Lord answered, “you are worried and upset about many things, 42 but few things are needed—or indeed only one. [ a ] Mary has chosen what is better, and it will not be taken away from her.” She ended our conversation with, “Sometimes, it’s ok to be Mary and sit at the feet of Jesus.  Stuff will still be there to do. It will eventually get done.  But the lasting investment is remembering to sit and BE at the feet of Jesus.” It was a much needed gentle rebuke along with a little encouragement from an unknown sister in Christ that I still remember to this day…thousands of productions later.   What we do is important…but not at the risk of forgetting to abide in Christ.

articles.title_zh: Koinonia
articles.content: Koinonia (Koy-no-nee’-ah) is a Greek word, occurring 20 times in the Bible, which means “fellowship” or “brotherly love.” It carries with it the meaning of a committed, trustworthy, and dependable relationship. Such a relationship can be experienced through participation, sharing, giving, and contributing. The first occurrence of koinonia is Acts 2:42 “They devoted themselves to the apostles’ teaching and to the fellowship, to the breaking of bread and to prayer.” But the rest of the passage reads:  “ 43 Everyone was filled with awe at the many wonders and signs performed by the apostles. 44 All the believers were together and had everything in common. 45 They sold property and possessions to give to anyone who had need. 46 Every day they continued to meet together in the temple courts. They broke bread in their homes and ate together with glad and sincere hearts, 47 praising God and enjoying the favor of all the people. And the Lord added to their number daily those who were being saved.” Christian fellowship is a key aspect of the Christian life. Believers in Christ are to come together in love, faith, and encouragement. The essence of koinonia: “one another”. Scripture commands us to be devoted to one another (Romans 12:10), honor one another (Romans 12:10), live in harmony with one another (Romans 12:16; 1 Peter 3:8), accept one another (Romans 15:7), serve one another in love (Galatians 5:13), be kind and compassionate to one another (Ephesians 4:32), admonish one another (Colossians 3:16), encourage one another (1 Thessalonians 5:11; Hebrews 3:13), spur one another on toward love and good deeds (Hebrews 10:24), offer hospitality (1 Peter 4:9), and love one another (1 Peter 1:22; 1 John 3:11; 3:23; 4:7; 4:11-12). Koinonia is translated many different ways in English Bibles: -fellowship (koinonia), to the breaking of bread and the prayers.” -contribution (koinonia) for them and for all others.” Paul writes to the believers in Philippi: “That I may know him and the power of his resurrection, and may share (koinonia) his sufferings, becoming like him in his death” (Phil 3:10). – Christian living– the dynamic whole of it. It describes an interactive relationship between God and believers who are sharing new life through Christ.  It captures the entirety of this relationship. It involves active participation in Christian community: sharing in spiritual blessings and giving material blessings. How does this idea fit into the theology of ‘And’? Acts 1:8—it empowers us with the chisomo—the grace to DO—the all-inclusive– “But you will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes on you; and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the ends of the earth.” And they will know you by your love.  (John 13:35)   “By this everyone will know that you are my disciples, if you love one another.”

articles.content: Isaiah 54:10  Though the mountains be shaken and the hills be removed, yet my unfailing love for you will not be shaken nor my covenant of peace be removed,” says the LORD, who has compassion on you. There is something of music in the very sound of these words. The thought that lies below them, sweeping as it does through the whole creation, and parting all things into the transient and eternal, the mortal and immortal, is still greater than the music of the words. ‘These’ are removed; ‘this’ abides. The thing in God which abides is all-gentle tenderness, that strange love mightier than all the powers of Deity beside, permanent with the permanence of His changeless heart. ‘My loving kindness and the covenant of My peace,’ outlast everything else. The antithesis of what passes and what abides is mind-boggling. ‘all things are in a state of flux’—it’s a basic tenant of physical science…and yet it seems as unchanging as anything we know…it’s the shape of the box…and yet,  if we had nothing abiding beyond this universe, what would be the point? There’s an unspoken  ‘But’  here–  in that vacuum, the Great Spirit moves all the material universe, Himself unmoved, undiminished by creation, or by said vacuum.  The Unknowable whose name means ‘breath’ is YHWH—who comes to us in man-form to help the created move toward and abide in this presence. I’m sort of blown away by how big this passage paints God…and blown away that we are His children…and that we able to abide because of Christ…that our part in glorifying Him and enjoying Him forever comes in walking alongside a global family and telling their stories.  Insignificant, by itself, but being used as a tool to help others abide and recognize the mercy and grace of this big Abba. We can touch the face of God…because He calls us to Himself.

articles.summary_zh: 圣经以弗所书: 6: 10-18(NIV) 10 最后,要坚固于主和他强大的力量. 11 穿上上帝的全盔甲,以便你能够采取立场对抗魔鬼的阴谋. 12,因为我们的斗争不是反对血肉之争,而是反对统治者,反对当局,反对这个黑暗世界的力量,反对天界邪恶的精神力量. 13 因此穿上神的全甲,使出恶事之日到来后能站起地来,在做了一切后能站起地来.
articles.title_zh: Innocent As Doves
articles.content: The Scriptures Ephesians 6:10-18 (NIV) 10 Finally, be strong in the Lord and in his mighty power. 11 Put on the full armor of God, so that you can take your stand against the devil’s schemes. 12 For our struggle is not against flesh and blood, but against the rulers, against the authorities, against the powers of this dark world and against the spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly realms. 13 Therefore put on the full armor of God, so that when the day of evil comes, you may be able to stand your ground, and after you have done everything, to stand. 14 Stand firm then, with the belt of truth buckled around your waist, with the breastplate of righteousness in place, 15 and with your feet fitted with the readiness that comes from the gospel of peace. 16 In addition to all this, take up the shield of faith, with which you can extinguish all the flaming arrows of the evil one. 17 Take the helmet of salvation and the sword of the Spirit,which is the word of God. 18 And pray in the Spirit on all occasions with all kinds of prayers and requests. With this in mind, be alert and always keep on praying for all the Lord’s people. Matthew 10:16-20 16 “I am sending you out like sheep among wolves. Therefore be as shrewd as snakes and as innocent as doves. 17 Be on your guard; you will be handed over to the local councils and be flogged in the synagogues. 18 On my account you will be brought before governors and kings as witnesses to them and to the Gentiles.19 But when they arrest you, do not worry about what to say or how to say it. At that time you will be given what to say, 20 for it will not be you speaking, but the Spirit of your Father speaking through you.” Today, it’s just been on my mind to bring our attention back to the armor of God and the fact we need to be wise like serpents, innocent as doves. I want to speak to the first part, being wise like serpents. Going to Malta helped bring to my attention how much I don’t know about my own country’s politics, the refugee crisis, trusting God, and even God’s word. I feel like I’m doing “better than the average U.S. citizen.” But, in reality, I don’t know very much. And I’ve realized when it comes to engaging in conversation with others, it’s important to have a handle on topics like these. I.e., talking with my dad about refugees. Having facts and knowing the what the constitution says helps me to better articulate and defend my stance culturally and based by our country’s laws. Knowing about the situation with refugees abroad also helps and is a tool in dispelling the fear which the current administration seems to use to get support to make the calls it’s trying to make both about refugees and immigrants in general. The second part, being innocent like doves…that’s a hard one for me because I’ve thought in the past it means to be naive. I don’t want to be naïve. But being innocent doesn’t mean you’re naïve. I think it means we guard our hearts and take our thoughts captive. What we put into our minds affects the lens through which we see the world and view the Bible—and it has the power to jade us. I.e., rape. I know rape is in the world. I know it is destructive. I’ve seen it damage lives. And I’ve seen God redeem. But, what I don’t need to do is read the part of a book or watch a TV series which details a situation of rape. I don’t need to invite that in my mind to “know” about rape. I’m thinking of a book one of my youth group girls was reading. I haven’t read it, but I see how she struggles with her sexuality, her relationship with God, and for a period even suicide. I also see how her parents are okay with exposing her to things that are a bit mature for her age. Compared to another one of our girls who is aware of what happens in the world, but her parents are careful to protect her from exposure to things which are dark, damaging, fracture her relationship with God. She’s being taught to be innocent, not naïve (or judgmental), and to take her thoughts captive. Both of these girls come from solid Christian homes. I can’t say for sure that what each of these girls has or hasn’t been exposed to has been the big factor in who they are today, but I think it’s clear it has played a role. No barely 12-year-old girl should be reading intimate details about sex or rape. And while I may think not allowing your 12-year-old to watch Harry Potter could be a little excessive, I see how this other young girl is being shaped to cast her thoughts on what is good and to pursue God in all things. Which leads me to the Armor of God. If we are sheep among wolves, if we are God’s people aware of the spiritual battle around us, we need the armor of God. We need our faith, especially when we don’t have answers to why God is still good in hard situations, but know that he is. We need the encouragement of salvation when doubt comes into our minds if we are truly loved by God. We need to know the scriptures, not just where to find them in the Bible, but to really be so in-tuned we can recite them when necessary. We need the breastplate of righteousness because frankly, the world is watching. And with the armor of God and I think it’s important to ask, do we believe in spiritual warfare? Do we believe the world we live in isn’t just made up of cold, hard facts or only what we can see? When I was talking about spiritual warfare with my friend who’s in Ecuador, she mentioned how we leave ourselves open to it. Every morning we can either be aware that it’s there and pray, or we can disregard it and leave ourselves open. Praying against spiritual warfare isn’t just for the days when we can sense it, but even when we don’t suspect it. With all of this said, I want to encourage each of us to really grab hold of the scriptures, of God, and for what it means to put on God’s armor as well as to be wise like serpents, but innocent as doves.
articles.content_zh: 圣经以弗所书: 6: 10-18(NIV) 10 最后,要坚固于主和他强大的力量. 11 穿上上帝的全盔甲,以便你能够采取立场对抗魔鬼的阴谋. 12,因为我们的斗争不是反对血肉之争,而是反对统治者,反对当局,反对这个黑暗世界的力量,反对天界邪恶的精神力量. 13 因此穿上神的全甲,使出恶事之日到来后能站起地来,在做了一切后能站起地来. 14 站稳了, 真理带系住你的腰部, 胸罩是正义的, 15 和你的脚 与来自和平的福音的准备。 16,除此外,取起信道之盾,用之能灭一切恶道所发之火箭. 17取出救生之盔和"灵剑",这是"神之道". 18,并随各种祷告和请求,在"精神"中作各种祈祷. 考虑到这一点,保持警惕,并始终为主的所有人民祈祷。 Matthew 10:16-20 16 “我把你像羊一样放出狼群。 因此要像蛇一样精明,像鸽子一样无辜. 17 个 人 守 住 ; 交给 地方 议会 、 在 犹太会堂 被 鞭打 . 18,就我而言,你们将被带见总督和国王,作为他们和外邦人的见证。 19,但当他们逮捕你时,不要担心该说什么或怎么说. 在那日,你们得享受你们所应当享受的,20个是你们所应当享受的,只有你们父亲的精神。 今天,我刚刚想到让我们重新关注上帝的盔甲, 以及我们需要像蛇一样聪明, 我想谈谈第一部分,像蛇一样聪明。 前往马耳他让我注意到我对本国政治、难民危机、信任上帝甚至上帝之言一无所知。 我觉得自己比普通美国公民做得更好。 但事实上, 我意识到在与他人对话时, 和我爸谈难民的事 了解事实、了解宪法内容, 有助于我更好地表达和捍卫我的立场, 了解国外难民的情况,也有助于消除现政府似乎用来获得支持的恐惧, 第二部分是像鸽子一样无辜, 我不想天真。 但无辜并不意味着你天真。 我认为这意味着我们保护我们的心 并抓住我们的思想。 我们脑中的东西影响着我们通过这个镜头看到世界并看到圣经——它有制玉的力量。 强奸 我知道强奸在世界上。 我知道这是破坏性的。 我见过它会伤害生命。 我见过上帝赎回。 但我不需要阅读一本书或看一部电视连续剧, 我并不需要邀请她「知道」强奸事件。 我想到一本我的青年团体女孩正在阅读的书。 我还没读过, 但我看到她如何与性、与上帝的关系相抗争, 我也明白她的父母 让她面对一些对她的年龄来说有点成熟的事情是怎样的 和另外一位我们的女孩相比,她知道世界发生的事情,但她的父母很小心地保护她免受那些黑暗,有破坏力,断裂她与上帝关系的东西的暴露. 她被教导自己是无辜的, 这两个女孩都来自坚固的基督教家庭. 我无法肯定每个女孩是否接触过她们, 没有仅仅12岁的女孩应该阅读关于性或强奸的亲密细节。 虽然我可能认为不让你的12岁小孩看"哈利·波特" 可能有点过分,但我明白这个年轻女孩是如何被塑造的, 将她的想法投到什么是好的, 并追求上帝的一切。 这让我找到神的盔甲 如果我们是狼群中的羊,如果我们是上帝的人民,知道我们周围的精神斗争,我们需要上帝的盔甲。 我们需要我们的信念, 尤其是当我们没有答案, 如果我们真的被上帝所爱,我们需要在出现疑虑时鼓励拯救。 我们需要知道经文, 不只是在圣经中找到它们的地方, 而且要真正地调和,我们在必要时可以朗诵它们。 我们需要正义的胸罩 因为坦率地说,世界正在看着。 我们相信精神战争吗? 我们是否相信我们所生活的世界, 我和在厄瓜多尔的朋友谈论精神战时, 每天早上,我们要么意识到它在那里并祈祷,要么我们无视它并敞开大门。 祈祷反抗精神战不仅仅是我们感知到的年代, 说到这里,我想鼓励我们每个人 真正抓住经文,上帝, 以及赋予上帝盔甲的意义,

articles.summary_zh: 创世记13 索·阿布拉姆从埃及出走,向北走入了内盖夫河,与他的妻子和洛特以及他们所拥有的一切. 2 (Abram有非常丰富的牲畜,白银和黄金. 3 他们从内盖夫出发,继续分步向贝瑟尔出行,在贝瑟尔和艾之间搭起帐篷,他们以前在那里扎营. 页:1 这是阿布拉姆建造祭坛的地方,在那里他再次崇拜了主.
articles.title_zh: 亚伯拉罕和洛特
articles.content: Genesis 13 So Abram left Egypt and traveled north into the Negev, along with his wife and Lot and all that they owned. 2 (Abram was very rich in livestock, silver, and gold.) 3 From the Negev, they continued traveling by stages toward Bethel, and they pitched their tents between Bethel and Ai, where they had camped before. 4 This was the same place where Abram had built the altar, and there he worshiped the Lord again. 5 Lot, who was traveling with Abram, had also become very wealthy with flocks of sheep and goats, herds of cattle, and many tents. 6 But the land could not support both Abram and Lot with all their flocks and herds living so close together. 7 So disputes broke out between the herdsmen of Abram and Lot. (At that time Canaanites and Perizzites were also living in the land.) 8 Finally Abram said to Lot, “Let’s not allow this conflict to come between us or our herdsmen. After all, we are close relatives! 9 The whole countryside is open to you. Take your choice of any section of the land you want, and we will separate. If you want the land to the left, then I’ll take the land on the right. If you prefer the land on the right, then I’ll go to the left.” 10 Lot took a long look at the fertile plains of the Jordan Valley in the direction of Zoar. The whole area was well watered everywhere, like the garden of the Lord or the beautiful land of Egypt. (This was before the Lord destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah.) 11 Lot chose for himself the whole Jordan Valley to the east of them. He went there with his flocks and servants and parted company with his uncle Abram. 12 So Abram settled in the land of Canaan, and Lot moved his tents to a place near Sodom and settled among the cities of the plain. 13 But the people of this area were extremely wicked and constantly sinned against the Lord. 14 After Lot had gone, the Lord said to Abram, “Look as far as you can see in every direction—north and south, east and west. 15 I am giving all this land, as far as you can see, to you and your descendants[a] as a permanent possession. 16 And I will give you so many descendants that, like the dust of the earth, they cannot be counted! 17 Go and walk through the land in every direction, for I am giving it to you.” 18 So Abram moved his camp to Hebron and settled near the oak grove belonging to Mamre. There he built another altar to the Lord. At this point in the story, God’s promise to Abraham of the promised land hasn’t come true yet, but good land is part of the promise We’ve seen Abraham have faithful triumphs and failures, but this is a time when Abraham showed great faith once again because there are SEVERAL reasons why Abraham could have taken the better land 1. movement towards God’s promise of good land anyway 2. and this is probably a more striking one to me, but culturally speaking, the older would NEVER defer to the younger. Lot, as the younger, should have deferred to Abraham the older – both in going to him to resolve the disagreement between their herdsmen and in giving him the better pick of land But Abraham wasn’t fixated on culture and on manipulating God’s promises Abraham’s dealings are not in seniority, but in brotherly love and that’s what faith does. Faith resolves tension with generous self-sacrifice Christians often say in tense situations, “Well, I’m not a doormat! I deserve not to be walked all over!” But my pastor said something very striking to me. “Aren’t we glad Christ never said that?” A faithful and generous person doesn’t need to manipulate or control the situation because they are resting in the promises and sovereignty of God Faith leads to trust leads to generosity and self-sacrifice with others.
articles.content_zh: 创世记13 索·阿布拉姆从埃及出走,向北走入了内盖夫河,与他的妻子和洛特以及他们所拥有的一切. 2 (Abram有非常丰富的牲畜,白银和黄金. 3 他们从内盖夫出发,继续分步向贝瑟尔出行,在贝瑟尔和艾之间搭起帐篷,他们以前在那里扎营. 页:1 这是阿布拉姆建造祭坛的地方,在那里他再次崇拜了主. 5,当时正与阿布拉姆一起出行的洛特也变得非常富有了有羊羊群,牛群和许多帐篷. 6个 但土地无法支撑阿布拉姆和洛特 他们所有的羊群和群 生活如此相近。 第7条 亞伯蘭和魯特的牧民,互相爭論; (當時,迦南人和比瑞斯人同住), 8 最后,Abram对Lot说: " 让我们不要让这场冲突发生在我们和牧民之间。 我们毕竟是近亲! 第9条 整个农村都对你开放. 你选择你想要的土地的任何部分 我们就会分开 如果你想让土地在左边,那我就让土地在右边。 如果你喜欢右边的土地,那么我就往左边去。 10 洛特对约旦河谷向左尔方向的肥沃平原进行了长时间的考察. 整个地区到处都有良好的取水,如主的花园或埃及美丽的地. (这是在主毁灭了索多玛和戈莫拉之前) 11 洛特自己选择了他们以东的整个约旦河谷. 他带着他的羊群和仆人去那儿,和他叔叔Abram分道扬镳。 12日,阿布拉姆在迦南地定居,洛特将帐篷搬到了索多姆附近的一个地方,并定居于平地的城市中. 13,但此地之人,极恶而常犯主. 14 在洛特离开后,主对Abram说: " 请你看看每一个方向,即北和南、东和西。 15,我把所有的土地,就你所看到的,作为永久财产,交给你和你的子孙。 十六,我给你这么多的后人,像地上的尘土一样,他们不能被统计! 17 出行,走遍地上,各行各业,我把它赏赐你们。” 18日,阿布拉姆将营地迁至希伯伦并定居在属于马姆雷的橡树林附近. 在那里他又为主建造了一座祭坛. 在故事的这一刻,上帝对亚伯拉罕的允诺还没有实现,但好地是我们所见到的亚伯拉罕有忠实的胜利和失败的诺言的一部分,但此时亚伯拉罕再次表现出了极大的信心,因为有SEVERAL的理由,亚伯拉罕可以夺取更好的地一. 但从文化上讲, 年长者决不会屈从于年轻人。 作为年轻人,洛特应该把年长者留给亚伯拉罕 — — 既去他解决牧民之间的分歧,又让他选择更好的土地 — — 但亚伯拉罕并不热衷于文化和操纵上帝对亚伯拉罕的诺言 — — 亚伯拉罕的交往不是在资历上,而是在兄弟般的爱心上,而这正是信仰的作用。 信仰用慷慨自救的基督徒解决了紧张局势, 我不应该到处走! 但我的牧师对我说了一些非常引人注目的话。 “难道我们不庆幸基督从未这么说吗?” 一个忠诚而慷慨的人不需要操控或控制局势,因为他们沉浸在上帝信仰的承诺中,而主权导致信任导致与他人的慷慨和自我牺牲。

articles.title: God’s comfort
articles.summary: My family still wrestles with what feels like very fresh grief over my dad’s passing last September. There are moments where things hit us and we feel this ache of...
articles.summary_zh: 我父亲去年九月去世, 有些时候 事情袭击了我们 我们感到他缺席很痛苦 我们知道他和他天父在一起 不再受到这个凡人圈子的限制 只是有时候,我们想念他。 我们的救世主, 我们作为基督的追随者, 这些提醒有助于鼓励我们打好这场好仗,使我们继续关注这一奖项。 我今天想到我爸,决定读一些他以前为他剩下的岁月所奉献的部会而作的奉献,"为基督而运输". 当他的健康不能再允许他当上牧师时,他写信给正在服役的卡车司机和牧师。
articles.title_zh: 神的安慰
articles.content: My family still wrestles with what feels like very fresh grief over my dad’s passing last September. There are moments where things hit us and we feel this ache of his absence. We know that he has gone to be with his Heavenly Father and no longer suffers from the limitations of this mortal coil. It’s just that sometimes, we miss him. It’s at those times when something happens that reminds us of the hope that we have in Christ our Savior, of our purpose here as followers of Christ, as co-laborers in the Kingdom of Heaven. These reminders serve as encouragement to fight the good fight, keeping our eyes on the prize. I was thinking of my dad today and decided to read some of the devotionals he used to write for the ministry to which he dedicated his remaining years, Transport for Christ. When his health could no longer allow him to serve onsite as a chaplain, he wrote encouragement to the truck drivers and the chaplains in service. I can hear his voice in these words. There’s great comfort in his reminder. I share his words with you so that you may also take comfort in a greater plan, and in the hope that comes from trusting God is in control: “Most of the time, when we grieve, we grieve over something that’s happened in our lives. But there are also times when we grieve over something that hasn’t happened or “what might have been.” Unrealized expectations and dashed hopes can paralyze us with sadness. We mourn for what we could have had, could have done or could have experienced. We live in a fog as we struggle with our unmet goals and dreams. Are you wrestling with accepting something in your life? Mourning a shattered dream? Instead of focusing on what might have been, try focusing on what is and what could still be. Revising your dreams isn’t bad. It’s realistic. And the sooner you do, the sooner the weight of grief will let go. The fog will lift. Hope will return.”
articles.content_zh: 我父亲去年九月去世, 有些时候 事情袭击了我们 我们感到他缺席很痛苦 我们知道他和他天父在一起 不再受到这个凡人圈子的限制 只是有时候,我们想念他。 我们的救世主, 我们作为基督的追随者, 这些提醒有助于鼓励我们打好这场好仗,使我们继续关注这一奖项。 我今天想到我爸,决定读一些他以前为他剩下的岁月所奉献的部会而作的奉献,"为基督而运输". 当他的健康不能再允许他当上牧师时,他写信给正在服役的卡车司机和牧师。 这些话我都能听到他的声音。 他提醒大家, 我和你们分享他的话,以便你们也能在更大的计划中得到安慰,希望来自信任上帝的希望是控制着:“多数时候,当我们悲伤的时候,我们对生活中发生的事情感到悲伤。 但有时我们也为一些没有发生的事情而悲伤, 未实现的期望和破灭的希望会使我们感到悲哀。 我们对本可以、本可以或本可以经历的事情表示哀悼。 当我们与未实现的目标和梦想相抗争时,我们生活在雾中。 你是在拼命接受你生活中的东西吗? 打破了梦想? 与其专注于可能已经发生的事情,不如专注于现在和可能仍然可能发生的事情。 改变你的梦想并不坏。 这是现实的。 你越早做, 悲伤的重量会越快松开。 雾会升起 希望将回归。”
articles.author: R.B. Klama

articles.title: A chance meeting?
articles.summary: You’ve probably heard someone say ‘There is no such thing as a coincidence’. Usually people nod their heads and murmur agreement, but the real question is “Do you believe it?“...
articles.summary_zh: 你可能已经听到有人说“没有巧合”了。 通常人们点头并含糊其辞,但真正的问题是“你相信吗? ” 难道人们只是希望的思想家,还是上帝真的如此亲密地参与我们的日常生活,以至于他代表我们组织各种活动? 机会会议以后会变成什么?
articles.title_zh: 一相逢
articles.content: You’ve probably heard someone say ‘There is no such thing as a coincidence’. Usually people nod their heads and murmur agreement, but the real question is “Do you believe it?“ Are people just wishful thinkers, or is God really so intimately involved in our daily lives that He orchestrate events on our behalf? What will a chance meeting turn into later? The idea of seeds, planting and harvest is a theme resonant throughout Scripture. Aside from the overt nature of sharing the hope of Christ, there are times we don’t recognize an opportunity at the time, but hindsight has a way of revealing it to us. On my last day in Cairo, I was sitting in the hotel lobby waiting for the rest of the team to come down for checkout. I opened my laptop, and began weeding through emails, and getting pictures uploaded for post, and checking through Facebook. An older gentleman (whom I’d seen at different times all week) came over and said ‘You work too much’. I told him I was just killing time and not really working at all. He began asking me questions about my visit to Cairo. Given the upset of the country, I was still guarding my words very carefully so as not to endanger people who live and minister in Cairo. He began asking more pointed questions like “What do you think of this revolution?” Alarm bells were ringing in my head, so I trod very carefully as I answered. I told him that it was a very exciting time in Egypt’s history. Nothing would ever be the same for the country again. To be here during this growth period was both exhilarating and a little scary. He then asked what my friends thought of the goings on. Now, here I had to be very careful. I asked God for wisdom and told him that depended on who I spoke with. There were some who were very optimistic about the outcome, although they knew there would be a hard period to get there. Others were very pessimistic and a little fearful about what lay ahead for them. Still others were moving forward in confidence. He nodded a few times as I responded to his question, then said, “You should come to Lebanon.” I responded “I would LOVE to come to Lebanon!” So he handed me his business card and said, “E-mail me when you come.” He wrote his email address on the bottom of the card. Initially, I was wary about taking some stranger’s e-mail, but I figured I would not necessarily use it and I did not have to respond by giving him my e-mail. We stood, shook hands and parted. I noted that as he left, he entered a diplomat’s vehicle. Only then did I read his business card. It read “Mahmoud Hammoud, Lebanese Ambassador”. He’s the former Foreign Minister of Lebanon, currently serving as an ambassador. I have no idea why our paths crossed. However, God orchestrated it for some reason. There are no coincidences…just opportunities. I wonder what comes next.
articles.content_zh: 你可能已经听到有人说“没有巧合”了。 通常人们点头并含糊其辞,但真正的问题是“你相信吗?” 难道人们只是希望的思想家,还是上帝真的如此亲密地参与我们的日常生活,以至于他代表我们组织各种活动? 机会会议以后会变成什么? 种子、种植和收割的理念是贯穿整个圣经的主题。 除了分享基督希望的公开性质外, 有时我们并不认同当时的机会, 在开罗的最后一天,我坐在酒店大厅里,等待队伍的其他人下来看病。 我打开了笔记本电脑, 开始通过电子邮件去除草, 一位年长的绅士(我整个星期在不同时间见过他)过来说道:你工作太忙了。 我告诉他我只是在浪费时间 完全没有工作 他开始问我关于我访问开罗的问题。 鉴于这个国家的不安,我仍在非常谨慎地捍卫我的话,以免危及在开罗生活和担任部长的人。 他开始提出更尖锐的问题,如“你对这场革命的看法如何?” 警钟在我脑中响起,所以我回答时非常小心。 我告诉他,这是埃及历史上一个非常激动人心的时刻。 对这个国家来说,一切都不会变了 在这个成长时期来到这里既令人振奋,又有些吓人。 他接着问我的朋友们对事情的看法如何。 现在,我必须非常小心。 我向上帝求取智慧 告诉他这取决于我和谁说话 有些人对结果非常乐观,尽管他们知道要到达那里会有一段困难的时期。 其他人则非常悲观,有些担心未来会如何。 还有一些国家正在以信任的态度向前迈进。 当我回答他的问题时,他点了几次头,然后说:“你应该来黎巴嫩。” 我回应说, 他把他的名片递给我,然后说:“你来了就给我电子邮件。” 他写了他的电子邮件地址 在卡底。 起初,我对收取陌生人的电子邮件很担心,但我想我不一定会使用,我不必通过把电子邮件给他来回应。 我们站了起来,握起手来分开。 我注意到,当他离开时,他进入一名外交官的车辆。 那时我才看他的名片 原文为“黎巴嫩大使马哈穆德·哈穆德”。 现任大使。 我不知道我们为什么要过路 然而,上帝出于某种原因安排了它。 没有巧合 只是机会 不知道接下来会怎样

articles.title: What comes first: chicken or the egg?
articles.summary: One thing I am noticing here is how different the context of ministry is from country to country. You can sometimes THINK you understand the concept of the vehicle, like...
articles.summary_zh: 我在这里注意到的一件事是,部委的背景因国而异。 MNN的Ruth Kramer在执行任务 你有时可以认为你理解汽车的概念, 比如微型企业, 但一旦你听到事情是如何付诸实践的, 什么可行什么不可行, 你就会开始看到微妙之处的出现。 例如,我们昨天会见了一个协助社区发展的伙伴。 他们毫不羞愧地信奉基督教, 因为福音书是他们所做的一切的一部分.
articles.title_zh: 先吃鸡还是先吃鸡蛋？
articles.content: One thing I am noticing here is how different the context of ministry is from country to country. MNN's Ruth Kramer on assignment. You can sometimes THINK you understand the concept of the vehicle, like micro-enterprise, but once you hear how things are put into practice, what works and what doesn’t, you begin to see the subtleties emerge. For example, we met with a partner yesterday who assists community development. They are unashamedly Christian, because the Gospel is part of everything they do…however, they know that dealing with poverty is a ‘must’, as well. So, which came first, the chicken (community development) or the egg (Gospel)? Can they be done simultaneously and be effective? Do you really just have two eggs or two chickens? The clear answer on that was: ‘We have an egg, it becomes a chicken’. Folks, that’s the answer to the question of questions. The hope of Christ changes the outlook for the poor in this context. The other big question was how the community development works in the Egyptian Muslim context in the rural areas. It is in these places where it’s likely opposition will rise up and equate physical attacks. The mindset is quite different. Micro-enterprise comes up at this point. In some Asian countries, the structure of a micro-enterprise program works like this: church committee sees community member in need (often a believer under the discipleship of the pastor), they provide a loan so this person can start a small business–i.e.—buy a sewing machine to make clothes, or a couple of goats to make cheese and sell milk…from the profits, the person tithes to the church, enabling the support of the pastor…and the person is more able to support him/herself. However, when I asked about the structure of the micro-enterprise, it can’t work that way in the Egyptian context. There are lots of things that can really be misinterpreted within the social structure (and Islam) and this is one of them. The set up of the program is similar, but different because it’s tailor-made to fit the need of the people and the mission of the group. That just struck me. I had made an assumption that all micro-enterprise was the same. I made similar assumptions about vocational training programs, literacy programs, etc (thinking I adjusting for a different context, language, etc). I think it’s kind of a colonialistic thinking that we slip into. It’s kind of like providing someone a loaf of bread (mission field)…from the grocery store (missionary). They need the food to stay alive, but the plastic around the bread is giving them indigestion. They need to prepare the bread the way they now how and all we need to do is supply the ingredients (resources) and the recipe (training). Yes, I know you might be thinking ‘well, duh’. It is one thing to say it and to think you might even understand it, it is another thing entirely to actually see it with my own eyes, hear what works and what doesn’t from the guys implementing helps. By the way, because they do this work well, they have just come under scrutiny. One of this ministry’s main offices was raided by the Egyptian government this week, and the hard drive with the database was taken. All of their records on every program were on it. Everything is exposed. Their face is an NGO and they are well-known. With the events that have occurred in Egypt over the last month, it’s no surprise they’re looking at all NGO’s. Please pray for this team. They are careful, and they are smart. Most of all, they want to share the hope of Christ with those they encounter. That love for people permeates everything they touch…including the chickens in the coop…and eggs in the community. Works for me…
articles.content_zh: 我在这里注意到的一件事是,部委的背景因国而异。 MNN的Ruth Kramer在执行任务 你有时可以认为你理解汽车的概念, 比如微型企业, 但一旦你听到事情是如何付诸实践的, 什么可行什么不可行, 你就会开始看到微妙之处的出现。 例如,我们昨天会见了一个协助社区发展的伙伴。 他们毫不羞愧地信奉基督教, 因为福音书是他们所做的一切的一部分. 那么,什么是第一位的, 鸡(社区发展)还是蛋(Gospel)? 它们能否同时进行并有效? 你真的有两只蛋还是两只鸡? 答案是:我们有一个鸡蛋,它变成了一只鸡。 各位,这就是问题答案。 基督的希望改变了穷人在这方面的前景。 另一个大问题是社区发展如何在农村地区埃及穆斯林背景下运作。 这些地方很可能会有人反对, 心态完全不同。 此时小微企业也出现了. 在一些亚洲国家,微型企业计划的结构是这样运作的:教会委员会看到社区成员有需要(常常是牧师门徒下的信徒),他们提供贷款,以便此人能够创办小企业,即购买缝纫机来做衣服,或买一对山羊来做起司和卖牛奶. 从利润中,一个人一分之一到教堂,使牧师能够支持.这个人更有能力支持自己。 然而,当我问到微型企业的结构时,在埃及不可能如此。 在社会结构(和伊斯兰教)中, 有许多事情可以真正被误解, 节目的设置类似,但因适合人民的需要和团体的使命而有所不同. 这让我很吃惊 我假设所有微型企业都是一样的 我对职业培训计划,扫盲计划等做出了类似的假设(认为我适应不同的环境,语言等). 我认为我们滑入的是一种殖民主义思想。 像是从杂货店(Missionary)提供面包。 他们需要食物才能活下来 但面包周围的塑料 让他们消化不良 他们需要用他们现在的方式准备面包,我们需要做的就是提供原料(资源)和食谱(培训)。 是的,我知道你可能在想,“好,好” 并且认为你可能甚至能理解, 以我自己的眼光亲眼目睹, 顺便说一句,因为他们做得很好,他们刚刚受到审查。 埃及政府本周突袭了该部的一个主要办公室, 他们在每个程序上的所有记录都在上面。 一切众生被所出. 他们的外表是非政府组织,是众所周知的。 在埃及上个月发生的事件中, 请为这支队伍祈祷. 他们很小心,很聪明。 最重要的是,他们想与所遭遇的人分享基督的希望. 这种对人的爱贯穿了他们所接触的一切... 包括笼子里的鸡... 和社区的鸡蛋. 为我工作...

articles.title: The power of prayer unleashed
articles.summary: Last night, I attended a prayer meeting at a church in downtown Cairo, near Tahrir Square. The church was gathering to cry out to God in their distress over the...
articles.summary_zh: 昨晚,我参加了在开罗市中心的一座教堂举行的祈祷会,该教堂靠近塔里尔广场. 埃及的MNN 教会正在集会 向上帝呼喊 在他们的痛苦 最近的国内事件, 当我们一起唱歌,一起崇拜,互相鼓励时,我经历了一些我从未经历过的事情. 我是一个相当有保留的人, 是在大难之时,我走出了自己的道路,倒向了主的叩头. 昨晚,虽然我周围的每个人都用阿拉伯语祈祷,但我发现自己在主面前谦卑并加入了那场叫喊的合唱.
articles.title_zh: 释放祈祷的力量
articles.content: Last night, I attended a prayer meeting at a church in downtown Cairo, near Tahrir Square. MNN in Egypt The church was gathering to cry out to God in their distress over the recent events in the country, and cry out, they did. As we sang together, worshiped together, and encouraged one another, I experienced something I have never experienced before. I’m a fairly reserved person and I am even more so in prayer. It is in times of great distress that I get out of my own way and fall before the Lord prostrate. Last night, although everyone around me was praying in Arabic, I found myself humbled before the Lord and joining in that chorus of crying out. The pastor was beyond ‘crying out’….he was screaming and sobbing before the Lord, as was much of this nearly 1,000 person gathering. Here they were, in prayer before God, confessing, repenting, requesting and rejoicing…even as tear gas seeped into the courtyard from Tahrir Square. All of a sudden, I found myself reminding God of His promises, and asking Him to give comfort to His bride in Egypt, to give them hope and wisdom and to be asking with a fierceness I had not ever before encountered…and moments later, the pastor or worship leader would be saying the same thing, or using the same verse, or introducing the song on the same topic…that happened over and over last night. An immediate confirmation of God’s response left me stunned. Much of what I have heard from Egypt’s Christians that I have encountered has been this is a year of prophecy coming true. There is a GREAT confidence in many of the church leaders and congregations in forging ahead… The other thing that we’re often hearing is that Egypt’s Church is not ‘persecuted’ so much as it is a church under pressure. The boldness of this family is so encouraging, and such a reminder of the presence of the Holy Spirit…especially as they go out with joy to tend to the wounded people coming into the field hospital set up in their courtyard. The confirmation of God’s answers to prayer gives a great boldness to those on the frontlines of the missional movement in Egypt. While bombings, riots and general chaos looks really bad in the headlines (and it is happening), fear is not the response of this emboldened Body. Church leaders we have met with all over the city have said the same thing ‘The wall of fear is broken’. Change is coming. Egypt will have her Revolution…and its face is the Church.
articles.content_zh: 昨晚,我参加了在开罗市中心的一座教堂举行的祈祷会,该教堂靠近塔里尔广场. 埃及的MNN 教会正在集会 向上帝呼喊 在他们的痛苦 最近的国内事件, 当我们一起唱歌,一起崇拜,互相鼓励时,我经历了一些我从未经历过的事情. 我是一个相当有保留的人, 是在大难之时,我走出了自己的道路,倒向了主的叩头. 昨晚,虽然我周围的每个人都用阿拉伯语祈祷,但我发现自己在主面前谦卑并加入了那场叫喊的合唱. 牧师已经超越了“哭出声来”的范围, 他们在这里向上帝祈祷,忏悔、悔改、请求并欢欣鼓舞, 突然间,我发现自己提醒了上帝他的承诺,要求他安慰他的埃及新娘,给他们以希望和智慧,并以我从未遇到过的激烈要求. . . 立即确认上帝的反应,使我感到震惊。 我从埃及基督徒那里听到的大多是今年的预言。 许多教会领袖和会众对前进充满信心... 我们经常听到的另外一件事是,埃及的教会并没有像压力下的一个教会那样被 " 迫害 " 。 这个家庭的胆量是如此鼓舞人心,如此地提醒着圣灵的存在...... 特别是当他们欢快地出门去照顾受伤的人进入他们院子里建立的野外医院时. 在埃及传教运动的前线, 虽然爆炸、暴动和普遍混乱在头条新闻上看起来非常糟糕(而且正在发生), 我们与全市的教会领袖都说过同样的话:恐惧之墙被打破了。 变化即将到来。 埃及将会有她的革命... 它的脸是教会。

articles.title: Best Practices from Evangelistically Effective Churches
articles.summary: While thousands of Americans are dechurching, some churches are baptizing many new members. Here’s how the country’s most evangelistically effective churches are sharing the gospel.
articles.summary_zh: https://media. thegospelcoalition. org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/2310213/ 有效-福音主义. mp3 互联网档案馆的存檔,存档日期2013-12-21.
articles.title_zh: 传福音有效教会的最佳实践
articles.content: https://media.thegospelcoalition.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/23102213/effective-evangelism.mp3 In the summer of 2021, pastor Luke Peterson moved to Columbus, Ohio, to look for lost people. To find them, he joined a gym. He started building friendships. And then he began asking those friends if they wanted to come over. “Word started getting around—‘You’re not going to believe this, but Luke’s a pastor,’” he said. ‘It created some intrigue, and people started coming. I used to have a note in my phone of how many people came to our church because I went to CrossFit Grandview. It was up to like 60 or 70 before I stopped counting because it was impossible.” Peterson’s good at evangelism, and his church is too—last year, they welcomed around 500 first-time visitors. When he preaches, he knows about half his audience is probably unchurched. Pastor Luke Peterson (right) chats with Capital Church attendees / Courtesy of Capital Church Facebook This is unusual in a country where 40 million adults have stopped attending church over the last 30 years, and where 76 percent of pastors said “fostering connections with unchurched people” is a need in their church. Much has changed since the Billy Graham rallies of the ’60s, the door-knocking of the ’80s, and seeker-sensitive church billboards of the ’90s. In the past, “you could randomly walk up to the person pumping gas next to you and say, ‘Do you know Jesus?’” said Perimeter Church pastor Jeff Norris. “Could that still work? Sure. But more and more, we tell people to invite neighbors into their home. The reality is that evangelism is much slower, and more relational, than it used to be.” Today, people aren’t as likely to read the Bible, think it’s the Word of God, or go to church . But they’re also less hostile to Christianity than they were five years ago. And while they read the Bible less—especially in Gen Z—the trajectory is moving up . “We’re not past ‘my truth, your truth,’” said Rob Warren, pastor of Doxa Church in Madison, Wisconsin. “But people aren’t as sure that their truth is actually true.” These days, evangelistically effective churches are keeping evangelism front of mind in the way they preach, train, and encourage their congregations. They’re celebrating small wins. And they’re leading with a high view of Scripture, prayer, and God’s sovereignty. “We’ve seen all of our ministries grow—from kids to youth to college ministry to Doxa Church as a whole,” Warren said. “It’s not just one demographic of people who are getting saved. God’s doing something.” Times Have Changed Thirty years ago, evangelical churches leaned on programs like Evangelism Explosion or Continuous Witness Training to deliver evangelistic focus and training, church leader Thom Rainer said . Those structured initiatives fit well in a culture that was more Christian and more institutionalized—it took an average of 20 church members to reach one person for Christ per year. Today, it takes 50, Rainer said . “Evangelism efficacy, evangelism effectiveness, has definitely diminished.” That trend is likely to continue. As social media and AI fill our time and increase our social anxiety, even relational evangelism is growing more difficult. As social media and AI fill our time and increase our social anxiety, even relational evangelism is growing more difficult. “I’ve got a new couple that moved into my neighborhood a while ago, and I haven’t even seen them yet,” said Daniel Simmons, executive pastor of campuses and central discipleship at The Summit Church. This means equipping the congregation is more challenging—and important—than ever before. “Evangelism can be this thing that is so burdensome and guilt-driven,” said pastor Christian Gracia. He planted King’s City Church in Las Vegas in 2024 with around 80 people and has seen the church grow to more than 400. “People can feel like they’re not ready or not good enough at evangelism,” Gracia said. “They don’t always know what to say, and can feel like a terrible Christian because they don’t do it. And I always want to help them understand that’s not true.” Start with Leadership If church leaders want to create a culture of evangelism in their church, there’s only one place to start, said Warren, who has baptized 150 people in the last eight months. “Tell me 10 people that you’ve shared the gospel with over the last month or two,” he said. “Because if the leadership team is not doing that, then it’s just an aspirational thing and you’re not going to be able to sustain it. You need those ‘just the other day’ stories.” At Perimeter, they’re putting structure around this. This PCA megachurch in Atlanta was planted by a gifted evangelist, Randy Pope, in 1977. Over the years, they’ve seen thousands come to Christ. But last spring, during a staff training, Norris noticed the focus had slipped. “What we tend to do, if left unto ourselves, if church leaders aren’t constantly pushing, is default to what is comfortable,” he said. “Church becomes more about me and my comfort or what my children need. . . . If you don’t constantly keep pushing on evangelism, it’s going to become too big of a burden and people will stop doing it.” Perimeter Church has grown largely through evangelism / Courtesy of Perimeter Church He saw this during Perimeter’s two-day staff workshop: “It became a bit more evident that most of us aren’t making disciples,” he said. “I told them—starting with the executive leadership team all the way down—that their supervisor is going to begin asking them what’s going on in their personal ministry.” This isn’t quota-driven, like “How many times have you shared the gospel this week?” It’s more along the lines of “Who are you praying for who doesn’t know Jesus?” “How are you trusting the Lord to provide opportunities for you to share the gospel with that person?” And then, “Have you been able to have those conversations? If so, how have those gone? Is there anything I can be praying for?” Over at The Summit Church, pastored by evangelist J. D. Greear, similar conversations are taking place. “We only grew 2 percent this year—we have not grown much over the past few years,” Simmons said. “We did some real soul searching in the spring, and found that our people have lost that invitation culture.” So Summit staff are reminding themselves of their goals. “Every ministry needs to know how they contribute to reaching lost people with the gospel, including the ones that may not intuitively do it,” Simmons said. “We’ve got a strong prayer ministry here. How does prayer contribute to reaching lost people? They should know that. Our deacon ministry should know how they contribute to reaching lost people. Our small group ministry should know how they contribute to reaching lost people.” Preaching As leaders begin to share their faith, it’ll come out in their conversations: “Just the other day, I was talking to a guy . . .” This is especially powerful if it comes from the pulpit—and that’s only the beginning of how pastors can use their platform to encourage the spread of the gospel. In a recent sermon, Gracia talked about truth and morality, explaining ideas such as postmodernism and cultural relativism. Christian Gracia preaching at King’s City Church in Las Vegas in October 2026 / Courtesy of King’s City Church YouTube “We’re not trying to win arguments,” he told his congregation. “I’m not trying to give you ammo for the water cooler. I’m trying to help you understand the world you live in. I’m giving you names for the water you’re swimming in, and then trying to help you navigate it. There are actually great reasons for what you believe. And there are also people who are seeking better answers than they have.” The Sunday teaching is primarily for believers. But it can be done in a way that’s aware others are there to “come and see” (John 1:39). “People have shown a lot of courage and risked a lot of relational capital to bring their friends along,” Peterson said. “When you’re sitting next

articles.title: We Need to Know Our Reformed Roots
articles.summary: This volume is an invitation to rediscover that heritage and to find fresh encouragement in the faithfulness of God, who has sustained his church through the centuries.
articles.summary_zh: 改革意味着什么? 标签经常使用,但并不总是谨慎。 对某些人来说,它只是提到救赎的特定观点. 对其他人来说,它引起一种传统、一种文化,甚至一种美学。
articles.title_zh: 我们需要了解我们的改革根源
articles.content: What does it mean to be Reformed? The label is used frequently but not always carefully. For some, it simply refers to a particular view of salvation. For others, it evokes a tradition, a culture, or even an aesthetic. Yet historically, to be Reformed has meant something much richer. While no single sentence can capture the fullness of the Reformed tradition, at minimum it means three things: to be biblical, to be covenantal, and to be confessional. The authority of Scripture governs our theology, covenant theology provides Scripture’s redemptive framework, and the historic confessions summarize and safeguard the church’s doctrinal convictions. Remove any one of those pillars, and something essential to the Reformed tradition is lost. With “Reformed” in its name, it’s hardly surprising that Reformed Theological Seminary has long sought to equip pastors and church members in all three areas. In recent years, members of its faculty have produced substantial volumes on the Old and New Testaments and on covenant theology. Now, with The Westminster Confession of Faith: A Comprehensive Commentary on Its History, Theology, and Application , they turn their attention to the confessional foundation of the Reformed tradition. The result is a volume that seeks not only to explain what the confession teaches but also to demonstrate why confessional theology remains vital for the church today. What Is the Westminster Confession of Faith? The Westminster Confession of Faith takes its name from the Westminster Assembly, a gathering of more than 100 ministers and theologians convened by the English Parliament in 1643 at a time of profound political and ecclesiastical upheaval. The assembly was tasked with recommending reforms to the doctrine, worship, government, and discipline of the Church of England. After more than five years of careful biblical study and theological deliberation, the assembly produced the Westminster Confession of Faith along with the Larger and Shorter Catechisms. Together, these documents have served as the doctrinal foundation of Presbyterian churches throughout the world for nearly four centuries. The assembly’s influence, however, extends far beyond Presbyterianism. The confession has helped shape the broader Reformed tradition, providing the framework for later confessional statements. As a result, its theological influence shaped generations of Congregationalists, Baptists, and other evangelical Christians. The editors of this volume rightly observe, The confession is also ecumenical because it found wide acceptance among Congregationalists and Particular Baptists in the seventeenth century, as two different groups of theologians adapted the confession according to their theological convictions, producing the Savoy Declaration (1658) and the Second London Confession (1689). Thus the Westminster Confession is relevant to Presbyterians, Congregationalists, and Baptists. (xx) Why Another Commentary? The Westminster Confession has never lacked commentators. From the 17th century onward, pastors and theologians have written to explain its theology. Quality works by A. A. Hodge , G. I. Williamson, R. C. Sproul, and more recently Chad Van Dixhoorn have each served the church well in different ways. So why do we need another commentary on the confession, and what makes this one useful? The Westminster Confession has helped shape the broader Reformed tradition, providing the framework for later confessional statements. First, this isn’t the work of a single author but a collaborative effort by scholars whose expertise spans several areas of theology. That breadth allows the volume to approach the confession from different perspectives while maintaining a clear unity of purpose. Each contributor brings particular expertise to the section he addresses, but the volume as a whole is concerned with helping readers understand the confession and its significance for the church. Second, the commentary is consciously pastoral. Rather than treating the confession merely as a historical artifact or an academic text, the contributors consistently demonstrate how its theology serves the life of the church. Readers are reminded that the confession was written not simply to settle theological disputes but to help the church understand and live out the whole counsel of God. This pastoral emphasis matters. It’s easy for a confession to become something we study without allowing it to shape the way we live as Christians. The Westminster Confession was never intended to be a document we merely admire or defend. Its doctrines are meant to shape the faith of the church as we “contend for the faith that was once for all delivered to the saints” (Jude 1:3). This commentary is useful because it helps readers make that connection, showing not only what the assembly confessed but why those truths matter today. Faith with Roots As a pastor, I’m finding that one of the great needs of our day is a sense of rootedness. Many Christians are looking for something that will give them a deeper sense of stability and connection to the historic Christian faith, something that didn’t begin with the latest movement or cultural moment. They’re looking for something with roots. It’s easy for a confession to become something we study without allowing it to shape the way we live as Christians. This is one of the gifts of the Westminster Confession of Faith. Its doctrinal roots have given generations of believers a lasting stability, keeping them grounded in the historic faith through waves of theological and cultural change. It doesn’t simply teach us what to believe; it roots those beliefs within the life of the church, connecting us to generations of faithful Christians who have confessed these same truths before us. The Westminster Confession helps us to see that we don’t have to find our footing in the Christian faith on our own. We receive the gift of learning from generations of believers who have gone before us, helping us see the riches of Scripture with greater clarity and confidence. This volume is an invitation to rediscover that heritage and to find fresh encouragement in the faithfulness of God, who has sustained his church through the centuries. May it help a new generation find joy in the riches of the Reformed tradition and pass them on with confidence to those who follow.
articles.content_zh: 改革意味着什么? 标签经常使用,但并不总是谨慎。 对某些人来说,它只是提到救赎的特定观点. 对其他人来说,它引起一种传统、一种文化,甚至一种美学。 然而,从历史上看,改革意味着更加富有的东西。 虽然没有一句话能捕捉到被改造后的传统的全部,但至少它意味着三件事:是圣经,是盟约,是忏悔. 圣经的权威支配着我们的神学,盟约神学提供了圣经的红发框架,历史的忏悔总结并捍卫了教会的教义信念。 移除其中任何一根支柱,失去对改革后的传统至关重要的东西。 改革神学院长期试图在所有三个领域为牧师和教会成员提供教具, 近年来,该校院士编写了大量关于"旧约"和"新约"和"盟约神学"等著作. 现在,随着《威斯敏斯特信仰的忏悔:对其历史、神学和适用的综合评论》,他们把注意力转向改革后传统的忏悔基础。 结果的一卷不仅试图解释忏悔的教义,还试图表明为什么忏悔神学在今天仍然对教会至关重要. 韦斯敏斯特对信仰的忏悔是什么? 威斯敏斯特信仰忏悔会取而代之的是威斯敏斯特大会(Westminster Assembly),这是1643年英国议会在政治与教会剧变深刻的时期召开的由100多位部长和神学家组成的集会. 大会的任务是建议对英格兰教会的学说,崇拜,政府和纪律进行改革. 经过五年多的认真的圣经研究和神学审议后,大会产生了"威斯敏斯特信仰忏悔"(Westminster Confession of Faith)和"更大规模和更短的卡特克主义". 近四个世纪以来,这些文件共同成为全世界长老会教会的理论基础。 然而,议会的影响远远超出长老会。 忏悔有助于形成更广泛的改革后传统,为后来的忏悔声明提供了框架。 因此,它的神学影响塑造了几代基督教会,浸信会等福音派基督徒. 这本书的编辑们正确地指出,《忏悔书》也具有普世性,因为它在17世纪被基督教会和特定浸信会广泛接受,因为两个不同的神学家群体根据他们的神学信念修改了供词,产生了"萨伏依宣言"(1658年)和"第二次伦敦忏悔书"(1689年). 因此,威斯敏斯特忏悔与长老会、基督教会和浸信会有关。 (二十) 为什么另作一评注? 威斯敏斯特的"忏悔"从未缺少评论家. 从17世纪起,牧师和神学家都撰文解释其神学. A. A. Hodge、G. I. Williamson、R. C. Sproul和最近的Chad Van Dixhoorn以不同方式为教堂服务。 因此,我们为什么需要关于供词的另一条评论,是什么使得这一条有用呢? 威斯敏斯特忏悔有助于形成更广泛的改革后传统,为后来的忏悔声明提供了框架. 首先,这不是一位作者的工作,而是学者的合作努力,他们的专业知识跨越了神学的几个领域。 这种宽度允许量从不同的角度对待供词,同时保持明确的目的一致。 每个贡献者都会为他所讲的一节带来特殊的专门知识,但该卷整体关注的是帮助读者理解忏悔及其对教会的意义. 第二,评注是自觉的放肆。 撰稿人不但没有将忏悔仅仅视为历史文物或学术文本,反而一贯表明其神学如何为教会的生活服务. 读者们被提醒,供词的写作不仅是为了解决神学上的争议,而且是为了帮助教会理解并活出整个上帝的劝告. 这种对牧业的重视很重要。 忏悔很容易成为我们研究的东西, 威斯敏斯特的忏悔书 从来都不是我们只崇拜或捍卫的文件 它的教义意在塑造教会的信仰,因为我们“延续着永远交给圣徒的信仰”(Jude 1:3)。 这篇评论很有用,因为它有助于读者建立这种联系,不仅表明大会承认了什么,而且表明这些真理为何今天重要。 对根的信念 作为牧师,我发现我们这个时代的伟大需求之一是一种扎根感。 许多基督徒正在寻找一些能让他们更深刻地感受到基督教历史信仰的稳定与联系的东西, 他们正在寻找有根的东西。 忏悔很容易成为我们研究的东西, 这是威斯敏斯特忏悔信仰的礼物之一. 它的理论根源使几代信徒获得持久稳定,通过神学和文化变革的浪潮,使他们建立在历史信仰的基础之上。 它不只是教导我们该相信什么;它把这些信仰植根于教会的生活之中,把我们与几代忠实的基督徒联系起来,他们向我们坦白了同样的真理。 西敏的忏悔有助于我们发现我们不必靠自己找到基督教信仰的基础。 我们接受从我们之前的几代信徒那里学习的礼物,帮助我们更清楚地、更自信地看到天经的丰富之处。 这一卷是邀请人们重新发现这一遗产,并找到对上帝忠诚的新鼓励,上帝在几个世纪中一直维持着他的教堂. 愿它能帮助新一代人在改革后的传统财富中找到欢乐,并充满信心地将这些财富传给追随者。

articles.title: If the Church Did Its Job, Would the Parachurch Exist?
articles.summary: Do pregnancy centers, food pantries, or campus ministries exist because the church is failing to do her work?
articles.summary_zh: 我听到它不止一次地说 : “ 如果教会完成了它的工作, 例如,我在咨询一位当地牧师,他希望看到教堂为他所在社区的穷人服务。 对他来说重要的是,教会必须这样做,而不是非营利组织。 由于他知道上帝的王国比他的会众还大,他想让多个教会参与这个项目. 我建议他考虑成立一个牧师理事会,并集体雇用一名工作人员来管理合并方案的运作。
articles.title_zh: 如果教会做了它的工作，教堂会存在吗？
articles.content: I’ve heard it said more than once: “If the church did its job, the parachurch wouldn’t have to exist.” For instance, I was consulting with a local pastor who wanted to see the church serve people in poverty in his community. It was important to him that the church do it, not a nonprofit. Since he understood that God’s kingdom is bigger than his congregation, he wanted to engage multiple churches in the project. I suggested he consider forming a council of pastors and collectively hiring a staff member to manage the operations of the combined program. He thought that could work well for his context. I’m not sure he was aware of the irony. I certainly was: We’d just reinvented a variant of the 501(c)(3) nonprofit that he so keenly wanted to avoid in the first place. While the allergy to faith-based nonprofits was especially strong in his case, many people accept the premise at a basic level. In my experience, this sentiment is just as likely to come from someone who works in nonchurch ministry as from a pastor. If we understand the church is the core institution created by Christ to advance the kingdom of heaven, has it failed so badly that we need an army of auxiliaries to prop it up? Clarifying Terms and Roles I answer that the parachurch doesn’t exist because the church has failed. It exists because God’s commands naturally generate institutions beyond family, church, and state. Proving that starts with clarifying terms. The parachurch exists because God’s commands naturally generate institutions beyond family, church, and state. “Church” has more than one use in Scripture. In some contexts, it describes the people of God universally (Matt. 16:15–18; Eph. 1:22–23; Col. 1:18). In others, it’s a local congregational institution with the parameters God has placed around its operation (1 Thess. 1:1; 1 Tim. 3:1–5; Philem. 1:2; James 5:14). “Parachurch” typically refers to faith-based nonprofits who serve people in need or provide evangelistic and discipleship resources. Certainly, as part of the universal church, all God’s people hold equal status in advancing God’s mission, whether they labor as nurses, students, pastors, or tentmakers (see Acts 18:1–3). Just as surely, all God’s people shouldn’t merely attend but be accountable to a local congregation that enables their spiritual formation. When not assembled, God’s people are charged with many tasks—everything from stewarding creation to seeking justice for the oppressed. We can fulfill these tasks as individuals, but it often makes sense to create or join institutions dedicated to fulfilling them. Which brings us to a crucial point: God ordained some institutions specifically, and some emerged organically from God’s commands. Ordained or Emergent Institutions The family, the local church, and the government are ordained institutions. The Bible gives each ordained institution some guidance but also leaves a lot open to interpretation. While these ordained institutions are necessary for all people, they aren’t sufficient to fulfill God’s myriad commands to their fullest extent. Thus, some institutions emerge from the commands, rather than from a revealed institutional structure: The command to work led to the formation of businesses. The command to pass knowledge to subsequent generations led to the formation of schools. The command to care for the sick caused Christians to form the first hospitals. The command to care for the poor, widows, orphans, and strangers led to the formation of charities . The command to make disciples of all nations led to mission boards, publishing houses, and Bible-translation ministries. This ordained-emergent distinction parallels Abraham Kuyper’s “ sphere sovereignty ” in its recognition of institutions not explicitly outlined in Scripture. Many of these commands can be fulfilled to some lesser degree by the ordained institutions, but there are limitations. A family may work without forming a business, but they’ll never raise a skyscraper. Most believers recognize that the bulk of emergent institutions are legitimate. No one says, “If the church did its job being hospitable, restaurants wouldn’t need to exist.” Similarly, I don’t hear a lot of people saying, “If the church cared for the sick, hospitals wouldn’t need to exist.” Businesses, schools, hospitals, and charities all work best when operated by believers in accordance with God’s precepts. But they don’t have to answer to a plurality of elders any more than they have to be structured like a family whose children must answer to their parents. Churches, Nonprofits, and Businesses Ordained institutions have distinct mandates that limit what other institutions should do. That’s why Paul instructs Timothy that the local church shouldn’t aid a widow who has a family capable of aiding her (1 Tim. 5:3–4). Without question, overeager nonprofits at times impinge on the core duties of a family or local church. But in general, emergent institutions are legitimate and complement the work of the government, congregation, and family. Ordained institutions have distinct mandates that limit what other institutions should do. The Bible acknowledges this by its support of businesses . While the command to work is ordained by God, Scripture nowhere defines a prescriptive business structure. Yet the employer-employee relationship is acknowledged as legitimate, and the institution as one that promotes human flourishing. Once for-profit entities aren’t viewed as a local congregation’s failure, the line between a kingdom-minded business and a kingdom-minded nonprofit becomes fuzzy. For instance, plenty of for- and nonprofit enterprises intentionally employ and disciple people who are difficult to employ. Surely the tax structure doesn’t determine the theological validity of the enterprise. Thus, claims like “God created the church; he didn’t create the pregnancy resource center”—while true in the most literal sense—don’t communicate much of value. It’s a bit like saying, “God made trees. He didn’t make your table.” My table is made almost entirely of trees. The table is a good thing for which I should be grateful to God. The parachurch exists because God’s commands naturally generate institutions beyond family, church, and state. The more the church does its job, the more local congregations there will be, the more nonprofits there will be, and the more redemptive businesses there will be. The question isn’t whether the church should replace the parachurch but whether God’s people will faithfully build every institution needed to accomplish his will.
articles.content_zh: 我听到它不止一次地说 : “ 如果教会完成了它的工作, 例如,我在咨询一位当地牧师,他希望看到教堂为他所在社区的穷人服务。 对他来说重要的是,教会必须这样做,而不是非营利组织。 由于他知道上帝的王国比他的会众还大,他想让多个教会参与这个项目. 我建议他考虑成立一个牧师理事会,并集体雇用一名工作人员来管理合并方案的运作。 他认为这对他的背景来说是可行的。 我不确定他是否意识到讽刺。 我当然是:我们刚刚重新发明了501(c)(3)非营利的变体,他一开始非常想避免它。 虽然在他的案件中对基于信仰的非营利组织特别过敏,但许多人在基本层面上接受了这一前提。 根据我的经验,这种情绪可能来自在非教会部工作的人和牧师。 如果我们理解教会是基督为推进"天国"而建立的核心机构,那么它是否如此地失败了,以至于我们需要一支辅军来支撑它? 我回答说教区并不存在, 它的存在是因为上帝的命令自然产生超越家庭、教会和国家的体制。 证明从澄清条款开始。 教区之所以存在,是因为上帝的命令自然会产生超越家庭、教会和国家的体制。 “教会”在《圣经》中有不止一种用途。 在某些情况下,它普遍描述了上帝的人民(Matt. 16:15–18;Eph. 1:22–23;Col. 1:18)。 在其他情况下,它是一个具有上帝设定参数的地方教会机构,围绕它的运作(1 Thess. 1:1; 1 Tim. 3: 1–5; Philem. 1:2; James 5:14). “教会”一般是指为有需要的人服务或提供福音和门徒资源的基于信仰的非营利组织。 当然,作为普世教会的一部分,所有上帝的人民在推进上帝的使命方面都具有同等的地位,无论是作为护士、学生、牧师还是帐篷匠(见第18:1至3号法案)。 诚然,所有上帝的信徒不应该只参加,而应该对能够形成精神的当地教会负责。 在没有集合的时候,真主的宗族将担负许多任务,从管理创造到为被压迫者寻求正义。 我们可以作为个人完成这些任务,但建立或加入专门履行这些任务的机构往往是合理的。 这让我们到了一个关键点:真主专门规定一些制度,有些制度是从真主的命令中有机地出现的。 组织或应急机构 家庭、地方教会和政府是法定机构。 《圣经》为每个指定机构提供了一些指导,但也为解释留下了很大余地。 尽管这些指定机构对所有人来说都是必要的,但它们不足以最充分地执行上帝的众多命令。 因此,有些机构产生于指挥部,而不是一个公开的体制结构: 工作指挥导致了企业的形成. 将知识传给后人的命令导致了学校的形成. 照顾病人的命令使得基督徒组成了第一批医院. 照顾穷人、寡妇、孤儿和陌生人的命令导致了慈善机构的成立。 使各国门徒的指挥导致了传教板,出版社,和圣经翻译部. 这一规定性的区别与亚伯拉罕·库伊珀的 " 领域主权 " 相似,因为它承认了《圣经》中没有明确阐述的机构。 许多这些命令在较低程度上可以由指定机构执行,但有一些限制。 一家人可以工作而不创业, 大多数信徒承认,大多数新兴机构是合法的。 没有人会说,“如果教会做好了自己的工作, “如果教会照顾病人, 医院就不需要存在。 企业、学校、医院和慈善机构在由信徒按照上帝的戒律运作时都做得最好。 也不必像家庭一样, 子女必须向父母负责。 教会、非营利和经商机构有不同的授权,限制其他机构应做什么。 这就是为什么保罗指示蒂莫西,当地教会不应该帮助一个有家庭能力帮助她的寡妇(1 Tim. 5:3–4). 毫无疑问,过度的非营利组织有时会损害家庭或地方教会的核心职责。 但总的来说,新兴机构是合法的,是对政府,会众和家庭工作的补充. 法定机构有不同的授权,限制其他机构应做什么。 《圣经》通过支持企业来承认这一点。 虽然工作命令由上帝下达,但《圣经》却无一规定一种规范的商业结构。 然而,雇主与雇员的关系被公认为合法,而这种关系是促进人类繁荣的机构。 一旦盈利实体不被视为当地众会的失败,一个有王国意识的企业和有王国意识的非营利之间的界线就会变得模糊不清。 例如,许多营利和非营利企业有意雇用难以雇用的人和门徒。 当然,税收结构并不决定企业的神学有效性。 因此,“上帝创建了教会;他没有创建孕期资源中心”之类的说法,尽管从最直白的意义上讲是真实的,但并没有传达多少价值。 这有点像“上帝造出树木。 他没有给你做桌子。 我的桌子几乎是树做的 桌子是件好事 我该感谢上帝 教区之所以存在,是因为上帝的命令自然会产生超越家庭、教会和国家的体制。 教会的工作越多,当地的会会越多,非盈利性会越多,而红发会的企业也就越多. 问题不在于教会是否应该取代教区,

articles.content: What can pastors today learn from the Puritans? Matt Smethurst and Ligon Duncan welcome Joel Beeke to discuss the lasting wisdom of Puritan pastors and theologians. Drawing from decades of studying and teaching the Puritans, Beeke explains why they placed such a high priority on prayer, personal holiness, and applying Scripture to the hearts and lives of their congregations. articles.title: On My Shelf: Life and Books with L. Michael Morales
articles.summary: L. Michael Morales talks about what’s on his bedside table, favorite fiction, favorite rereads, and more.
articles.summary_zh: 《我的书架》帮助你了解各种作家, 通过幕后人物的一幕来了解他们作为读者的生活。 我问L. Michael Morales — — 格林维尔长老会神学院的教授和《出老而新:救赎的圣经神学》的作者 — — 关于他的床边桌子上的内容、他最喜欢的虚构故事、他经常重读的书籍等等。 现在睡台上有什么?
articles.title_zh: 在我的架子上： L. Michael Morales的生活和书籍
articles.content: On My Shelf helps you get to know various writers through a behind-the-scenes glimpse into their lives as readers. I asked L. Michael Morales—professor at Greenville Presbyterian Theological Seminary and author of Exodus Old and New: A Biblical Theology of Redemption —about what’s on his bedside table, his favorite fiction, the books he regularly revisits, and more. What’s on your nightstand right now? Malcolm Guite’s Galahad and the Grail . Myths of origin hold potential for shaping a society’s culture and character. I believe Guite, aside from writing good poetry and a national epic, is endeavoring to reawaken (or refound) England to her rich Christian heritage. This volume is the first of a projected four-volume work that may well represent the new definitive collection of Arthurian legends. Writings of the Ramban , translated and annotated by Charles B. Chavel. Nachmanides is my favorite medieval Jewish exegete and commentator, and these essays illumine his character and offer gleaming gems of insight. His essay on redemption, for example, gives a nuanced understanding of eschatology in the Hebrew Scriptures. He argues convincingly that the exile threatened in Leviticus relates to the Babylonian exile that occurred in Jeremiah’s day, whereas exile in Deuteronomy uses more eschatological language and seems to relate to the exile after the Second Temple’s destruction. Another essay records his Disputation in Barcelona, when Nachmanides was forced by the Spanish government to engage in debate with a Jewish Christian convert. The disputation eventually led to his exile from Spain since, as one of the intellectual giants of his era, he acquitted himself overly well. (Christian readers will, for the most part, be disappointed with the representation of our faith by his opponent, but the disputation is helpful in that it offers insights into the sort of questions about the Messiah we should think about more deeply.) What are your favorite fiction books? Aside from literary classics, I enjoy mystery books, especially medieval mysteries, although it’s hard to find good ones. Ellis Peters’s Brother Cadfael series is good, although aimed for a younger audience (and so a bit tame). She had a beautifully poetic sense of providence and justice, which makes for satisfying conclusions. I also appreciate the espionage genre, such as the early works of John le Carré, like The Spy Who Came in from the Cold , A Small Town in Germany , and Tinker, Tailor, Soldier, Spy . Perhaps less thoughtful but often more fun, Alistair MacLean’s books never fail to offer a little escape into adventure. What biographies or autobiographies have most influenced you and why? Iain H. Murray’s two-volume biography of D. Martyn Lloyd-Jones had a profound impact on me as a young, inexperienced pastor—my copies are filled with underlining and scribbled notes. This account of the Doctor’s life and ministry not only led me onto the paths of the Reformed faith, but demonstrated God’s blessings on a faithful minister’s diligent commitment to the ordinary means of grace, to prayer and preaching. Many of the problems and challenges facing the wider evangelical church when I was pastoring had their roots in the era of Lloyd-Jones’s ministry, so reading his biography offered much-needed biblical wisdom and the discernment of hindsight. Augustine’s Confessions is also a treasured book—it’s so personal and honest, and displays the sure and gracious hand of God in one’s life. Confessions is also about Augustine’s mother, Monica, and how she persevered in prayer on his behalf; and about God’s faithfulness and goodness in answering her prayers so abundantly. Throughout the book, readers also get fascinating glimpses of life in the late fourth and early fifth centuries. What are some books you regularly reread and why? Aside from regular Bible reading, it’s a challenge to reread many books, since my research-reading stacks are always waiting. Classics and modern classics, however, grow with you, so I prioritize these. Recently, I reread Sophocles’s Oedipus Cycle (actually, I listened to audio versions on my commute). Dante’s Divine Comedy —the Anthony Esolen or Robert and Jean Hollander translations—is the work I return to most, because I often find my soul needs to retake the journey, following in the Messiah’s footsteps from his passion to the resurrection. The historian Philip Schaff referred to Dante as an early reformer, which I think is true, even if we (Protestants) would still object to many aspects of Roman Catholicism in Divine Comedy (like Mariology and purgatory). There are still so many profound biblical lessons and theological truths that make Dante a spiritually profitable read. The Heidelberg Catechism and Calvin’s Golden Booklet of the True Christian Life are also worth rereading regularly, providing both comfort and conviction. What books have most profoundly shaped how you serve and lead others for the sake of the gospel? Early on it was books on the life and ministry of the apostle Paul, like Robert L. Reymond’s Paul: Missionary Theologian . Lately, given the focus of my research and writing, it’s been the life of Moses, especially through my commentary work on the book of Numbers. Both Moses and Paul labored tirelessly, sacrificially, and with much opposition, and by God’s grace they finished their race as faithful servants looking to the Lord in hope. Paul uses vivid sacrificial imagery to capture the life of ministry, that he was being poured out as a drink offering to God (Phil. 2:17; 2 Tim. 4:6). What a wonderful and devotional way to view being spent for his kingdom. When I was a pastor I also devoured Christian History magazines . Reading about the weighty and vigorous labors of others, whether John Wesley, John Newton, Oswald Chambers, Chrysostom, or William Wilberforce, was an inspiration and encouragement to persevere in my own labors (which, by comparison, were quite minimal!). What’s one book you wish every would pastor read? Although it’s not pleasant reading, I think every pastor should read (for starters) Stan Telchin’s Abandoned or Michael Brown’s Our Hands Are Stained with Blood . Christians are woefully ignorant about some of the blots on our history regarding our relations with the Jewish people, a tragic misrepresentation of Jesus and regrettable stumbling block to the gospel. Sadly, there is also a lack of prayer for the Jewish people offered up from our pulpits, which runs contrary to the hope expressed by many of our leading lights historically, such as Charles Haddon Spurgeon and Robert Murray M’Cheyne, not to mention the apostle Paul (Rom. 9:1–5). This was not always the case, and Scottish Presbyterianism in particular has a delightful history of collegial relations with our Jewish friends. On this point, I’d commend the book Time for Favour by John Stuart Ross. Part of the larger narrative, whereby the candle of the church’s heart for Jewish people has been quite snuffed out (at least in Reformed circles), is that a shallow apprehension of the Hebrew Scriptures has led to a flat biblical-theological understanding of redemptive history. Although they might not own the label, such “replacement theology” means, practically, that the church forgets about—or worse, disdains—Jewish people, which again is a terrible departure from both Scripture and the more refreshing eras of the church’s theology. There’s an appallingly pugnacious and high-handed antisemitism swirling in our world today, often fomented further by the media. This provides the church with an opportunity to pray and to repay our debt of love, which may be used by God to heal some old wounds. What’s your best piece of writing advice? For biblical and theological writing, I endeavor to write unto God as well as in the presence of God, that is, prayerfully. Beyond this, I’m the last one who should offer advice; writing is a hard and sometimes discouraging process for me, with a few moments of beauty
articles.content_zh: 《我的书架》帮助你了解各种作家, 通过幕后人物的一幕来了解他们作为读者的生活。 我问L. Michael Morales — — 格林维尔长老会神学院的教授和《出老而新:救赎的圣经神学》的作者 — — 关于他的床边桌子上的内容、他最喜欢的虚构故事、他经常重读的书籍等等。 现在睡台上有什么? 马尔科姆·盖特的加拉哈德和圣杯。 起源神话具有塑造社会文化和性格的潜力。 我相信Guite除了写好诗作和国史诗外,还努力使英国重新认识(或重新发现)她丰富的基督教遗产。 本卷是一出预测的四卷作品中的第一部,很可能代表了"亚瑟传奇"的新最终集. 由Charles B. Chavel翻译和注释的《拉姆班人》的著作。 纳克曼尼得斯是我最喜欢的中世纪犹太人的特质和评论家,这些散文照亮了他的性格,并提供了光辉的洞察力. 例如,他关于赎罪的论文对希伯来圣经中的空想学有细微的理解. 他令人信服地辩称,在利维提库斯受到的放逐与耶利米时代发生的巴比伦人放逐有关,而Deuteronomy的放逐则使用更多的宗教语言,似乎与第二圣殿被摧毁之后的放逐有关。 另一篇散文记录了他在巴塞罗那的争议,当时纳克曼尼得斯被西班牙政府强迫与一名犹太基督徒皈依者展开辩论. 争议最终导致他被流放出西班牙,因为作为他时代的知识巨头之一,他为自己释出过好. (基督教读者大多会对其对手代表我们的信仰感到失望,但争论很有帮助,因为它能让人们深入了解我们应该更深入地思考的弥赛亚问题。 ) 你最喜欢什么小说? 除了文学经典之外,我还喜欢神秘的书籍,特别是中世纪的神秘,尽管很难找到好的书籍。 Ellis Peters的"Cadfael兄弟"系列虽然针对年轻观众(也有点温柔), 她有着美妙的诗意感 天赐和正义, 这可以得出令人满意的结论。 我也欣赏间谍流派,如约翰·勒·卡雷的早期作品,如"从寒冷中进来的间谍"(The Spy Who Came in from the Cold),"德国的一个小镇"(A Small Town)和"丁克"(Tinker,裁缝,Soldier,Spy)等. Alistair MacLean的书中, 什么传记或自传 影响最大,为什么? Iain H. Murray的两卷自传D. Martyn Lloyd-Jones对我这个年轻、经验不足的牧师产生了深远的影响——我的书中充满了强调和写作的笔记。 这种对医生生活和牧师的描述不仅使我走上了改革后信仰的道路,而且表明上帝保佑一位忠实的大臣勤勉地致力于普通的恩典、祈祷和传道。 在我做牧师时,广大福音派教会所面临的许多问题和挑战都起源于劳埃德-琼斯部的时代,因此阅读他的传记提供了急需的圣经智慧和后视力。 奥古斯丁的忏悔书也是一本珍贵的书 -- -- 它非常个人和诚实,在一个人的生活中展现出上帝的坚定和仁慈之手。 忏悔的内容还包括奥古斯丁的母亲莫妮卡,以及她如何代表他坚持祈祷;以及上帝如此忠实和善良地回答她的祈祷。 在整个书中,读者也获得了第四世纪后期和第五世纪初生活的迷人一瞥. 你经常读什么书? 除了定期阅读圣经之外, 重读许多书籍也是个挑战, 然而,经典和现代经典随着你的成长而增长,所以我优先处理这些。 最近,我重新阅读了Sophocles的《Oedipus Cycle》(实际上,我在通勤时听了音频版本 ) 。 但丁的"神通喜剧"(The Divine Comedy)——安东尼·埃索伦(Anthony Esolen)或罗伯特(Robert)和让·奥朗德(Jean Hollander)(Jean Hollander)的译作——是我回归的大部分作品,因为我经常发现我的灵魂需要重新踏上旅程,沿着弥赛亚从他的激情到复活的脚步走. 历史学家菲利普·沙夫(英语:Philip Schaff)将但丁称为早期改革者,我认为这是正确的,即使我们(抗议者)仍然会反对神通喜剧中的罗马天主教的许多方面(类似"海洋"和"炼狱"). 仍然有如此多的深刻的圣经教义和神学真理使但丁在精神上有利可图地阅读. 海德堡卡德克主义和加尔文的"真正的基督教生活"金本册也值得定期重读,既提供了舒适又提供了信念. 是什么书最深刻地塑造了 你如何为福音服务 并领导他人? 早期是关于使徒保罗的生平和牧师的书籍,如罗伯特·雷蒙德的"保罗:传教神学家". 最近,鉴于我的研究和写作的重点,这是摩西的生活,特别是通过我关于"数字"一书的评论工作。 穆萨和保罗都坚持不懈地努力,不屈不挠地反对,在上帝的恩惠下,他们作为忠实的仆人,以望主而完成了他们的种族. 保罗用生动的牺牲形象来捕捉部会的生活,即被倒出作为献给上帝的饮料(Phil. 2:17;2 Tim. 4:6). 多么美妙和忠心的观赏 被花在他的王国。 当我是牧师的时候,我也吃过基督教历史杂志。 阅读他人的重心和强力劳动,无论是约翰·韦斯利,约翰·牛顿,奥斯瓦尔德·钱伯斯,克赖索斯托姆,还是威廉·威尔伯福斯,都是坚持自己劳动的灵感和鼓励(相比之下,这实在是微不足道了!). 你希望每个牧师都读一本书是什么? 或迈克尔·布朗的手被血染了。 基督教徒对我们历史上有关我们与犹太人民关系的污点感到悲哀无知,这是对耶稣的悲惨歪曲,是福音的令人遗憾的绊脚石。 可悲的是,我们没有为犹太人祈祷,这与历史上许多主要灯光,如查尔斯·哈登·斯普根和罗伯特·默里·姆谢恩,更不用说使徒保罗(9:1-5)所表达的希望背道而驰。 情况并非总是如此,苏格兰长老会尤其与我们的犹太朋友建立了友好关系。 我赞扬约翰·斯图尔特·罗斯的《时间倾斜》一书。 部分较大规模的叙事,即教会对犹太人的心灵的蜡烛被相当地吸出(至少在改革圈子中是如此),那就是对希伯来圣经的浅浅的担忧导致了对红色先发制人历史的平淡的圣经-神学理解. 虽然他们可能不拥有这个标签,但这种“替代神学”实际上意味着,教会忘记了——或者更糟糕的蔑视——犹太人民,这再次可怕地背离了圣经和教会神学中更加新鲜的时代。 当今世界上有一种骇人听闻的傲慢和高压的反分裂主义,常常被媒体进一步煽动。 这为教会提供了一个祷告和偿还我们相爱之债的机会,上帝可能利用这些债务来治愈一些旧伤. 你最好的写作建议是什么? 对于圣经和神学著作,我努力给上帝写作,以及当着上帝的面,即祈祷。 写作对我来说是一个艰难有时令人沮丧的过程,
