featured.title: Beware Making Mental Illness an Identity
featured.summary: ‘All in Your Head’ is a concrete and compelling remapping of mental health culture with impressive explanatory power.
featured.summary_zh: 在他非自愿地被送入精神病院治疗两极分化后的几年里,弗雷德里克·德·博尔带着对挽救他生命的系统深表感谢和明显的沮丧,因为他的治愈经验变得如此罕见. 在你的脑海中:作为身份的疾病,作为时尚的创伤,以及希望陷入混乱,是互联网上最异形的思想家和作家之一的最新一面。 作为一位最以写作"聪明的邪教"而出名的"老派"马克思主义者,德博尔以自己的部落内部的文化漂移为目的,让那些最需要的人如此难以接受精神保健:"将精神疾病视为激动人心的冒险的倾向,在流行文化中无休止地浪漫化的放荡,是多年来我所照顾的诸多恶化之一"(8). 他的病情恶化的根源——将精神疾病和残疾视为一种值得庆贺的身份,而不是需要治疗的残疾——并不是他脑子里所有的东西。
featured.title_zh: 小心让精神疾病成为一种身份
featured.content: In the years since he was involuntarily committed to a mental health institution for bipolar disorder, Frederik deBoer has wrestled with both profound gratitude for a system that saved his life and also palpable frustration that his experience of healing has become so rare. All in Your Head: Illness as Identity, Trauma as Fashion, and the Desire to Be Disordered is the latest broadside from one of the internet’s most heterodox thinkers and writers. As an “old school” Marxist best known for writing The Cult of Smart , deBoer takes aim at how the cultural drift within his own tribe is responsible for making mental health care so elusive for those who need it most: “The tendency to treat mental illness as an exciting adventure, the endless romanticization of lunacy in popular culture, is one of many aggravations I have nursed for years” (8). The root of his aggravation—the treatment of mental illness and disability as an identity to be celebrated rather than a disability that needs treatment —isn’t all in his head. The use of talk therapy rose 47 percent between 2019 and 2024 . A 2025 LifeStance survey found around 29 percent of U.S. adults have self-diagnosed their mental health condition after consuming online content, rising to 50 percent among Gen Z (versus 9 percent of boomers). Of the people who self-diagnose symptoms, almost a quarter (24 percent) “rarely” or “never” feel the need to take the next step to discuss them with a qualified clinician. DeBoer argues that rather than reducing the stigma surrounding mental illness, the inordinate attention given to the mildly and dubiously afflicted is a dangerous distraction crowding out help for the severely ill. Accelerated by social media, this “gentrification of disability” has become a full-blown social contagion, compromising even the experts and institutions responsible for mental health care (153–54). DeBoer is largely right, and the cultural shift he identifies has real-world implications both inside and outside the church. But the same ideological priors that so sharpen deBoer’s critique also suffer from two significant blind spots that, were they addressed, would make All in Your Head the more courageous, more constructive, and, therefore, more widely read manifesto we need. General Bipartisan Ire If you picked up All in Your Head to understand how modern therapy culture spread like wildfire across social media over the last several years, it’s not immediately obvious why deBoer starts his argument with an in-depth analysis of the anti-psychiatry movement’s influence in late 20th century politics and academia. But, if you can forgive me the pun, there’s a method to his madness. After a blistering critique of “rightwing libertarian” policies that neglected mental illness, he cashes in on the subsequent trust he earns with left-leaning readers to launch a series of absolute haymakers toward “a species of thought that sometimes amounts to a kind of leftist pseudo-radicalism or a libertarian fantasy” (198) that drives the “destabilizing . . . move from mental illness as reality to mental illness as symbol” (8). American individualism and anti-institutional bias aren’t new, but the painstakingly specific way deBoer traces their spread through the culture surrounding mental health and therapy is refreshing and instructive. Our “apolitical romanticism of resistance to modern society” fuels two opposite errors: On the right, mental illness is sometimes seen as either imagined or a symptom of weak character. But on the left, the same romanticism often describes mental disability as more en abling than dis abling, as if neurodivergent minorities don’t need society’s help—society needs theirs. Gentrification of Disability DeBoer’s emphatic rejection of this predominantly progressive error— of “making a medical disorder an identity”—is the “overarching principle of [his] book” (165). This is never more clear in what he labels “the gentrification of disability,” where “diagnoses become fads” because the “intellectual and discursive space once dedicated to the interests of the most afflicted have become fixated instead on a class of patients whose disorders range from mild to dubious” (154). Said spaces and institutions have become so compromised due to “the diseased incentives of social media” and “liberal conventional wisdom that says it’s offensive to question any claim any individual makes about a disability.” Combined, “we’ve created ‘disorder communities’” not unlike fan clubs “rooting for a particular sports team” (154). The disproportionate attention given to those wealthy enough or high-functioning enough to perform their disability online is a dangerous distraction with real consequences: The more that influential elites use their status to “define the disorder in the public mind,” the more those who are impoverished or severely disabled go unseen and neglected. The disproportionate attention given to those wealthy enough or high-functioning enough to perform their disability online is a dangerous distraction with real consequences. Clear to anyone not living under a rock for the last decade is how familiar these patterns are. As I argued in The Reason for Church , counterfeit institutions (e.g., social media) have bypassed gatekeepers and hijacked the incentives of vital social and spiritual institutions undergirding American life. All in Your Head won’t add many new tools for recognizing these patterns. DeBoer’s contribution is in tracing them throughout an often convoluted bureaucratic ecosystem from the perspective of a “crabby old Marxist” frustrated by the privileged hypocrisy of pop-critical theory and progressive politics. However useful, the same ideological priors also handicap his analysis with two glaring omissions. Incomplete Diagnosis and Insufficient Prescription His most obvious omission is the rapid rise of gender dysphoria diagnoses and sex-reassignment surgery for minors. For more than a decade, gender-affirming physicians have been telling parents they must choose between having “a trans kid or a dead kid,” but, as Rebecca McLaughlin points out , the evidence says otherwise: “Puberty blockers can make the mental health of some young people worse, not better.” Considering deBoer’s impressive track record of taking unpopular, heterodox positions within his own tribe, his failure to address what is arguably the most volatile and life-altering consequence of toxic therapy culture is bewildering. DeBoer’s second omission is more understandable. While he concludes with well-reasoned (if regrettably materialist and socialist) policy prescriptions, he doesn’t offer any remedy for the broader therapeutic culture (i.e., the “ideological commitment to radical individual autonomy” [77]) that he spends most of the book arguing is the root of resistance to reform. That neglect robs his policy prescriptions of much persuasive power. Christians can affirm deBoer’s diagnosis of the problem of individual autonomy, but the church has the social and spiritual resources missing from all legislative and policy prescriptions. We know humans were never meant to construct our identities but to receive them in Christ and through belonging to our families, to our churches, and ultimately to God. Church has the social and spiritual resources missing from all legislative and policy prescriptions. Despite any omissions, All in Your Head is a clear-eyed and validating read, especially for those in (or disappointed by) mental health care. It would be a fine complement to Matthew Loftus’s Resisting Therapy Culture and describes many of the downstream problems Philip Rieff anticipated in The Triumph of the Therapeutic . All in Your Head is “not a memoir” (8) but a pragmatic antimemoir seething with a holy discontent that challenges both performative mental illness and the also voyeurism that incentivizes it. The result is a concrete and compelling remapping of mental health culture with impressive explanatory
featured.content_zh: 在他非自愿地被送入精神病院治疗两极分化后的几年里,弗雷德里克·德·博尔带着对挽救他生命的系统深表感谢和明显的沮丧,因为他的治愈经验变得如此罕见. 在你的脑海中:作为身份的疾病,作为时尚的创伤,以及希望陷入混乱,是互联网上最异形的思想家和作家之一的最新一面。 作为一位最以写作"聪明的邪教"而出名的"老派"马克思主义者,德博尔以自己的部落内部的文化漂移为目的,让那些最需要的人如此难以接受精神保健:"将精神疾病视为激动人心的冒险的倾向,在流行文化中无休止地浪漫化的放荡,是多年来我所照顾的诸多恶化之一"(8). 他的病情恶化的根源——将精神疾病和残疾视为一种值得庆贺的身份,而不是需要治疗的残疾——并不是他脑子里所有的东西。 2019年至2024年间,谈话疗法的使用率上升了47%. 2025年生活稳定调查发现,约29%的美国成年人在消费了在线内容后自行诊断出自己的心理健康状况,在Gen Z中上升到了50%(相对于9%的繁荣者). 在自我诊断的人群中,近四分之一(24%)的人“勉强”或“从未”感到有必要采取下一步措施,与合格的临床医生讨论这些症状。 DeBoer认为,对受轻度和可疑折磨的人的过度关注,与其减少精神疾病的污名化,不如说是一种危险的分心,挤出对重病患者的帮助。 社交媒体加速了这种 " 残疾意识化 " ,已成为一种全面的社会传染,甚至损害负责精神保健的专家和机构(153-54)。 DeBoer基本上是正确的,他所认定的文化转变在教堂内外都具有现实世界的影响. 但德布尔批评如此尖锐的意识形态前科也遭遇了两个重大盲点,如果这些盲点得到解决,将使你的头脑更加勇敢,更具建设性,因此,我们需要更广泛地阅读宣言。 一般两党爱尔兰人 如果你在脑海中看到现代治疗文化在过去几年里如何像野火一样在社交媒体上传播,那么DeBoer为什么以深入分析20世纪后期反精神病运动在政治和学术界的影响为出发点,这并不明显。 但是,如果你能原谅我的双关语,他疯狂是有办法的。 在对忽视了精神疾病的“右翼自由派”政策猛烈批评后,他依靠后来与左翼读者获得的信任,发动了一系列绝对的干草人,走向“有时相当于一种左翼伪激进主义或自由派幻想的思想”(198年),这种思想驱使“从精神疾病变成现实,转变为精神疾病作为象征”(8)。 美国的个人主义和反机构偏见并非新事物, 但DeBoer通过精神卫生与治疗的文化, 我们“反对现代社会的政治浪漫主义”助长了两个相反的错误: 在右边,精神疾病有时被视为一种想象或一种弱性症状. 但是在左边,同样的浪漫主义常常将精神残疾描述为比分身更困难,仿佛神经分身的少数民族不需要社会的帮助——社会需要他们的帮助。 对DeBoer残疾人的强烈反对,即 " 使医疗障碍成为身份 " 这一主要进步的错误,是 " 书中的首要原则 " (165)。 在他所谓的“残疾的基因化”中,这一点再清楚不过了,因为“曾经专为受感染最深的人的利益服务的智慧和模糊空间已经固定在一类疾病从轻度到可疑的病人身上”(154个)。 因为“社会媒体的有病刺激”和“自由传统智慧, 综合起来, " 我们创建了`混乱社区 ' " ,与粉丝俱乐部 " 为某一特定体育队 " (154个)不同。 对足够富有或高运作能力的人的过度关注, 有影响力的上层人士越是利用其地位“界定公众心中的混乱”,穷人或严重残疾者就越是被忽视和忽视。 对那些足够富有或高功用、足以在线处理残疾的人的过度关注是一种危险的分心,会产生实际后果。 过去十年里没有生活在岩石下的人很清楚 这些模式是多么熟悉。 假冒机构(如社交媒体)绕过守门人, 并劫持了影响美国生活的重要社会及精神机构。 在你的脑海中, DeBoer的贡献在于从一个被流行批评理论和进步政治的特有伪善所挫败的“疯狂的老马克思主义者”的视角来追踪整个经常被曲解的官僚生态系统。 不管多么有用,同样的意识形态前科也以两个明显的遗漏来阻碍他的分析。 未完全诊断和处方不足 他最明显的遗漏是性别障碍诊断和未成年人性转移手术的迅速上升. 十多年来,具有性别特征的医生一直告诉父母,他们必须在“一个跨性别的孩子或一个已经死亡的孩子”之间做出选择,但是,正如Rebecca McLaughlin所指出,证据却说道 : “ 纯洁的阻塞者可以使一些年轻人的精神健康恶化,而不是更好。 ” 考虑到德博尔在自己的部落内占据不受欢迎的、异性立场的令人印象深刻的记录,他未能解决毒害性疗法文化可能带来的最动荡和最改变生命的后果是令人困惑的。 DeBoer的第二次遗漏更让人理解。 虽然他最后给出了合理(如果令人遗憾的是唯物主义和社会主义)政策处方,但他并没有为更广泛的治疗文化(即“激进个人自主的意识形态承诺”[77])提供任何补救,他花在书中的大部分争论是抵制改革的根源。 这种忽视剥夺了他的政策处方 很大的说服力。 基督徒可以肯定DeBoer对个人自治问题的诊断,但教会在所有立法和政策处方中都缺少社会和精神资源。 我们知道人类从来就不是要建立我们的身份,而是要在基督中,通过属于我们的家庭、我们的教会以及最终属于上帝来接受他们。 教会在所有立法和政策规定中都缺少社会和精神资源。 尽管有任何疏漏,但《你的头脑》是一个清晰而真实的读物,特别是对于接受(或因)精神保健的人来说。 并描述了Philip Rieff在《治疗的凯旋》中预料到的许多下游问题。 你脑子里全是“不是回忆录”(8),而是一种务实的预言,充满了圣洁的不满,既挑战了表现性精神疾病,也挑战了刺激这种疾病的巫术。 结果是以令人印象深刻的解释对心理健康文化进行了具体和令人信服的再规划。
featured.author: Brad Edwards

featured.title: How a Former Prisoner in Iran Wants You to Pray for Christians in Chains
featured.summary: Pray not only for what God might do for Christian prisoners in Iran but for what God might do through them, for his glory.
featured.summary_zh: 不久前,我和两名基督教青年在伊朗最困难的监狱之一服刑。 因为他们拒绝停止宣扬耶稣。 我问自己如何为他们祈祷, 他们说,“祈祷我们在这里的工作结束前不会被释放。 ” 他们带领许多同狱囚犯信仰。
featured.title_zh: 伊朗前囚犯如何希望你为被锁的基督徒祈祷
featured.content: Not long ago, I had a surreal phone call with two young Christian men serving prison sentences in one of Iran’s hardest prisons. They’re there because they refuse to stop preaching about Jesus. When I asked how I could pray for them, their answer wasn’t what you might expect. “Pray that we would not be released until our job here is finished,” they said. They had led numerous fellow prisoners to faith. Now, their chief concern was to remain inside long enough to disciple them. The call took me straight back to the five years I spent in prison for my faith. Now, these dear brothers (let’s call them Vahid and Reza) were behind bars, and I was outside. As we spoke, I pictured the wards and corridors, imagined the sounds and smells, and remembered how hard it was not to know how many years I would be there. But it was also an encouraging call. Vahid and Reza were in high spirits, talking about Bible passages that were sustaining them and how the Lord was at work. They didn’t see themselves in a miserable, dark place. They saw themselves in a different mission field. Their focus was the same as Paul’s in Colossians 4:3: “Pray also for us, that God may open to us a door for the word, to declare the mystery of Christ, on account of which I am in prison.” Paul’s request wasn’t for an open prison door but for an open door for the gospel. Pray for Gospel Fruit Vahid and Reza’s request resonated with me. I remember being unable to pray for my own release. I tried on a few occasions, but I couldn’t open my mouth to ask the Lord to release me. If I’m following Christ, I cannot choose the path. I cannot choose the location. I should follow him wherever he goes. And as I followed him to prison, he brought beautiful fruit. They didn’t see themselves in a miserable, dark place. They saw themselves in a different mission field. I think of one prisoner, a devout Muslim, who was wrongly accused of spying for Iran’s enemies. He was praying he would be released and was frustrated to get no answer. He approached me one day, saying, “Farshid, our God is dead. But I’ve heard yours is alive. Will you pray for me?” Fearing it might be a trap, I took him quietly aside and prayed briefly in the name of Jesus: “Lord, you know this man. Please hear his prayer.” The very next day, the man rushed over excitedly and gave me a huge hug. That morning, he had learned his name had been cleared. He was released two weeks later. Our God is indeed alive. The Lord was also at work softening my parents’ hearts toward Christ during those years. I always say that even if only for the salvation of my parents, my time in prison was worth it. So, when you pray for persecuted believers, pray not only for what God might do for them but—as Vahid and Reza requested—for what God might do through them, for his glory. Pray for gospel fruit. Pray for Comfort and Endurance I don’t want to make prison sound easier than it was. The suffering was real. So pray also for comfort and endurance. They beat me; they broke my toe. But the prolonged separation from my two children was the hardest burden to bear. The day I went to prison, my son was 2 years old and my daughter was 7. Missing their childhoods was an unspeakable loss. Yet I know others who have suffered much more than I did. I think of a brother currently in prison who has been tortured. I think of a sister who was sexually assaulted when she was arrested. Even the apostle Paul was at times “so utterly burdened beyond [his] strength that [he] despaired of life itself.” And his request to the church was simple: “You also must help us by prayer” (2 Cor. 1:8, 11). Brothers and sisters like these need us to pray for them with love. Whatever the situation, we can pray that God would grant the suffering believer comfort, peace, and endurance. The more specific the prayers, the better. While in prison, I received letters from people around the world who were praying for me. One wrote, “I am praying for your sleep. May the Lord give you peace to sleep well in prison.” I really loved it. And honestly, I did sleep well in prison; many inmates suffered from nightmares, but I cannot remember having a single one. I believe God answered that man’s prayers. Your Prayers Reach Through Prison Walls Prayer is especially needed when a prisoner is in solitary confinement. I spent 361 days in a solitary cell: For a year, I couldn’t see the sun in the sky. Yet prayers reached me through the prison walls. I remember one day I was in cell 73. I was sitting; I wasn’t praying. Suddenly, I was able to hear, let me say, a heavenly melody in my soul—not in my ears but in my soul. And I stood up. In that moment, I was overwhelmed by joy and peace. I started dancing. The cell was only two meters by two meters, but I danced before the Lord! The guard opened the door to see what I was doing. I turned to him with a wide smile and said, “Hey, sir, how are you today?” He looked at me with big eyes. “Wow, it seems you are better than me,” he said. And then he shut the door. For a year, I couldn’t see the sun in the sky. Yet prayers reached me through the prison walls. I believe someone, or maybe a group of people, was praying for me at that time. That’s why I had the experience of hearing that melody in my soul, and I was overwhelmed by joy, even though I was in solitary confinement. Many brothers and sisters around the world prayed for me during my imprisonment. Perhaps you were one of them. I cannot find the words to say thank you. Now, I want to ask, Will you pray for those in prison right now for their faith? Scripture tells us to “remember those who are in prison, as though in prison with them” (Heb. 13:3). I believe your prayer goes through the prison walls. It can touch the prisoners, encourage them, and give them joy while they’re suffering, because it’s possible to have joy and suffering at the same time. Vahid and Reza are just two of the Christians in Iran’s prisons today. There are so many. Maybe you’re asking, Where do I start? Elam’s free Bound Together resources can help your church or small group pray on the International Day of Prayer for the Persecuted Church on November 1. We pray because our God is faithful to his children. He is faithful right now to Vahid and Reza and to all our brothers and sisters in prison. And he was faithful to me. When I came out of prison, people would say to me, “Praise God, Farshid, you were faithful to the Lord. You stood for the Lord.” I always try to correct them. That’s not true. He was faithful to me. He stood for me.
featured.content_zh: 不久前,我和两名基督教青年在伊朗最困难的监狱之一服刑。 因为他们拒绝停止宣扬耶稣。 我问自己如何为他们祈祷, 他们说,“祈祷我们在这里的工作结束前不会被释放。” 他们带领许多同狱囚犯信仰。 现在,他们最关心的是 留在里面的时间足够长 让他们入门。 那通电话把我带回我为信仰在监狱里度过的五年。 现在,这些亲爱的兄弟(让我们叫他们Vahid和Reza)在监狱里,我在外面。 就在我们发言的时候,我想象了病房和走廊,想象了声音和气味,并想起了不知道我会在那里呆了多少年是多么困难。 但这也是一个令人鼓舞的呼吁。 瓦希德和礼萨精神高尚,谈论着支撑着他们的圣经段落,以及上帝是如何工作的. 他们并没有看到自己在一个悲惨而黑暗的地方。 他们看到自己在另一个任务领域。 他们的重心与保罗在Colosisans 4:3中的重心相同 : “ 也为我们祈祷,以便上帝为我们打开一个话语之门,宣告基督之谜,我为此而入狱。 ” 保罗的要求并不是打开监狱的门, 祈求福音果实Vahid, 我还记得我无法为自己的自由祈祷 我尝试过几次, 我无法选择道路。 我无法选择位置 我该跟着他 不管他去哪 当我跟着他进监狱时 他带来了美丽的水果 他们并没有看到自己在一个悲惨而黑暗的地方。 他们看到自己在另一个任务领域。 我想到一个囚犯, 一个虔诚的穆斯林, 他祈祷自己会被释放,并因得不到答复而感到沮丧。 有一天,他靠近我说,“法尔希德,我们的神死了。 但我听说你还活着。 你会为我祈祷吗?” 我担心那可能是一个陷阱,悄悄地把他放在一旁,以耶稣的名义简短地祈祷道:"主啊,你认识这个人。 请听他的祈祷。” 第二天,那个男人激动地冲过来,给了我一个巨大的拥抱。 那天早晨,他得知自己的名字已被清除。 他两周后被释放。 我们的神确实还活着。 在那些年中,上帝也在努力使我父母对基督的心软化。 我总是说,即使只是为了拯救我的父母, 我在监狱的时间是值得的。 当你们祈祷受迫害的信士们的时候,你们应当祈祷真主所意欲者,犹如瓦希德和里萨所意欲者那样,祈祷真主所意欲者。 祈取福音果实. 祈祷舒适与耐力, 苦难是真实的。 因此也祈求安慰和耐力. 他们打我,把我的脚趾弄断了 但是,与我的两个孩子长期分离是最难承受的负担。 我入狱那天,我的儿子2岁,女儿7岁。 失去童年是一个难以形容的损失。 然而,我认识其他人,他们遭受的痛苦比我多得多。 我想到目前在监狱里的一个兄弟 曾遭受酷刑 我想到一个妹妹在被捕时曾被性侵犯. 甚至使徒保罗,有时也“承受了超过他力量的沉重负担,以致于他对生命本身绝望”。 他向教堂提出的要求很简单:“你还必须通过祈祷帮助我们”(第1:8、11节)。 这样的兄弟姐妹需要我们用爱为他们祈祷. 无论情况如何,我们可以祈祷上帝会给予受苦受难的信徒以安慰、和平和耐力。 祈祷越具体越好 在狱中,我收到了世界各地为我祈祷的人的来信。 有人写道:“我在为你的睡眠祈祷。 愿主赐予你和平,让你在狱中安眠。” 我真的很喜欢 老实说,我在狱中睡得还不错,许多囚犯都遭受了噩梦,但我不记得有过一次噩梦。 我相信上帝回答了他的祈祷。 当囚犯被单独监禁时,特别需要你的祈祷书。 我在一个单独牢房呆了361天: 一年来, 然而祈祷通过监狱的墙壁来到了我。 我记得有天我在73号牢房里 我坐在一旁, 突然间,我得以听到,让我说,我的灵魂中充满了天堂的旋律——不是在我耳朵中,而是在我的灵魂中。 我站起来。 在那一刻,我被欢乐与和平所淹没。 我开始跳舞。 牢房只有两米一两米 但我在主面前跳舞! 卫所开出门来见我所为. 我大笑地对他说,“先生,你今天好吗?” 他用大眼睛看着我 “哇,看来你比我好,”他说。 然后他关了门。 一年来, 然而祈祷通过监狱的墙壁来到了我。 我相信当时有人,或可能是一群人在为我祈祷. 也为欢乐所压抑, 尽管我被单独监禁。 世界上许多兄弟姐妹在我入狱期间为我祈祷. 也许你是其中之一。 我找不到话要说谢谢。 现在,我想问,你会祈祷 那些在监狱里的人现在的信仰? 圣经告诉我们,“记住那些在狱中的人,好像在狱中一样”(Heb. 13:3)。 我相信你的祈祷会穿过监狱的墙壁 它可以触摸囚犯,鼓励他们,在他们受苦时给他们以欢乐,因为可以同时有欢乐和痛苦。 Vahid和Reza只是伊朗今天监狱中的两名基督徒。 有这么多。 可能你问, Elam的免费Bond College资源可以帮助你的教会或小团体在11月1日为受迫害的教会祈祷国际日进行祈祷. 我们祈祷是因为我们的上帝忠于他的孩子. 他现在忠于瓦希德和雷扎 忠于我们狱中的所有兄弟姐妹 他对我忠诚 当我出狱时,人们会对我说,“赞美真主,法希德,你忠于主。 你拥护上帝。” 我总是试图纠正他们。 这不是真的。 他对我忠诚 他代表着我

featured.content: The older I get, the more convinced I am that a posture of gratitude is key to a life of joy. God’s gifts are constant and abundant—his daily provision of life and breath far more than we deserve. Being alert to the constancy of his gracious provision is the epitome of rightly ordered attention . That’s why Thanksgiving is such a great holiday. It’s at least one day dedicated to pausing and taking stock, giving our attention to the Giver of all good gifts. Being alert to the constancy of God’s gracious provision is the epitome of rightly ordered attention. But it’s a shame Thanksgiving is just one day. Because really, we should practice gratitude constantly. What if, as a start, we dedicated the whole month of November to giving thanks? What if we dedicated time each day this month to intentionally naming God’s provision and giving him thanks? To help, I created a new playlist all about giving thanks to God. The playlist has 30 songs (one for each of November’s 30 days) expressing gratitude to God for our salvation in Christ, for the many blessings of marriage and family, and for the beauty of the earth. You can access the playlist now on Spotify and Apple Music . Enjoy! featured.title: The Voice of the Martyrs: Prayers of the Persecuted
featured.summary: We pray for justice, but we do so as forgiven sinners.
featured.summary_zh: " 耶和华说,多久? . . .
featured.title_zh: 殉道者的声音：受迫害者的祈祷
featured.content: “How long, O LORD? . . . Pour out your anger. . . . Let the avenging of the outpoured blood of your servants be known among the nations before our eyes!” (Ps. 79:5–6, 10). As you’re reading through Psalms and you stumble across Psalm 79, you can’t help but wonder what to do with this very Old Testament-sounding prayer. Surely, Asaph needed to be educated in the gospel, right? Revelation 6:9–10 describes the martyrs in heaven who have been slain for their testimony to the gospel and places Psalm 79 on their lips: “O Sovereign Lord, holy and true, how long before you will judge and avenge our blood on those who dwell on the earth?” Scholars agree the prayer of Psalm 79 is the likely background for the prayer of the martyrs, furthering our appreciation of this as a prayer for the church. It’s a prayer of and for the persecuted church. As we stand alongside them, we have divine warrant to pray Psalm 79 on their behalf. Trevor Laurence explains , “The vengeance petition of Rev. 6:9–10 thus supplies a model for the ongoing prayer of Christ’s body on earth.” Rather than being contrary to New Testament ethics, then, Psalm 79 fuels the church’s longing for every wrong to be made right. Nevertheless, you may still wonder, How do I take up a psalm like this in prayer for my persecuted brothers and sisters without falling into vindictive rage and vengefulness? Thankfully, Psalm 79 provides the guidelines needed to answer this question. Pray in Response to Horrific Injustice Verses 1–4 catalog the horrors God’s people suffered at the hands of the Babylonians who destroyed their temple: They defiled God’s holy place, they gave the flesh of God’s faithful ones to the beasts of the earth, they poured out their blood like water and refused them a proper burial, and they were the cause of God’s people becoming a taunt to their neighbors. Psalm 79 is not prayed in response to petty grievances but birthed out of horrendous evil. Psalm 79 is not prayed in response to petty grievances but birthed out of horrendous evil. This has two implications. First, these prayers do not give license for us to pray such things against just anyone. Second, if we object to such prayers, they challenge us to ask whether we have ever faced anything close to the agonizing evil that gave birth to this prayer. As Jamie Grant posits , “Perhaps our reluctance to appropriate the psalms of enmity is rooted in the comfort of our lives.” If we knew the kind of horror Psalm 79 speaks of (and that our persecuted brothers and sisters endure daily), perhaps we wouldn’t be so quick to dismiss these psalms. Pray for the Glory of God As psalms like this respond to such evil, they are fundamentally concerned with God’s glory. We see this in Psalm 79:6, where the nations’ refusal to call on God’s name is the motive behind Asaph’s cry. Likewise, verse 9 cites the glory of God’s name and his “name’s sake” as a rationale for God to answer this request. And verse 10 is concerned that, at present, the onlooking nations say, “Where is their God?” So Asaph asks that God’s justice would be made known among the nations (v. 10), and that God’s people might praise him for it (v. 13). The glory of God is the ultimate end of the imprecatory psalms. Or as James Hamilton says , “The glory of God in salvation through judgment is the center of the theology of Psalms.” The same is true of imprecatory psalms like Psalm 79. Their controlling desire is “Hallowed be thy name.” Pray with a Humble Posture The imprecatory psalms are not prayed in a spirit of self-righteousness; those praying them understand their need for God’s grace. They pray for justice from a posture of humility, where they confess that this judgment is what they too deserve apart from God’s grace (vv. 8–9). This is not unlike the widow’s prayer for justice in Luke 18:1–8 being paired with the parable of the Pharisee and tax collector in verses 9–14. We pray for justice, but we do so as forgiven sinners. We pray the second petition of the Lord’s Prayer (“Thy kingdom come”) with the fifth petition also in mind (“Forgive us our debts”). Pray with a Desire for Repentance If God could turn his anger away from repentant sinners in exile (Ps. 79:5), then he could do the same for Israel’s enemies. While this is not explicit in Psalm 79, its near neighbor Psalm 83, at the conclusion of this section of Asaph psalms, prays that God would fill the faces of these enemy nations with shame “that they might seek [the LORD’s name]” (v. 16). It is legitimate to see this desire as qualifying the earlier imprecations in the Asaph collection (indeed, in the whole Psalter). Hamilton even suggests every prayer for judgment in the psalms should be read as if containing an implicit “footnote” desiring repentance as a possibility. Pray with the Hope of Final Justice The prayers of judgment, like Psalm 79, are not petty prayers incompatible with a Christian ethic. God’s people pray in response to horrific injustice, aimed at the glory of God, with a posture of humility and openness to their enemies becoming God’s friends. We pray for justice, but we do so as forgiven sinners. The imprecatory psalms, then, fit perfectly with the gospel of Jesus Christ. And they arm the church to intercede for the saints in a day when our Christian brothers and sisters suffer great harm throughout the world. We long for God to answer these prayers through the conversion of our enemies. But if they remain impenitent, it is only right for God to bring justice. And it is thus right for us to pray that he would.

featured.title: Martin Luther in 5 Latin Phrases
featured.summary: Jesus’s perfect life and sacrificial death count for all believers. So God’s righteousness isn’t merely his judgment. It’s also his gift.
featured.summary_zh: 马丁·路德于1483年11月10日生于德国艾斯莱本. 第二天他在圣彼得和保罗教堂被洗礼. 7岁时,路德进入了曼斯菲尔德拉丁学校. 他在那里学习了拉丁语的语法和祷告,并记住了艾索普的"寓言".

featured.content: Martin Luther was born in Eisleben, Germany, on November 10, 1483. He was christened at Saints Peter and Paul Church the next day. At age 7, Luther entered the Mansfeld Latin School. There he learned Latin grammar and prayers, and he memorized Aesop’s Fables . From those early years through his time studying at boarding school in Magdeburg then later at the University of Erfurt, Luther was a diligent student. He kept up with his Latin, and several important Latin phrases appear throughout Luther’s writings. Five of them serve as a good summary of his life and chief theological emphases. 1. Iustitia Dei In July 1505, Luther was caught in a fierce thunderstorm. Panicked and terrified, he bargained with God, promising to become a monk. After entering the monastery, Luther was again overcome by fear. When he led his first mass as a priest, it wasn’t an occasion of joy. Instead, it was filled with trembling. As the service began, Luther took his place at the front of the chapel, and he began to recite the Latin prayers. Luther knew that God is perfect in judgment and completely without sin. So as he thought about iustitia Dei , “the righteousness of God” (Rom. 1:17), terror struck him. Biographer Roland H. Bainton describes the thoughts that plagued Luther’s mind: Who am I that I should . . . raise my hands to the divine Majesty? The angels surround him. At his nod the earth trembles . . . [but] I am dust and ashes. When Luther held up the bread and wine, he shook so badly he almost dropped the cup. During those years growing up in school and at the monastery, Luther only thought of God’s righteousness, or justice, as his active judgment against human sin. He later wrote , Though I lived as a monk without reproach, I felt and knew I was a sinner before God. I had an extremely disturbed conscience. . . . I hated the righteous God who punishes sinners. 2. Extra nos In 1512, Luther became a university professor in Wittenberg. As he studied the Bible for his lectures, he began to see God’s righteousness in a new light. Luther saw how Jesus Christ took on our humanity, how he lived a perfect life and died the painful and shameful death of the cross to take the punishment due for sin. He saw how God raised Jesus from the dead, and how he now justifies Christians by faith. God declares that in his sight, Jesus’s perfect life and sacrificial death count for all believers. So God’s righteousness isn’t merely his judgment. It’s also his gift of salvation. Jesus’s perfect life and sacrificial death count for all believers. So God’s righteousness isn’t merely his judgment. It’s also his gift. What happened when Luther made this discovery? Here’s how he described it: “I felt that I was altogether born again and had entered paradise itself through open gates.” After that day, Luther began to teach that God gives Christians his “alien righteousness,” that is, a righteousness that comes extra nos , “from outside of us.” Our righteousness isn’t from us; it doesn’t come from what we do. It can’t be earned by saying a prayer or even by having a good attitude. Our righteousness is ultimately found in and belongs to another, our Savior Jesus Christ. 3. Crux sola est nostra theologia On October 31, 1517, Luther famously posted his Ninety-five Theses on the door of Castle Church. In it, Luther spoke clearly against the money-raising indulgence schemes Pope Leo X and Germany’s own Prince Albert of Brandenburg had sponsored. The next year, in April 1518, Luther defended these views at the Augustinian order’s spring meeting in Heidelberg. Luther walked to the meeting in fear. He expected the leaders there to sternly rebuke him. After all, that’s what the pope had asked them to do. But to Luther’s surprise, the leaders at the meeting welcomed his defense with excitement. What did Luther say that got his new friends so excited? In his Heidelberg Disputation , Luther described two types of people—the “theologian of glory” and the “theologian of the cross.” Theologians of glory think people are capable and smart enough to know God through human reason. They also say we can know who God’s righteous people are because we see God reward them with political power, success, and wealth. Though Luther didn’t use Albert’s and Leo’s names in his disputation, it’s clear he was talking about their greedy doctrine of indulgences when he described the theologian of glory. Luther’s “theologian of the cross,” by contrast, knows it’s not always people who appear good, beautiful, and powerful by worldly standards who truly know God. After all, Jesus didn’t look glorious on the cross. “One deserves to be called a true theologian,” Luther wrote , “who sees God even in suffering.” As Paul wrote, “God chose what is foolish in the world to shame the wise; God chose what is weak in the world to shame the strong” (1 Cor. 1:27). After Heidelberg, the phrase “ Crux sola est nostra theologia ” (“The cross alone is our theology”) became a rallying cry for Luther’s followers. It still is today. 4. Oratio, meditatio, tentatio Luther’s teaching set the Protestant Reformation in motion. In support of his reforms, Luther published hundreds of books, sermons, and hymns. Significantly, he also translated the entire Bible into the language of Germany’s common people. But Luther didn’t want common people to merely read Scripture. He wanted them to study it too. In the 1539 preface to the Wittenberg edition of his German writings, Luther wrote, “God himself lives in the Bible. Therefore, worthy Christian: get in, get in!” Luther gave his readers three rules for digging into God’s Word. Each has its own Latin term: prayer ( oratio ), meditation ( meditatio ), and suffering ( tentatio ). A ‘theologian of the cross’ knows it’s not always people who appear good, beautiful, and powerful by worldly standards who truly know God. The first rule is kept before we read the Bible. Luther wrote, “Kneel down in your private room and with humility, pray to God to give you his Holy Spirit to enlighten and guide and give you understanding.” The second rule is kept while reading: “Read and reread the very words written down in the Bible. Observe and think about what the Holy Spirit means.” The last rule is kept when we practice what the Scriptures say. Luther said, As soon as you begin to know God’s word, the devil will afflict you. . . . This suffering will teach you how right, true, sweet, lovely, mighty, and comforting God’s word is. It is wisdom supreme. 5. Simul iustus et peccator Luther was zealous and driven. He once said, “When I want to compose, write, pray, and preach well, I must be angry.” But while anger may have given Luther energy for work, it too often burned out of control. Sadly, today, Luther is as famous for his harsh words spoken against his enemies and the Jews as he is for recovering the biblical doctrine of justification. Throughout his life, Luther taught that believers are simul iustus et peccator . That’s Latin for “simultaneously justified and a sinner.” Both realities are true of every Christian. Both were true of Luther. He was a broken man who desperately needed God’s grace, and he knew it. Luther died while visiting Eisleben on February 18, 1546. Before he died, Luther scribbled out his last written words: “We are beggars. This is true.” Luther knew he could never earn God’s grace. Salvation isn’t won through indulgences or daily prayers. This is what Luther had discovered from the Bible and taught again to the world. God sent his only Son. Christ has overcome the world. All he asks of poor, begging sinners is that we believe.
featured.content_zh: 马丁·路德于1483年11月10日生于德国艾斯莱本. 第二天他在圣彼得和保罗教堂被洗礼. 7岁时,路德进入了曼斯菲尔德拉丁学校. 他在那里学习了拉丁语的语法和祷告,并记住了艾索普的"寓言". 从早年到后来在马格德堡的寄宿学校学习,路德是一名勤奋的学生。 他跟上了拉丁语,几个重要的拉丁语短语也出现在路德的著作中. 其中5个是他的生平和首席神学重心的良好总结. 1. Iustitia Dei 1505年7月,路德被猛烈的雷暴所困. 惊慌惊恐地与上帝讨价还价,许诺成为和尚. 进入修道院后,路德再次被恐惧所克服. 当他第一次作为牧师主持弥撒时, 相反,充满了颤抖。 随着礼拜的开始,路德在礼拜堂前取而代之,他开始背诵拉丁语祈祷. 路德知道上帝在判断上是完美的,并且完全没有罪恶. 因此,当他想到了iustitia Dei“上帝的公义”(1:17)时,恐怖袭击了他。 传记家罗兰·H·班顿(Roland H. Bainton)描述了困扰路德思想的思想:我该向神圣的陛下举起手来, 众天神围绕他. 在他点头的时候,大地会颤抖... ...但是,我是灰尘和灰烬。 当路德拿起面包和葡萄酒时,他摇得这么厉害,差点把杯子掉下. 在那些年里,路德在学校和修道院里长大,他只把上帝的正义或正义视为他对人类罪恶的积极判断。 他后来写道, 虽然我作为一个和尚生活 没有责备, 我感觉和知道我是上帝面前的罪人。 我有一个极度不安的良心。 我憎恨惩罚罪人的善良之神 2. 1512年,路德成为维滕贝格的大学教授. 当他为他的演讲而学习圣经时,他开始在新的光芒下看到上帝的正义. 路德看到耶稣基督如何对待我们的人性,他如何过上完美的生活并死于十字架上的痛苦而可耻的死亡来取取罪的惩罚. 他看见了上帝如何使耶稣从死地复活,以及他现在如何通过信仰为基督徒辩护. 上帝宣布,在他看来,耶稣的完美生活和牺牲的死亡对所有信徒都很重要。 因此上帝的正义不仅仅是他的判断。 这也是他的救赎天赋。 耶稣的完美生活和牺牲的死亡是所有信徒的计数. 因此上帝的正义不仅仅是他的判断。 这也是他的天赋。 当路德做出这个发现时发生了什么? 他是这样描述的 : “ 我感到我再次出生,并通过开放的大门进入了天堂。 ” 在那一天之后,路德开始教导上帝给予基督徒“外星人的正义 ” , 即“来自我们以外的”一种格外不义的正义。 我们的正义不是来自我们, 祈祷, 我们的正义最终被发现 并属于另一个,我们的救主耶稣基督。 3. Crux sola est nostra Godologia 1517年10月31日,路德将他的"95个本事"出名地贴在了城堡教堂的门上. 路德在书中明确表示反对教皇利奥十世和德国自己的勃兰登堡阿尔贝特亲王赞助的集资宽恕计划。 次年,即1518年4月,路德在海德堡举行的奥古斯丁会令春季会议上为这些观点辩护. 路德在恐惧中走去开会. 他期望那里的领导人严厉斥责他。 这毕竟是教皇要求他们做的。 但令路德惊讶的是,与会领导人激动地欢迎他的辩护. 路德怎么说 他的新朋友这么兴奋? 路德在他的"海德堡争论"中描述了两类人——"荣耀之神"和"十字架之神". 荣耀的神学家们认为,人的能力和智慧足以通过人类理性来认识上帝. 他们也说,我们可以知道上帝的善良人民是谁,因为我们看到真主以政治力量、成功和财富奖励他们。 虽然路德在争论中并没有使用阿尔伯特和利奥的名字,但很明显,当他描述荣耀的神学家时,他在谈论他们贪婪的宽恕理论。 相对而言,路德的“十字架神学家”知道,并非总能让世界标准显示良好、美丽和强大的人真正了解上帝。 毕竟耶稣在十字架上并不光荣。 路德写道 : “ 一个人应该被称为真正的神学家,” 路德写道,“谁在痛苦中看到上帝。 ” 正如保罗所写道的:“上帝选择了世界上的愚蠢来羞辱智者;上帝选择了世界上的弱者来羞辱强者。” 海德堡之后, " Crux sola est nostra Godologia " ( " 十字架是我们的神学 " )成为路德信徒的呼声。 今天还是这样。 4. Oratio、meditatio、tentatio Luther的教义使新教改革运动开始。 为支持他的改革,路德出版了上百本书,布道,并作"赞". 重要的是,他还将整个"圣经"翻译成了德国普通人的语言. 但路德并不想普通人只读圣经。 他希望他们也研究它。 路德在他的德文著作"维滕贝格"1539年版的前言中写道:"上帝自己活在圣经中. 因此,值得的基督徒:上车,上车!” 路德给了读者三条钻入上帝之道的规则. 每个词都有自己的拉丁名词:祷告(oratio),冥想(meditatio)和苦难(tentatio). 一个“十字架的神学家”知道,并非总有人以世界标准看起来是好人、美丽人和强大的人真正了解上帝。 第一条规则在我们读出"圣经"之前被保留. 路德写道:“跪在你的私人房间里谦逊地祈祷真主赐予你他的圣灵以启蒙、引导和谅解。” 第二条规则在读取时保留:“读取并重读圣经所写的文字。 观察并思考圣灵的意义。” 最后一个规则是当我们实践圣经所说的话时, 路德说,一旦你明白上帝的话,恶魔就会折磨你。 这种痛苦将教你如何正确、真实、甜蜜、可爱、强大并安慰上帝的话。 智慧至高无上。 5. Simul iustus et peccator Luther是狂热和有动力的。 他曾经说过:“当我想写作、写作、祈祷和讲道的时候,我一定生气了。” 但是,虽然愤怒可能已经让路德精力充沛地工作,但是它经常被烧得失控. 可悲的是,今天,路德以其对敌人和犹太人的严酷言辞而出名,如同他收复了圣经中的辩解学说而出名. 路德一生教导信徒们, 这在拉丁语中是“极端合理和有罪者 ” 。 每个基督教徒都一样 路德也一样 他是一个破碎的人,他迫切需要上帝的恩惠,他知道这一点。 1546年2月18日路德在访问艾斯莱本时去世. 在他死前,路德写出他最后的文字:“我们是乞丐。 这是事实。” Luther知道他永远得不到上帝的恩惠。 救赎不是通过宽容或日常祈祷而赢得的。 这是路德从圣经中发现的,并再次向世界传授. 上帝派他唯一的儿子 基督战胜了这个世界 他只要求贫穷 乞求罪人 我们相信

featured.title: Ministry and Marriage: How to Be a Healthy Team
featured.summary: Marriages with one or both spouses employed in ministry face unique pressures, challenges, and opportunities.
featured.summary_zh: 与受雇于部委的配偶一方或双方的婚姻面临独特的压力、挑战和机遇。 多年来,我们的变化,我们各部的变化,对我们的压力也发生了变化。 我们如何以使我们更接近而不是把我们分开的方式来引导这些变化? 在这场在TGC25上录制的讨论中,迈克尔和露西·艾克森(Lucy Aitcheson)与吉姆和安吉拉·戴维斯(Angela Davis)谈起他们试图保持婚姻健康同时忠实地处理婚姻的经历.
featured.title_zh: 事工与婚姻：如何成为一个健康的团队
featured.content: Marriages with one or both spouses employed in ministry face unique pressures, challenges, and opportunities. Over the years, we change, our ministries change, and the pressures on us change. How can we navigate these changes in a way that draws us closer to each other instead of driving us apart? In this discussion, recorded at TGC25, Michael and Lucy Aitcheson talk with Jim and Angela Davis about their experiences of seeking to keep their marriage healthy while ministering faithfully. featured.title_zh: “蚊子碗” ：前线的足球明星
featured.content: Peter Berg’s The Mosquito Bowl is essentially Friday Night Lights meets Hacksaw Ridge . It’s a movie with the same creative vibe as Friday Night Lights (gritty handheld camera, muted color palette, Explosions in the Sky post-rock soundtrack) but applied to a brutally violent true story of WWII’s Battle of Okinawa, one of the single bloodiest battles of the 20th century. Also like Berg’s Friday Night Lights , The Mosquito Bowl ( out now in theaters ; coming to Netflix November 25) is based on a book by Pulitzer Prize–winning journalist Buzz Bissinger . The 2022 book—subtitled A Game of Life and Death in World War II —only has one chapter (of 41) devoted to the actual 1944 football game dubbed “The Mosquito Bowl.” Most of the book is about the war, and the young men who left wives, kids, and promising NFL careers to fight it. Likewise, Berg’s film adaptation is mostly a somber, unflinching WWII film, with a brief reprieve of joy in the form of a football game on Guadalcanal between the 4th and 29th regiments of the 6th Marine Division. Just as in Friday Night Lights , where the drama of high school football parallels the struggles and triumphs of life off the field, the football game in The Mosquito Bowl parallels the “game of life and death” that surrounds the men at war. Sports are interesting in this way: They provide escape from real life but also training for it, an arena of danger and high stakes but not ultimate stakes. Sports often map onto life—we draw up plans and plays but have to improvise; we get hurt but can heal; we thrive individually through teamwork; sometimes we win and sometimes we lose. Yet sports are unlike real life too. Winning or losing on the field is a matter of trophies and glory, but off the field, it can be a matter of life and death. Young Men Willing to Fight and Die The Mosquito Bowl (rated R for graphic war violence and language), opens with a well-known epigraph from Herbert Hoover : Older men declare war. But it is youth that must fight and die. And it is youth who must inherit the tribulation, the sorrow, and the triumphs that are the aftermath of war. This is a movie about youth—or rather, the passage from youth into adulthood that war accelerates. This is a movie about youth—or rather, the passage from youth into adulthood that war accelerates. The movie opens with muddy college football scenes in the fall of 1941, as the four central characters are introduced: John McLaughry (Nicholas Galitzine), Brown quarterback; Bob Baumann (Bill Skarsgård), University of Wisconsin tackle; Tony Butkovich (Ray Nicholson), Purdue fullback; and Dave Schreiner (Tom Francis), Wisconsin end. They were all-star athletes with promising futures. Many of them were collegiate All-Americans and drafted by NFL teams. Yet December 7, 1941, happened, and their futures were all changed. Once bound together by football skill, friendly rivalry, and fierce competition on the gridiron, these men soon bonded in a different setting: as marines in WWII’s savage Pacific theater. Instead of fighting for yards on the field, they fought for ground in a war of attrition on Okinawa. Instead of a football in hand, they carried guns and bayonets. Instead of tackling their opponents, they wrestled them to the death in hand-to-hand combat. Like many in the Greatest Generation, these men volunteered to enlist and fight. The Mosquito Bowl celebrates their duty and sacrifice. In one scene, Baumann’s younger brother says, “You don’t have to go,” to which Baumann replies, “I do. I’m needed.” It’s hard to imagine star athletes, whether collegiate or professional, volunteering to go to war in 2026. But in 1943, it was normal. Okinawa, Bissinger writes in the book, was “by far the largest collection of athletes ever to die in a single battle.” And in the entirety of WWII, 21 NFL players died in combat, as well as two players from Major League Baseball. Why were they so willing to lay down their lives? Perhaps back then, men had the bigger horizon more in view. Life isn’t about serving oneself. It’s about serving others, fighting for things bigger than personal fulfillment. As Dave Schreiner tells John McLaughry, “This is us sacrificing for the unborn. What other real thing is there? What’s the point in all of this if it’s not for passing something on?” Numbed by War-Movie Violence The Mosquito Bowl honors the Greatest Generation and is commendable in its straightforward embrace of manly virtues like duty and sacrifice. But I disliked several aspects of the film. One is the language. I realize wartime soldiers in every era tend to be prolific in their employment of profane language. But even if men in the 1940s were as creative with the f-word as they are in this movie, is it really essential to the movie? It makes the film much less likely to be watched by families, which is a shame because it’s the sort of thing dads might want to watch with their younger sons. I also wish Berg had given less screen time to bloody battles and more time to quieter character moments and the titular football game. I get that it’s important to underscore the savage bloodbath that was the Pacific theater, and I get that the joyful escape of football is most pronounced when juxtaposed with the horrific realities of war. But it’s hard for contemporary war movies to viscerally depict the “war is hell” experience after the genre has been so saturated. Edward Berger’s adaptation of All Quiet on the Western Front (2022) felt like the final word on war-movie blood and guts. We’ve become numb to watching bodies get mangled every which way. Going forward, movies about savage warfare probably need to take a different approach. There are ways to capture battle horror without showing every gruesome detail. Furthermore, the desaturated, shaky-camera, chaotic choreography of war movies has become clichéd. I checked out a bit during these prolonged battle scenes. At times, it felt like Berg was inspired by Terrence Malick’s Guadalcanal movie, The Thin Red Line (one of the best war movies of all time). But what made Malick’s film so effective is that it employed violence only in a few intense, lyrical sequences, juxtaposed with long stretches of more contemplative material and tender character moments. The experience of war is important to capture accurately. But a war film becomes great when the meaning of war is also a focal point. Clint Eastwood’s WWII diptych, Flags of our Fathers and Letters from Iwo Jima (2006), strikes this balance well. The action-to-reflection ratio is not quite right in The Mosquito Bowl . Football as Far as the Curse Is Found The high point of Berg’s movie is the Mosquito Bowl game, even though it occupies too little of the overall runtime. In a movie that is rather bleak thematically and visually, the game provides a much-needed moment of joy for the characters and audience. Hosted as a morale booster for soldiers who would soon be sent to fight on Okinawa, the game (broadcast on the “mosquito radio network”) was set up to be “two-hand touch” only but quickly devolved into full-on tackle. Some of the guys wore Santa hats. There were big smiles, laughs, playful rivalry: young men allowed to be boys again. Here’s how Bissinger describes it in the prologue of his book: For roughly two hours the Mosquito Bowl wasn’t simply a reminder of what life had once been like for the players, but freedom and abandon, with the spectators captured in the same moment, screaming their heads off, whether drunk or sober. The beauty of sports, the ultimate power of it to carry you away, had never been stronger. But the scene is also bittersweet, for we know it’s not reality. Real life is harsh. Okinawa looms. Many of these boys playing football on Christmas Eve 1944 won’t live to see Christmas Eve 1945. This scene reminded me of the resonant poetry of Friday Night Lights , which depicted football in much the same way: youthful vibrancy and freewheeling joy, but tempered by the painful pressures

Bissinger在书中写道,冲绳是“迄今为止在一次战斗中死亡的运动员人数最多的集合地”。 而在整个二战中,有21名NFL球员在战斗中丧生,还有来自主力联赛棒球的两名球员. 为什么他们这么愿意牺牲自己的生命? 也许那时,男人的视野更大 生活不是为自己服务。 而是为他人服务, 正如Dave Schreiner告诉John McLaughry的那样,“这是我们为未出生的人而牺牲。 还有什么真实的? 如果不是为了传递东西, "蚊子碗"以战争电影"暴力"(War-Movie Violence The Mosquito Bowl)为荣,以直截了当地拥抱"责任"和"牺牲"等人性美德而著称. 但我不喜欢电影的几个方面。 一是语言. 我意识到每个时代的战时士兵在使用污名语言方面往往很繁多. 但是,即使20世纪40年代的男性对"f-word"的创造力和这出电影中的一样,这是否真的对电影至关重要? 这让影片不太可能被家人看, 我也希望伯格给 较少的屏幕时间 对于血腥的战斗 更多的时间 安静的角色时刻 和三角足球比赛。 我理解强调太平洋剧场的野蛮流血很重要, 但当代战争电影很难直截了当地描绘出"战争就是地狱", Edward Berger在"西部战线"(2022年)上改编的"All Quiet"(All Quiet on the Western Front (2022年)),感觉就像战争-电影"血和胆"上的最后一句话. 我们对看尸体被打乱已经麻木了。 向前看,关于野蛮战争的电影可能需要采取不同的做法。 有一些方法捕捉出战斗恐怖而不展示出每一个可怕的细节. 此外,战争电影的不饱和、摇摇欲坠、杂乱无章地编舞也成了陈词滥调。 我在这些漫长的战斗场景中检查了一下 贝格有时觉得受到特伦斯·马利克出演的瓜达尔卡纳尔电影"瘦子红线"的启发(这是有史以来最好的战争电影之一). 但马利克的影片之所以如此有效, 是因为影片只使用几起激烈的、充满诗意的相接相接的暴力事件, 战争的经验对于准确捕捉是重要的. 但当战争的意义也成为焦点时,战争电影就变得伟大了. Clint Eastwood的二战Diptych, 我们父亲的旗帜和来自硫磺岛的信件 (2006年) 很好地实现了这种平衡。 《蚊子碗》中的动作-反射比并不完全正确。 足球如被诅咒所发现 Berg的电影的顶点是"蚊子碗"(Mosquito Bowl)游戏,尽管它占据了整个跑步时间太少. 在一部相当暗淡的主题和视觉电影中,游戏为角色和观众提供了非常需要的快乐时刻. 游戏(在“Mosquito电台网络”上广播)的制作只是“双手触摸”, 有些家伙戴了圣诞老人帽子。 曾有"大笑","取笑","玩弄相争":青年男子允许再做男孩. 以下是Bissinger在书前所描述的: 蚊子碗在大约两小时的时间里, 体育的美丽, 其最终的力量 把你带走, 从来没有更强大。 因为我们知道这不是现实。 现实生活很严酷 冲绳开始出现。 许多人在1944年平安夜踢足球, 这个场景让我想起周五"夜光"(Friday Night Lights)的回响性诗歌,这些诗歌以同样的方式描绘了足球:青春的活力和自由转动的快活,但被痛苦的压力所缓解.

featured.summary: Pastor, you cannot afford to coast. You cannot afford autopilot. Be a gospel entrepreneur. Eternity is at stake.

featured.title_zh: 牧师，抓住机会
featured.content: My coffee had gone cold as the church planter mourned that his church felt stagnant. Worse than not growing—a thick malaise had settled over the congregation. The first three years were exciting; the community was intrigued by a new church plant, genuinely curious about what it was all about. But everything had plateaued. Leaders grew complacent. Sundays—even with strong preaching—felt cold and passionless. The church’s reason for existing had shrunk to feeding and caring for the Christians who already called it home. The church planter couldn’t see how it was still transforming the community. An older mentor at the table cleared his throat. “I’m sorry to hear that. Let me ask you—what is one risky, hard thing the Lord is inviting your church to do that you’re hesitant to do?” The planter scratched his head. “I don’t know. I’ve never been asked that before.” The older man shrugged. “Every pastor should be ready to answer that question. If he can’t, he needs to spend some time praying and fasting until he can. Comfort and complacency are incredibly dangerous.” I’ve sat in enough of these conversations to know that wise, healthy risks are vital to the life of the church. Without them, the church atrophies. Its reason for existing collapses into self-care and, after a few years, into self-preservation. Risky and hard things keep gospel blood flowing through the body. Pastor, you cannot afford to coast. You cannot afford autopilot. You owe it to Jesus and to your church to make the most of opportunities in your city—which means that alongside preaching, teaching, praying, and developing leaders, you need to prioritize seeking new avenues for ministry. Be a gospel entrepreneur. Church-planting networks have long understood that entrepreneurial aptitude is essential for planters. But what about established churches—do their pastors need to be entrepreneurial too? What Is a Gospel Entrepreneur? There’s still hesitancy around saying pastors need entrepreneurial aptitude. Maybe it’s because we picture someone who constantly starts new things he can’t sustain—a person with a billion ideas who follows through on none of them. If this is what we mean, then no, we don’t want our pastors to be entrepreneurial. Comfort and complacency are incredibly dangerous. But a gospel entrepreneur is something different. He doesn’t pile up harebrained ideas. He stays awake and sober-minded about the opportunities the Lord is opening in the community. He sees the wooden frames of a new development and prays about how the gospel will reach those families once they move in. He looks at neighborhoods where existing churches can’t possibly reach everyone—and plants a church there. He saves, scrimps, and sacrifices to move a growing church plant into a more strategic location. He keeps his eyes open, his mind sharp, and his hands ready for the moment God opens a door. Biblical Call When this topic comes up, someone usually asks, “Where do you see the need for a pastor to be an entrepreneur in the Bible?” My answer often surprises people: Jesus’s parable of the dishonest manager. In Luke 16:1–9, a rich man discovers his property manager has been wasting his possessions and tells him to settle accounts—he’s about to be fired. The manager realizes losing his job means either digging or begging, so he immediately goes to work cutting deals to gain favor with other wealthy employers. When his employer finds out, he commends the manager for his shrewdness. Ethical or not, it was a genius move. At this point, we should ask, Why is Jesus telling this story? Maybe he’s about to indict people like the manager. But the manager’s dishonesty has nothing to do with Jesus’s point. The twist is that Jesus holds up the dishonest manager as an example of what he wants his disciples to be. “The master commended the dishonest manager for his shrewdness,” Jesus says. “For the sons of this world are more shrewd in dealing with their own generation than the sons of light” (Luke 16:8). The parable is, if anything, a lament. The world’s sons do a better job seizing opportunities to advance their kingdoms than we do in advancing Christ’s. The implication is sobering. The sons of light need to be as intentional and opportunistic about eternity as the world is about temporary gain. We need pastors who will prayerfully take risks, do hard things, feel the urgency, and grab opportunities. A gospel entrepreneur stays awake and sober-minded about the opportunities the Lord is opening in the community. Consider it this way. Walmart and Target already have plans for that empty lot next to the new development. Millions of dollars are being spent on demographic studies and marketing campaigns to grow somebody’s bottom line. Believe it or not, there’s probably a developer with more aggressive ideas for your church building than you have. I’ve even heard a story of a dying church in a small Colorado town that was slowly pushed out of its building—a local developer sent people to join as members, just so they could vote to sell. The sons of the world know how to expand their kingdoms. In the verses that follow the parable, Jesus connects the parable to faithfulness in little things, stewarding earthly resources well, and remembering that we serve God, not our budgets and assets. Our goal as pastors isn’t to keep our congregants happy, live off endowments, or maintain the institution’s favorite donors. Our job is to call people to pick up their crosses and follow Jesus into risky opportunities, where even if we die, people will see Jesus. Don’t Be Risk Averse The dishonest manager knew he had no time to be risk-averse or complacent. He had to seize every opportunity to save his own skin. Pastors and churches have no time to be risk-averse either—not for our own sake but for the gospel’s. Eternity is at stake. Pastor, be a gospel entrepreneur. When we stand before our Lord on the last day, may it not be true that the sons of the world had a greater influence on our community than we did.
featured.content_zh: 我的咖啡凉了,因为教堂规划师哀悼 他的教堂感到停滞。 更糟糕的是,一种浓郁的疾病已经笼罩着整个会众。 头三年令人兴奋; 社区被一个新的教会工厂所吸引, 真正好奇的是它是什么。 但一切都已经稳定下来了 领导人越来越自满。 星期日,即使有强烈的传道,也感到寒冷而无激情。 教堂的存在原因已经缩小,以供养和照顾已经称之为家的基督徒。 教会规划师无法理解如何仍在改变社区。 餐桌上一位年长的导师清了喉咙. " 我很遗憾听到这个消息。 我问你,上帝邀请你的教会来做你犹豫不决的事,这有多么危险? 栽培者将他的头挠了. “我不知道。 我从来没有被问过。 长者作是灌顶. “每个牧师应准备回答这个问题。 如果做不到,他需要花一些时间祈祷和禁食,直到他能够。 舒适和自满是极其危险的。” 我受够了这些对话, 知道明智、健康的风险对教会的生活至关重要。 没有他们,教堂的奖杯。 它的存在原因陷入了自我护理,并在几年后陷入了自我保护. 冒险而艰难的东西使血流经身体 牧师,你负担不起海岸。 你买不起自动驾驶 你对耶稣和你的教会都有责任 在你的城市里充分利用机会 也就是说,除了传教、教义、祈祷和发展领袖之外,你需要优先考虑为部委寻找新的途径。 成为福音企业家. 教会植树网早就明白,创业能力对植树人至关重要。 但是,那些已经成立的教会——他们的牧师也需要创业吗? 福音企业家是什么? 牧师需要创业能力, 可能是因为我们想象有人不断发起新事物, 如果这就是我们的意思,那么不,我们不希望我们的牧师成为企业家。 舒适和自满是极其危险的。 但福音企业家却不同 他不会堆起后脑勺的想法。 他保持清醒和清醒的头脑 关于机会 上帝正在社区打开。 他看到新发展的木框,并祈祷一旦这些家庭搬入,福音会如何传入. 他看着周围的街道, 他为了把一个正在成长的教会植物迁入一个更具战略意义的地点而拯救了,施舍了,并做出了牺牲. 他睁开双眼,头脑锐利,手为上帝打开一扇门时刻做好准备. 圣经召唤 当这个话题出现时,人们通常会问:“你在哪里看到牧师在圣经中成为企业家的必要性?” 我的回答常常让人惊讶:耶稣以不诚实的经理为例。 在Luke 16:1–9中,一个富人发现他的地产经理在浪费他的财产,并告诉他结清账款——他即将被开除。 经理意识到失去工作意味着挖掘或乞讨,所以他立即去工作切割交易,以获得其他富有雇主的青睐. 当他的雇主发现后,他赞扬经理的狡猾. 道德与否,这是一个天才的举动。 此时此刻,我们应该问,耶稣为什么讲这个故事? 也许他即将起诉经理这样的人。 但经理的不诚实与耶稣的观点无关. 曲折之处在于耶稣举起不诚实的经理作为他想要他的门徒们成为什么的例子. “主人称赞这位不诚实的经理的狡猾,”耶稣说。 “因为这个世界的儿子在处理自己的一代时比光明的儿子们更精明”(公爵16:8)。 譬喻如来所叹. 世界的儿子们比我们更能抓住机会推进他们的王国, 含义是清醒的。 光之子们需要像关于暂时收益的世界一样,是有意和机会性的。 我们需要牧师,他们将祈祷 冒险,做艰难的事情, 感受紧迫感,抓住机会。 一个福音的企业家 保持清醒和清醒的头脑 关于机会 主正在社区打开。 这样吧 Walmart和Target在新开发旁边已经计划了空地。 数百万美元用于人口研究和营销活动, 无论信不信, 可能有一个开发商 比你的教堂建筑更具有攻击性。 我甚至听到一个故事, 说科罗拉多州小镇的一座教堂正在死亡, 这座教堂被慢慢推出, 天下之子有能扩张其地之道. 在"比喻"之后的诗句中,耶稣将比喻与小事中的忠诚联系起来,妥善地管理地上的资源,并记住我们服务于上帝,而不是我们的预算和资产. 作为牧师,我们的目标不是让我们的教友们快乐,靠捐赠维持生活,或者维持该机构最喜爱的捐赠者。 我们的工作是号召人们拾起十字架,并跟随耶稣去冒险的机会,即使我们死了,人们也会看到耶稣. 不要规避风险 不诚实的经理知道,他没有时间反风险或自满。 他不得不抓住一切机会拯救自己的皮肤. 牧师和教会也没有时间回避风险, 永相危难. 牧师,做一个福音企业家。 当我们在最后一天站在我们的主面前时,也许世界的子孙对我们社会的影响比我们大。

featured.content: Get RNS’ thoughtful, essential religion reporting every morning. Sign up for free! (RNS) — Many have puzzled over the unusual number of pastors, former pastors and seminarians running for Congress as Democrats this year, but not the Rev. Adam Hamilton. Asked in August about the trend, Hamilton, a United Methodist megachurch pastor running an unexpectedly competitive race for U.S. Senate in Kansas as a Democrat, answered immediately. “Since the beginning of 2025, things are so abnormal in Washington, D.C.,” he told Religion News Service, explaining he believes actions by the Trump administration have spurred people to wrestle with what, exactly, constitutes American values. “I think there’s a lot of religious people — especially, I think, mainline Protestant pastors — who are saying: Somebody’s got to do something,” he said, adding that pastors-turned-candidates like himself are “feeling the sense of call, and I’m going to attribute it to the Holy Spirit.” It’s a sentiment shared by a surprising number of Democratic candidates this election cycle. Of the nine pastors, former pastors and seminarians running for Congress as Democrats this year, six — including four locked in tight, widely watched races — belong to mainline Protestant denominations , such as the UMC, Presbyterian Church (USA), and Evangelical Lutheran Church in America. The candidacies have put a spotlight on the theology of primarily white mainline Protestants, a politically moderate group whose clergy skew liberal and whose members make up around 13% of the U.S. population, according to the Public Religion Research Institute . The slate of mainline candidates with religious training follows a nearly decade-long spike in political engagement largely in response to the rise of President Donald Trump and his evangelical supporters. From Texas to Iowa to Kansas, mainline Protestant candidates, while careful to voice support for the separation of church and state, are giving voice to forms of public theology that could reclaim a position their tradition lost decades ago: a recognized Christian power in U.S. politics. Heath Carter, a scholar of American religion at Princeton Theological Seminary, said mainliners are having a moment partly because they have grown so frustrated with the longstanding dominance of conservative evangelicals in U.S. politics. “You probably see people who’ve wanted to say, ‘Hey, this is not the full extent of Christian witness. These folk actually don’t have a monopoly on Christian public witness,’” Carter said. “There are these other traditions of justice-oriented, pluralism-affirming, democratic Christian theology and politics that we want to tap into.” A more than 100-year split This unusual political moment, Carter said, is rooted in a split that has divided U.S. Christians for more than a century. Beginning in the 1920s, conservative-leaning Christians began blasting the theology of so-called “modernist” Christians, relative theological liberals who embraced a less literal approach to the Bible and concepts such as evolution. The conservative Christian bloc eventually broke away in protest, branding themselves “fundamentalists” and later embracing the term evangelicals. Meanwhile, liberal-leaning Christians became an ascendant force within mainline denominations, emerging as the leading religious influence in the U.S. for most of the 20th century. Their clergy forged alliances with Black Protestants during the Civil Rights Movement. And by the 1980s, mainliners were already engaged in heated debates over gay and lesbian rights, with many major denominations eventually moving to ordain LGBTQ+ people and allow clergy to officiate same-sex marriages. That history impacted Texas state Rep. James Talarico, a PC(USA) seminarian running a closely watched campaign for U.S. Senate in the state. The Democrat grew up attending St. Andrew’s Presbyterian Church in Austin, a deeply liberal PC(USA) church whose pastor, the Rev. Jim Rigby, was put on trial by the denomination in the early 2000s for ordaining a lesbian and officiating a same-sex marriage before the denomination approved such practices. (The charges were eventually dismissed on a technicality.) When Talarico, who cites Rigby as a spiritual mentor , entered politics years later, he imbued his political rhetoric with liberal theology. He told Religion News Service in 2023 that he staunchly opposes Christian nationalism and believes using political power to hurt LGBTQ+ people and other marginalized groups is “blasphemous.” But the mainline embrace of LGBTQ+ rights in the 2010s coincided with an overall reduction of membership and followed an era where conservative Christians — particularly evangelicals — reentered politics with a fervor. Rising to power as “values voters” in the ’ 90s, evangelicals and other conservative Christians have long derided the mainline embrace of LGBTQ+ rights, often suggesting those who do are un-Christian. That tradition persists: Pastor Robert Jeffress, a vocal Trump supporter who leads the Southern Baptist megachurch First Baptist Dallas, said on a podcast last month with Texas Lt. Governor Dan Patrick that Talarico is not a Christian, citing the representative’s past statements on gender and sexuality. He reiterated that stance in an interview with RNS, saying Talarico’s beliefs “disqualify him from being a Christian, and especially a Christian pastor.” Jeffress also voiced skepticism of the Democratic clergy and seminarians running as Democrats this year, noting most “come from mainline denominations that tend to be more liberal in their theological beliefs, and are becoming a decreasing part of the American population.” Even so, Jeffress acknowledged that evangelicals — including his own denomination — are now losing members as well. And what mainliners lack in numbers, they have made up for in visibility during the rise of Donald Trump. During his 2016 presidential campaign, Trump was still a mainliner himself — a Presbyterian like Talarico, having been baptized in a church that is currently PC(USA). But members of the denomination outraged by his rhetoric about immigrants launched an effort to kick him out (they were unsuccessful, as Trump was not an active member of any congregation ), and mainline Protestants quickly emerged as some of his loudest religious critics after he assumed the presidency. By the time he left office in 2020, Trump had changed his religious affiliation to “non-denominational.” Around the same time, mainline clergy such as the Rev. Sarah Trone Garriott, an Evangelical Lutheran Church in America pastor in Iowa, and the Rev. Lindsay James, a PC(USA) pastor who previously served as a chaplain on college campuses, began to enter politics. James ran and was elected to the Iowa House of Representative in 2019; in her campaign launch speech, she cited opposition to Trump’s proposed border wall. A year later, Garriott was elected to the Iowa state Senate , telling RNS at the time that she saw running for office as part of a “calling” to “care for my neighbor” and be “interconnected with others.” Thus began an embrace of politics that the Rev. Brian Ellison, a PC(USA) pastor who serves as Stated Clerk of the Synod of Mid-America and leads a group that advocates for LGBTQ+ people in the denomination, sees as a departure from past eras when mainliners were more reticent when it came to discussing their faith in public. Mainline Protestants, he said, “have at times sort of apologized for their public witness” or used secular language “so as not to be accused of violating a separation of church and state.” But recent years, he said, have seen mainline clergy “demonstrating a level of comfort and confidence in talking about a Christian approach to public policy.” Mainline clergy clash with ICE When Trump regained the presidency in 2024, mainliners — alongside many other people of faith — became even more visible in their pushback. (RNS)——许多人对今年作为民主党人竞选国会的牧师,前牧师和会士数量异常之多感到困惑,但并非亚当·汉密尔顿牧师. 8月被问及趋势,联合卫理公会特大教堂牧师汉密尔顿作为民主党人,在堪萨斯州为美国参议院进行一场出人意料的竞争,他立即回答. “自2025年初以来,华盛顿哥伦比亚特区的情况非常不正常,”他告诉宗教新闻社,他解释说,他相信特朗普政府的行动促使人们与美国价值观斗争。 “我认为有许多宗教人士 — — 特别是,我认为是主线的新教牧师 — — 正在说:有人必须做点什么,”他说,他补充说,牧师和他本人一样,是“感同身受,我要把它归功于圣灵。 ” 也是许多民主党候选人所认同的。 在今年竞选国会民主党议员的9名牧师中,有6名——包括4名被紧紧锁住,广受关注的种族——属于主干的新教教派,如UMC,长老会(美国)和美国福音路德会等. 以白人为主的新教徒为主的神学, 接受宗教培训的主线候选人名单紧接着长达近十年的政治参与激增,主要是为了应对唐纳德·特朗普总统及其福音派支持者的崛起. 从德克萨斯州到爱荷华州到堪萨斯州,主干线新教徒候选人在认真表达对教会和州分立的支持的同时,也给公众神学形式以发言权,这些形式可以恢复他们几十年前失去的传统:美国政治中公认的基督教力量. 美国宗教学者希斯·卡特(Heath Carter)在普林斯顿神学院(Princeton Theological Seminary)表示,主力派之所以有这一时刻,部分原因是他们因为保守派福音派人士在美国政治中的长期统治而变得如此沮丧. “你可能看到有些人想说,“嘿,这不是基督教证人的全部。 这些人并不垄断基督教公众证人。 “我们想利用的还有以正义为导向、以多元主义为主、民主的基督教神学和政治的其他传统。” 一百多年分红 卡特说,这个不寻常的政治时刻的根源在于一个多世纪以来使美国基督徒分裂的分裂. 从20世纪20年代开始,保守派的基督徒开始轰动所谓的"现代"基督徒的神学,相对的神学自由主义者对"圣经"和进化等概念所持的言行较少. 保守的基督教集团最终为了抗议而解体,自称为"原教旨主义者",后来拥护福音派一词. 与此同时,追求自由的基督徒成为了主线教派内部的一股优势力量,成为20世纪大部分时间里美国的主要宗教影响. 他们的神职人员在民权运动期间与黑人新教徒结成了联盟. 而到20世纪80年代,主流人士已经参与了关于男女同性恋权利的激烈辩论,许多主要教派最终都转向了Ordain LGBTQQ. 让神职人员认可同性婚姻 这段历史影响了德克萨斯州 詹姆斯·塔拉里克共和国,一个PC(美国)的神学院院士, 在美国州为参议院举办一场密切监视的运动。 民主党人成长于奥斯丁的圣安德鲁长老会,这是一座自由主义的PC(美国)教堂,牧师Jim Rigby牧师在2000年代初被教会审判,罪名是在教会批准这种做法之前任命女同性恋者并主持同性婚姻。 (这些指控最终因技术原因被驳回. ) 当塔拉里科(Talarico)引用里格比为精神导师, 他于2023年告诉宗教新闻服务社,他坚决反对基督教民族主义,并认为利用政治权力来伤害LGBT-Q和其他被边缘化群体是"亵渎". 但2010年代主线拥抱LGBT-QQ权利的同时,成员整体减少,紧随其后的时代,保守派基督徒——尤其是福音派教徒——以发火回流入政. 福音派和其他保守派基督徒长期嘲弄LGBTQQ的权利, 经常暗示那些不信奉基督教的人。 这一传统依然存在:领导美南浸信会特大教堂第一浸信会达拉斯的特朗普支持者罗伯特·杰弗里斯牧师上个月在与德克萨斯州长丹·帕特里克的播客上说,塔拉里科不是基督教徒,他引用了这位代表过去关于性别和性问题的说法。 他在接受RNS采访时重申了这一立场,称塔拉里科的信仰"使他没有资格成为基督徒,特别是基督徒牧师". Jeffress还表达了对民主党神职人员和神职人员今年以民主党身份竞选的怀疑,指出大部分“来自主线教派,这些教派倾向于在神学信仰上更加自由,并且正在成为美国人口正在减少的一部分。 即便如此,杰弗里斯承认福音派教徒——包括他自己的教派——现在也在失去成员。 而主线在人数上所缺乏的是,在唐纳德·特朗普崛起期间,他们在能见度上有所弥补. 在2016年总统竞选期间,特朗普本人仍是一名主要人物——像塔拉里科这样的长老会教徒,曾在目前为PC(美国)的教堂受洗. 但各教派成员对他关于移民的言论感到愤慨,他们发动了驱逐他的努力(他们没有成功,因为特朗普不是任何会众的积极成员),而主线新教徒在他出任总统后迅速成为他最大声的宗教批评者. 2020年卸任后,特朗普将宗教信仰改为"非教派". 大约在同一时间,主要神职人员,如艾奥瓦州的美国福音会路德会牧师Sarah Trone Garriott牧师和以前在大学校园担任牧师的PC(美国)牧师Lindsay James牧师,开始进入政界。 詹姆斯跑出并被选入了2019年的爱荷华州众议员大厦;她在其竞选启动演说中引用了反对特朗普提议的边界墙. featured.content: Get RNS’ thoughtful, essential religion reporting every morning. Sign up for free! ﻿ ﻿ This week on State of Belief, Rev. Paul Brandeis Raushenbush talks with Ambassador Norm Eisen, a renowned attorney, about election lawsuits, corruption, and the rule of law as the midterms approach. They also discuss how faith can bring people together across party lines. Listen now to hear what the Ambassador expects in the final days before Election Day. As co-founder of Democracy Defenders Fund, Norm has been in court fighting attempts to disenfranchise voters and subvert the Constitution; as he says, “We’ve got your back.” More about our guest Ambassador Norm Eisein is a globally recognized authority on law, ethics, and anti-corruption. He’s a graduate of Harvard Law School and former ambassador to the Czech Republic. As special counsel to the House Judiciary Committee from 2019 to 2020, he was a critical force in their work on the impeachment and trial of President Trump. He previously led the fight against corruption for the Obama administration. His books include A Case for the American People: the United States versus Donald Trump , and Overcoming Trumpery: How to Restore Ethics, the Rule of Law and Democracy . In 2023, Norm co-founded the Democracy Defenders Fund and serves as its executive chair. featured.title_zh: Etsy女巫的堕落
featured.content: Get RNS’ thoughtful, essential religion reporting every morning. Sign up for free! (RNS) — For years, witches found a home on Etsy. Now they’re facing a problem even magic can’t fix. Etsy witches hit the zeitgeist last year due to a series of viral videos and a controversial article about Etsy witches hexing conservative activist Charlie Kirk, but in recent months, longtime spellcasters have begun exiting the platform. Since its 2005 launch, the online marketplace has been known as a purveyor of homemade goods, vintage clothes and craft supplies — and, for those with magical inclinations, as a destination for the occult. Alongside personalized ornaments and embroidered tote bags, buyers could peruse spells for love, passing exams and good weather for a wedding. Some practitioners say they’ve left as Etsy cracks down on metaphysical content and grapples with an influx of AI-generated listings. But though Etsy may no longer be witches’ platform of choice, their offerings, practitioners say, remain as in demand as ever. “There’s been a migration from Etsy to platforms on the web,” said Florida-based spellcaster and gemologist Hank Mason, who co-founded the online shop Crystal Conjure Magic . “The whole concept of metaphysical services has had a difficult time finding a commercial platform to be on.” The tradition of purchasing spells is as old as witchcraft itself, said Courtney Weber, a witchcraft author and tarot reader based in Portland, Oregon. “There’s always been somebody in the community who could make the luck charm, who could make a love charm,” she said. These days, many of those purchases happen online. And research shows the practices may be losing their taboo. Last year, Pew Research Center found that nearly 1 in 3 Americans consult a fortune teller , tarot cards or astrology on a yearly basis, meaning Americans are about as likely to consult these practices as they are to attend religious services at least monthly. Scholars who study religion and modern witchcraft say the popularity of click-and-buy spells show that many buyers are seeking agency and guidance at a time of cultural upheaval. That popularity was especially evident last year. In 2025, beyond the Kirk controversy, Etsy witches gained new visibility as influencers posted about paying them to change wedding-day weather , repair romantic relationships , sway sports outcomes and secure big work wins . New York City-based influencer Jaz Smith posted a May 2025 TikTok with the caption: “me trying to explain to people that they got perfect weather for the holiday weekend because I paid a etsy witch for good weather for my wedding.” The video has over a million views. Today, searches for spells on Etsy turn up thousands of listings, many featuring images of candles or women draped in shawls. Some have AI-renderings of the spell’s desired outcome: a picturesque wedding day , an illustration of weight loss . Most spells are digital-only products; the purchaser submits information about the desired effect or questions they are seeking insight on, and the seller sends a picture of the ritual setup and an Etsy message with a summary of the ritual. Almost all include disclaimers that specific outcomes aren’t guaranteed. “In terms of people selling spells, there’s probably a gamut there that runs from people who certainly believe in their own power to help other people through magic, all the way to people who are charlatans and are taking advantage of other people because they can make a buck,” said Sabina Magliocco, professor emeritus at the University of British Columbia’s Department of Anthropology who studies the modern pagan movement. Within the metaphysical community, these spells can be divisive. Sociologist Helen Berger, who has studied contemporary witchcraft and magic since the 1980s, said many older witches — especially those who belong to a coven or who are Wiccan — feel that commercialization has tainted the practice. They value the tradition of passing down knowledge in community free of charge. “They feel that it’s moving away from the real meaning, spiritual meaning, of their practice,” said Berger. “The emphasis in the beginning was to move away from commercialization and move closer to nature, closer to a direct interchange with the divine or with the other world.” But other witches, including Weber, are glad to see spellcasters making a living whatever way they can. She said online platforms make witchcraft more accessible and can still be avenues for spiritual meaning and connection, even across the virtual divide. Still, witches with online storefronts have faced hurdles. EBay halted the sale of spells in 2012, and since 2015, Etsy’s services policy has banned metaphysical services, including spellcasting, rituals and items that advertise attracting specific outcomes. Historically, practitioners have evaded the policy by offering tangible goods along with their spells and labeling their spells as “for entertainment only.” But Mason of Crystal Conjure Magic said that last year, as Etsy witches gained attention, the platform began more strictly enforcing its ban on metaphysical content. “We left Etsy last summer,” said Mason, explaining he received an email from Etsy notifying him that it would be enforcing its rules. Since Crystal Conjure Magic already had a separate website selling the same offerings — “Back Together Spell” for $12.95, “Bewitching Beauty Spell Bundle” for $39.95 — they decided to leave. “They’re free to run it the way they want to. If you want to sell on their platform, you should follow their rules,” said Weber. Etsy didn’t respond to requests for comment. RELATED: ‘Witches’ epithet hurled at abortion proponents has roots in Appalachian history James, a Vancouver, British Columbia-based magician who asked to withhold his last name, citing personal and professional repercussions, has been on Etsy for eight years. He updated his Etsy listings to ensure they abide by the guidelines, selling tangible goods like amulets and ritual kits. His spells are now purchased through his individual Planetary Spells site . James said sellers are “moving out en masse” due to concerns about Etsy’s selling fees, challenges with the search algorithm and a deluge of AI-generated content. “Ever since the whole AI boom, there are people out there that are churning AI slop really, really quickly,” James told RNS. “Etsy built much of its identity around handmade products, independent creators and unusual things you couldn’t necessarily find anywhere else … And their slogan was, you know, ‘keep commerce human.’ I think a lot of sellers are increasingly asking whether the platform still lives up to that.” On Oct. 22, Etsy announced an updated AI policy requiring sellers to include at least one unedited photo of the item being sold. They also said bot-generated listings without human involvement would be removed. “We’re investing in tools to better identify authentic versus misleading images and detect and remove listings that use AI to create fraudulent inventory,” the update said. Elisabeth, a clairvoyant and witch, said Etsy was instrumental in helping her develop her business. She operates a website and Etsy business under that name, and like James, asked that her legal name be withheld due to concerns about repercussions in her personal and professional life. She still has an Etsy storefront but currently conducts most of her sales for readings and spell castings through her Elisabeth’s Room website. “AI content diluted search results but it also triggered a major flight to quality,” said Elisabeth, who, like James and Mason, said demand for her services remains high. “There’s been a massive surge in people seeking a real practitioner, a human that can form an energetic connection within the sea of AI rubbish.” That “rubbish,” she said, can be identified by looking for high-volume, low-priced spells for under $10. featured.content: Get RNS’ thoughtful, essential religion reporting every morning. Sign up for free! (RNS) — A conservative Christian blogger and podcaster who once wrote, “If you love America, you should support ICE,” has been removed from the U.S. and is now in Canada, his family said Friday (Oct. 30),  nine days after immigration agents arrested him at an Ohio airport. Samuel Sey, whose “Slow to Write” blog is popular with Reformed evangelical Christians, was arrested by ICE at the Columbus International Airport. Supporters  and his family initially believed a clerical error had led to his detention. “We sincerely believed we were following the legal process, which we continue to respect,” Sey’s wife, Annie, posted on X. “Sadly, Samuel was removed from the U.S. and is in Canada as of today,” October 30. RELATED: DHS says Christian blogger Samuel Sey, arrested by ICE, will be deported Earlier this week, a Department of Homeland Security spokesperson said that Sey, who lived in Ohio with his family, had overstayed his visa after entering the country in 2022. “Sey has no pending applications and accepted voluntary departure. He will remain in ICE custody until removed from the United States,” the spokesperson told RNS in an email on Oct. 25. In an email on Sunday (Nov. 1) DHS said that Sey had departed the country voluntarily. Originally from Ghana, Sey grew up in Canada after his family immigrated there. After moving to the U.S. to get married, he had been working on obtaining long-term legal status, according to statements from his family and supporters. Sey’s arrest made headlines, in part because of his past support for Trump administration immigration policies, including writing that Christian ethics demand deportations. “If you love America you should support ICE,” he wrote on X in January. A series of well-known conservative influencers, including Allie Beth Stuckey , Megan Basham , and Joel Berry ,  also have all posted support for Sey on social media after news of his arrest became public. He is best known for writing about theology and for his conservative social views on abortion, along with his criticism of DEI initiatives and COVID-19 vaccine mandates.  More recently, he had feuded with a group of Christian influencers who promote openly antisemitic and white supremacist views online. Such views, Sey told RNS, were unchristian. Sey did not immediately responded to a text requesting comment. A crowdfunding campaign for Sey and his family has raised more than $35,000. In her social media post, Annie Sey thanks supporters for their prayers and assistance following her husband’s arrest.  “Although this has been devastating to our family and the outcome is not what we had hoped, we will trust God’s sovereign plan and work to reunite our family.” ( This story has been updated with a DHS statement that Sey’s departure was voluntary.)
