featured.content: Get RNS’ thoughtful, essential religion reporting every morning. Sign up for free! (RNS) — Pope Leo XIV has done his civic duty: He has voted from Rome in the U.S. midterm election, the Vatican announced, marking another first for the American pope. “Pope Leo XIV has exercised his right to vote as a United States citizen, whenever he was eligible to do so,” reads the Friday (Oct. 30) announcement about the Chicago native. “The Holy See Press Office confirms that in keeping with this longstanding practice of civic participation, he has submitted his mail-in ballot in Chicago.” The Holy See Press Office noted that when Leo lived in Peru, he also voted whenever he was eligible to mark a ballot. “The Holy Father expresses his belief in the right and the duty of citizens to participate in the democratic processes,” it added. The action by the leader of the world’s Catholics was announced two and a half weeks after Leo underwent successful surgery for lung cancer. He was released from a Rome hospital on Oct. 17. In a “Vote By Mail Report” of the county clerk’s office in Will County, Illinois, the name “Prevost, Robert F” is listed just below his brother’s (“Prevost, John J”) at an address in the southwest Chicago suburb of New Lenox, Illinois. RELATED: Is an American pope still a US citizen? Leo is described in Illinois records as “undeclared” for a political party. During the 2024 and 2020 general elections, in which he also voted absentee, he had the same affiliation, according to documents provided to Religion News Service. When Leo voted in the general elections of 2018, 2014 and 2012, his affiliation also was listed as “undeclared.” But in the primary elections of 2016, 2014 and 2012, his affiliation was listed as Republican. For the elections listed from 2012 through 2018, he often voted early and at the voting location of the Village of New Lenox. CBS News reported that Leo voted in the Democratic primary most recently in 2010. Illinois voters do not need to register with a political party to vote in a primary. As is the case for other Illinois voters, Leo’s ballot included candidates for U.S. Senate and House and gubernatorial contests. Based on the listing on Ballotpedia, Leo also had the opportunity to vote for an East Joliet Sanitary District Trustee Board at-large seat as well as for candidates for county clerk, sheriff and treasurer, and as many as 16 county board members. Christian Maxwell, the GOP candidate in Illinois’ 1st District, told RNS in a statement that she appreciated the pontiff’s execution of his duty. “I think it’s wonderful to see the Pope exercising his right to vote,’’ said Maxwell, who is running against incumbent Jonathan Jackson, son of the late Rev. Jesse Jackson. “And I’ll admit, there’s something exciting about knowing that his ballot could have included my name in this election.” Added Maxwell: “Of course, his vote is private, and I would never presume to know whom he supported. But it’s a fascinating reminder that every voter, regardless of their position or prominence, has a voice in our democracy.” Jackson also voiced his admiration for Leo in taking the time to vote. “I’m deeply grateful to him for that, and for the example it sets for every voter in our district,” Jackson said. “How he voted is his own, as it is for every voter, but I can say with real admiration and humility that I’m honored to count him as a constituent. The South Side and the south suburbs have always produced people of faith and purpose, and it fills me with pride that the first American pope still calls the 1st District home.” Chieko Noguchi, executive director of public affairs for the U.S. Conference of Catholic Bishops, described Leo as a role model for others during the election season. “In voting, our Holy Father sets the example that encourages each citizen to exercise their civic responsibility,” Noguchi said in a statement. “The U.S. bishops have emphasized that (it) is not “who” one is voting for, but rather on encouraging Catholics to inform their conscience as they prepare to vote and to uphold human dignity and the common good in doing so.” Steven P. Millies, professor of public theology at Catholic Theological Union in Chicago, said Leo’s action demonstrates a sense of “duty” born out of Catholic social teaching. “As has always been the case, the binary choices in U.S. politics do not correspond well at all to Catholic social teaching,” Millies, chairman of The Bernardin Center at CTU, told RNS via email. “I think Leo would agree, for Catholics, the choice is between bad and slightly less bad. But the choice is one we can make.” The Rev. Mark Francis, Leo’s former classmate and longtime friend, did hazard a guess as to Leo’s ballot choices, although he noted he had no firsthand information. “I really would not have much to tell you about the Pope’s politics, since I have not spoke(n) with him about this since we were Superiors General together in Rome in the 2000s,” Francis told RNS via email. “I think you can infer from his constant reiteration of Catholic Social teaching that he would not be voting straight Republican.” This story has been corrected to change the pronoun referring to Christian Maxwell from he to she. featured.content: Get RNS’ thoughtful, essential religion reporting every morning. Sign up for free! (RNS) — Think of some of the most iconic scenes in classics of the horror genre — priests gathered around a rotting, spitting child in “The Exorcist”; the chanting of the neighborhood coven in “Rosemary’s Baby”; the priest warning Damien’s father in “The Omen.” Notice a theme? Horror villains and monsters show up in all shapes and sizes, but when religion shows up, it is usually Catholicism. In Hollywood, it’s the faith often featured for its mysterious conclaves and Gothic churches, depicting the white clerical collar up against the ultimate prince of darkness. “When a vampire is at your door or your child is possessed, you don’t call for a Methodist,” said Matthew J. Cressler, the co-author of the new book “ Body and Blood: Catholic Horror in America ,” along with Jack Lee Downey, Kathleen Holscher and Michael Pasquier. “God love the Unitarians, but you don’t ask for your Unitarian minister. You grab your rosary beads, your St. Christopher medal, your holy water, your priest.” Cressler said that beyond the dripping candles and ominous devotional music, Catholicism also has theological themes that work with the genre. “Catholics have long had a sense that when one suffers, one is bearing the cross of Christ. And that in suffering, one is drawn closer to Christ,” he said. Aislinn Clarke said having an Irish Catholic childhood was the perfect preparation to become a horror film director. She wrote and directed the 2024 horror movie “Fréwaka.” “I  remember reading a book about the lives of the saints, which my parents probably thought was a very wholesome thing for a child to read,” remembers Clarke. “But there was a lot of stuff about, like, St. Lucia plucked out her eyeballs, and another saint cut off her breasts. And everybody’s wearing hair shirts and thorns and flagellating.” RELATED: Chicago Catholics suing Trump administration bring migrant detainees’ stories to Pope Leo Clarke said the Mass itself has elements of what we might now call body horror. “The priest holds up a cup and says, ‘This is the blood of Christ, this is the body of Christ,’ and we’re invited to drink the body and blood of Christ,” she said. “Which, as a child who was really interested in horror, I was thinking, this is a bit cannibal-ish.” Of course, horror movies take these ideas and ratchet them up to 11, Cressler said. He argued that Catholic themes, like venerating the remains of the beloved dead, can show up in movies that are not even overtly Catholic. For example, keeping the mummified corpse of your mother in the basement of the house next to your roadside motel, as Norman Bates does in “Psycho.” Beyond the fictionalized depictions, it is a faith that can take spiritual warfare fairly literally. The Rev. Aaron Williams, a pastor at the Basilica of Saint Mary in Natchez, Mississippi, consulted on the 2025 horror film “The Ritual.” Williams said that while most people are far more likely to fall into sin through temptation rather than possession, “we do come in contact with the occult and the enemy and his minions, the demons.” Though the average Catholic may not hold these views, the church still performs the rite of exorcism. And the Catholic Church positions its clergy to deal with ultimate evil by imbuing them with ultimate good. “A priest … through ordination, he’s sacramentally received a character that allows him to act with the authority of Christ,” Williams said. Some films use that heightened authority to save characters from the demonic. And some use horror to point out broken elements in the church itself. Clarke discussed a scene from her 2018 film, “The Devil’s Doorway,” in which nuns sing hymns to Christ and perform a brutal symphysiotomy procedure while ignoring the suffering of the young woman giving birth in front of them. It was a nod to the confinement of women in Magdalene laundries, asylums run by Protestants and Catholics between the 18th and 20th centuries. “There are things flying around, and crosses going upside down, and we have some stuff like that,” Clarke said. “But the most horrific scene in the movie from the script stage for me was always going to be this birth sequence.” Catholic symbols and songs show up in horror so much so that Cressler said it can influence how we see the church itself. “If you walk into a room that’s got too many candles and too many crosses and too many statues, you know you’re in trouble,” he said. But Cressler said that also goes for the tropes of Catholic grace and redemption, as horror brings monsters out into the open — whether they’re coming from inside or outside of the house. The movies help us see and defeat them, at least until they’re resurrected for the sequel. RELATED: ‘Witches’ epithet hurled at abortion proponents has roots in Appalachian history

The Rev. Aaron Williams是密西西比州纳特切斯圣玛丽主教座堂的牧师,曾就2025年的恐怖电影“礼仪”进行磋商。 威廉姆斯说,虽然大多数人更有可能通过诱惑而不是占有而陷入罪恶之中,但“我们确实与神秘和敌人及其走狗——恶魔相接。” 虽然一般的天主教徒可能不持有这些观点,但教堂仍然进行驱魔仪式. 天主教会通过向神职人员灌输终极利益 来对付终极邪恶 威廉姆斯说,“一位牧师...通过授职,他圣洁地接受了一个使他能够以基督的权威行事的性格。” 一些电影利用这种增强权威,从恶魔中拯救出角色. 有人用恐怖来指出教堂内部的破碎元素. 克拉克讨论了出自她2018年电影"恶魔之门"(The Devil's Doorway)的一幕,其中修女向基督唱出赞美歌并进行残酷的对称切除手术,而忽略了当着她们面前分娩的年轻女性所承受的痛苦. 这是18世纪到20世纪在马格达莱纳洗衣店,由新教徒和天主教徒经营的庇护地中妇女被禁闭的点头. 克拉克说,“有些东西飞来飞去,交叉颠倒,我们有一些类似的东西。” “但从剧本舞台上看,电影中最恐怖的一幕对我来说永远是这种出生顺序。” 天主教的象征和歌曲如此恐怖地出现,以至于克雷斯勒说它可以影响我们如何看待教堂本身. “如果你走进一个有太多蜡烛、太多十字架和太多雕像的房间, Cressler说, 天主教的恩惠和救赎也一样, 因为恐怖会把怪物带入空地, 电影帮助我们看和打败他们, 相关内容: " Witches " 的口号,

featured.content: Get RNS’ thoughtful, essential religion reporting every morning. Sign up for free! FRANKLIN, Tennessee (RNS) — After a four-year stint in Hungary, conservative writer Rod Dreher has returned to the American South and is taking on the “hard right” just as he has sought to do with “wokeness” on the left, he said. Famous for his 2017 book, “The Benedict Option,” and his friendship with Vice President JD Vance, Dreher — a former Catholic turned Eastern Orthodox convert — has been a voice for traditional Christian values as a counterweight to the progressive left. He has supported President Donald Trump and former Hungarian Prime Minister Viktor Orbán, who lost a high-stakes election in April amid criticisms of corruption and his authoritarian style of governance. Dreher hasn’t utterly disavowed Trump or Orbán, though he’s far more critical of them than he has been in the past. Nevertheless, his fiercer criticisms lately are against self-avowed Christian nationalists and Nick Fuentes, a white nationalist with a large online following of fans known as Groypers. Fuentes and Groypers are well-known for antisemitic conspiracy theories and Nazi apologetics. “There is a temptation, and it’s going to increase after the midterms, for the current institutional leaders and political leaders on the right to think that they can harness the enthusiasm of these firebrands and that it can work for normie politics,” Dreher told RNS in an interview in Franklin, Tennessee, a week before the midterm elections. The midterms could be a test of just how much influence these camps will exert on conservative political and religious circles as the Republican Party looks toward a post-Trump future. RELATED: Nick Fuentes and the Groyper challenge to Catholicism Dreher isn’t the only high-profile conservative voicing these concerns. In September, conservative pundit Erick Erickson went on the offensive against certain self-avowed Christian nationalists and their allies for what he characterized as an attempt to poison the GOP and evangelical church with white nationalist and antidemocratic ideology. His denunciations, both in a widely read Substack post and on his nationally syndicated radio show, which he hosts from an Atlanta studio, earned praise from fellow conservatives and sparked backlash. “They want to speak very loudly to vilify those of us who call them out so that they can further take over the conservative movement,” Erickson told RNS. “So, all I can do is stand on my convictions and let the people judge where the convictions are.” Erickson has sustained this criticism, most recently by saying he didn’t know if he could vote for Georgia Republican Senate candidate Mike Collins, who has come under fire for campaign staffers who have expressed antisemitic and racist views. The debate about Groypers’ status in the Republican Party erupted after Fuentes appeared on Tucker Carlson’s podcast in October 2025. A rift in conservative circles opened , with the Heritage Foundation — a leading conservative think tank, which had an advertising contract with Carlson at the time — and Vance facing demands to unequivocally denounce Groypers. But Vance has faced criticism for dancing around the issue, including from Dreher, whom the vice president has credited with jumpstarting his political ascent. Dreher’s criticisms against Groypers and Christian nationalists have come as he prepares to publish his next book, “Weimar America: A Warning for a Decadent Democracy,” in the spring. It compares the infant Nazi Party in 1920s Germany to 2020s America. And in December, Dreher will speak on a panel on Christian nationalism in a Greek Orthodox cathedral in Birmingham, Alabama. “The problem is when you go from appreciating and cherishing your local or national expression of Christianity into sacralizing the nation or race,” Dreher said, adding Christian nationalism is a “heresy” in Orthodoxy. New York Times opinion columnist David French, who’s likewise a conservative but a longtime vocal critic of Trump, hopes voices like Dreher and Erickson can reach audiences that are “catering to the Groypers.” “They’re aiming more at your donor class, educated Republicans who have completely turned a blind eye to the rot in the GOP and the rot in GOP institutions. So, they’re reaching for persuadable people,” French told RNS. But as French sees it, someone like Dreher is part of the problem. He said some of Dreher’s attacks against the left created the discursive conditions Groypers have seized upon. “He cultivated this existential angst about the left that that level of alarmism has made people ready, willing and able to at least tolerate Groyperism or, in some circumstances, receive it gladly,” French said. Where French, Dreher and Erickson are all aligned is in their concern about far-right infiltration within the church, where they see it as a graver danger than in politics. “Politics trickles down from culture. If it starts infesting churches and if churches don’t have immunity to it, it’s going to spread further into politics,” Erickson said. In his own denomination, the Presbyterian Church in America (PCA), an influential conservative Reformed evangelical denomination, Erickson said there have been promising developments. For example, in June, the PCA advanced an ad hoc committee’s report on Christian nationalism , which denounced ideologies that promote racial and ethnic superiority. Meanwhile, Erickson said he has received notes of appreciation from pastors, marriage counselors and seminary professors for publicly condemning Groyperism and Christian nationalism. “They’re the people on the frontlines of this who are going to have to deal with it, not me,” he said. For Dreher, he acknowledged his time in Hungary and past association with Orbán, who faced criticism for pushing Christian nationalist policies and ideas, may be a liability as he now aspires to be an authority on condemning Christian nationalism in the U.S. But French said that may be an asset. “Here, you have a guy who moved to Hungary because he supported Orbán so much,” French said. “Nobody can sit there and say Rod Dreher is a squish about the left.” RELATED: Orbán’s defeat is a defeat for Christian nationalism challenge to Catholicism

FRANKLIN,田纳西州(RNS)——在匈牙利度过了四年之后,保守派作家罗德·德雷尔(Rod Dreher)回到了美洲南方,正像他试图用左边的"醒来"来做的那样,正在采取"硬右". 以他2017年的著作"本笃选择"而出名,并和副总统JD Vance,德雷赫(Dreher)的友谊——前天主教转而信奉东方正教的皈依者——作为进步左翼的制衡者,一直为传统的基督教价值观出声. 他一直支持唐纳德·特朗普总统和前匈牙利总理维克多·奥尔班,他在4月的一次高调选举中,在对腐败的批评和他专制的治理风格中落败. Dreher并没有完全否认特朗普或奥尔班, 不过,他最近更激烈地批评自封的基督教民族主义者和尼克·富恩特斯,他是一位白人民族主义者,在网络上大量追随被称为"Groypers"的粉丝. Fuentes和Groypers都是以抗菌阴谋论和纳粹论著称. 在中期选举前一周, 德雷赫尔在田纳西州富兰克林接受采访时告诉RNS, 当共和党展望后特朗普未来时, 中期计划可能只是测试这些阵营会给保守的政治和宗教圈子带来多大影响。 相关:尼克·富恩特斯(Nick Fuentes)和格鲁佩尔(Groyper)挑战天主教, 9月,保守派知识分子埃里克·埃里克森(英语:Erick Erickson)针对某些自封的基督教民族主义者及其盟友发动了攻势,因为他称其企图用白色民族主义和反民主思想毒害GOP和福音会. 他的谴责,无论是在被广泛阅读的"Substack"一篇文章中,还是在他从亚特兰大工作室主持的全国辛迪加广播节目上,都赢得了同党保守派的赞誉并引发了反弹. Erickson对RNS说, “他们想大声说话来诋毁我们这些叫他们出来的人, “所以,我所能做的就是坚持我的信念,让人民判断这些信念在哪里。” Erickson支持这种批评, 最近的一次是说他不知道他能否投票支持乔治亚州共和党参议院候选人Mike Collins, 在2025年10月富恩特斯出现在塔克·卡尔森的播客上后,关于格罗珀斯在共和党的地位的争论爆发. 保守圈子的一分裂痕开启了,传统基金会——一个主要的保守智囊团,当时它与卡尔森签有广告合同——而万斯则面临明确谴责格罗珀斯的要求. 包括来自德雷赫尔的批评, 副总统称赞他的政治崛起。 德雷赫对格鲁珀斯和基督教民族主义者的批评在他准备在春季出版下一本书“魏玛美国:一个十年之久的民主的警告”时就来了。 它比较了1920年代新生的纳粹党德国和2020年的美国. 而在12月,德雷赫尔将在阿拉巴马州伯明翰的希腊正教大教堂的基督教民族主义面板上演讲. “问题是,当你从欣赏和珍视基督教的地方或民族表现转变为亵渎国家或种族时,”德雷赫尔说,加上基督教民族主义是东正教的“异教徒”。 纽约时报的舆论专栏作家 David French — — 他同样是保守派,但长期是特朗普的声乐评论家 — — 希望像德雷赫和埃里克森这样的声音能够传到“对格鲁伊珀斯人”的观众。 “他们更多针对你的捐献阶级, 受过教育的共和党人, 因此,他们正在帮助那些有说服力的人。 但正如法国人所见,像德雷赫这样的人就是问题的一部分. 他表示德雷赫对左翼的一些攻击造成了格洛伊珀斯所抓住的扭曲条件. 法国人说,“他制造了这种生存主义的愤怒,因为左侧的这种惊恐情绪使人们准备、愿意并能够至少容忍格鲁伊佩尔主义,或在某些情况下欣然接受格鲁伊佩尔主义。” 法国人,德雷赫尔人和埃里克森人都结盟的地方,是因为他们担心教会内部极右渗透,他们视其为比从政更严重的危险. “政治从文化中消失。 如果它开始侵袭教堂, 如果教堂对此没有豁免权, 在他自己的教派中,美国长老会(PCA),一个有影响力的保守派改革派福音教派,埃里克森说,已经出现了一些有希望的发展. 例如,6月,常设仲裁法院提出了一份关于基督教民族主义的特设委员会报告,该报告谴责了宣扬种族和族裔优越性的意识形态。 同时,埃里克森说,他收到了牧师,婚姻顾问和神学院教授的感谢信,他们公开谴责了格罗佩尔主义和基督教民族主义. 他表示:「他们是前线民众, 对德雷赫尔来说,他承认自己在匈牙利的时间和过去与奥尔班的联系,奥尔班因为推动基督教民族主义政策和思想而面临批评,现在他渴望成为谴责美国基督教民族主义的权威,但法国人说这可能是资产。 “这里,有一个家伙因为支持奥尔班这么多而搬到了匈牙利。” 没有人可以坐在那里说罗德·德雷赫是左撇子。 相关:奥尔班的失败是基督教民族主义挑战天主教的失败

featured.summary: VATICAN CITY (RNS) — Villanova and Notre Dame bring basketball, school pride and a friendly contest for Pope Leo XIV’s loyalties to Rome, exploring what faith brings to competition, teamwork and defeat.

featured.content: Get RNS’ thoughtful, essential religion reporting every morning. Sign up for free! VATICAN CITY (RNS) — Notre Dame and Villanova will face off this weekend to open the men’s and women’s college basketball seasons in Rome under the first U.S.-born pope, bringing a distinctly American combination of sports and Catholic pride to the Eternal City. Pope Leo XIV graduated from Villanova in 1977 and shares its Augustinian identity, but he was born in Chicago, not far from the Notre Dame campus in South Bend, Indiana. The pope has avoided taking sides in the upcoming games, but he told journalists on the plane to France in September that he had heard that more people from Villanova were coming to see the match. “The voice of the people of God will be very strong on the Villanova side,” he said. The unprecedented event will showcase the rivalry between the two Catholic universities on and off the court, as both expand their visibility and deepen their Vatican connections under Leo. “Pope Leo is going to be very interested in the game,” Ed Hastings, a Villanova theology professor and former basketball player, told RNS. “I’m sure he’s not going to say who he’s hoping to win,” he added. “But we know it’s Villanova.” The “Eternal City Tip-Off” will pit the schools’ men’s and women’s teams against each other in a doubleheader Sunday (Nov. 1) at the Palazzo dello Sport in Rome, with the men’s game set for 9:30 a.m. ET and the women to follow at noon. It’s unlikely that the pope, who recently recovered from surgery to treat cancer in his right lung, will personally attend the games, which organizers say will draw more than 7,000 people. But Leo will have a private meeting with the teams and their families at the Paul VI Hall at the Vatican on Saturday (Oct. 31), preceded by a private Mass in St. Peter’s Basilica celebrated by Archbishop Nelson J. Pérez of Philadelphia, home to Villanova. The pregame party at Rome’s Spazio Novecento, promising food, drinks and university “spirit groups,” is sold out, while other events and student gatherings will enliven the city in the days leading up to the games. Fans will cheer from across the Atlantic at campus viewing parties and alumni watch events worldwide. For the athletes, the prospect of encountering the pope and being at the Vatican provides elevated enthusiasm for the season opener. Villanova guard Kelsey Joens said she passes by a large poster of the pope every day when she walks to class, a reminder that someone who once studied at the university is now the leader of 1.4 billion Catholics around the globe. “Just having the pope from your school,” she told RNS, “it just brings … a different vibe around it.” A Catholic raised in the Midwest, Notre Dame guard Ethan Roberts said during a press conference on Oct. 22 that he drew strength from the prospect of playing in Rome. “My confirmation saint was St. Peter, so St. Peter’s Basilica is going to be sweet for me to see,” he said. Catholic universities have long occupied an outsize place in basketball culture. Holy Cross, La Salle, San Francisco, Loyola Chicago, Marquette, Georgetown and Villanova have all won men’s NCAA championships. Villanova, despite being the smaller university, is no basketball underdog by pedigree, having won the men’s championship in 1985, 2016 and 2018. Three members of its 2016 NCAA championship squad — Jalen Brunson, Josh Hart and Mikal Bridges — are teammates on the New York Knicks, the reigning NBA champions. This season’s Wildcats include promising freshman center Luigi Suigo, touted as a potential NBA lottery pick, who will make his Villanova debut in his home country. With the Notre Dame men’s team rebuilding after losing three of its leading scorers, it’s the Fighting Irish women’s team that will likely be the main attraction on Sunday. Guard Hannah Hidalgo is considered a top WNBA prospect after a record-breaking 202 steals last season. The women’s basketball game will mark the first time the two teams have met since 2018. Beyond the basketball court, the universities bring different connections to the papal court, where both schools have drawn visibility following the election of the U.S.-born pontiff. Villanova shares a personal connection to Leo, with its theologians and campus ministers describing a pope who is close to Pennsylvania. “It’s just a really unique thing we get to enjoy here in Villanova, how much closer Vatican City is,” said David Walsh, Villanova’s campus minister for sports and spirituality. But Notre Dame can claim an extensive institutional relationship with the Holy See. Leo has appointed two Notre Dame faculty members and a university trustee as consultors to the Vatican Dicastery for Integral Human Development and recently named theologian Khaled Anatolios to the International Theological Commission. “I’d like to say that the competition level might be friendly, but I don’t necessarily think that’s going to be true,” Hastings said. Joens confirmed this sentiment, saying that playing against another Catholic university would fire up her competitiveness. RELATED: Chicago Catholics suing Trump administration bring migrant detainees’ stories to Pope Leo Popes being drawn into sporting rivalries is nothing new. Leo X cheered from the sidelines as he watched his hometown calcio Fiorentino, a violent Renaissance ballgame, play in the Vatican’s Belvedere Courtyard in 1521. Saint John Paul II became an honorary member of German rivals Schalke and Borussia Dortmund, and Francis joked about divided loyalties before an Italy-Argentina soccer match in 2013. Leo himself had barely been elected when Chicago baseball reached the Vatican: After his brother confirmed his White Sox allegiance, the American League Wild Card playoff team proclaimed, “HEY CHICAGO, HE’S A SOX FAN!” Walsh said that the universities’ shared faith shapes how their athletes approach each other on the court. He said both Catholic and Augustinian spirituality encourage students to see their opponents “not as an enemy, but as someone who’s pushing them to raise their level.” He described the deeper purpose of sports as the connections players discover with teammates, but also with God. Leo, who plays sports and leads an active lifestyle, offered a similar sentiment in his February letter on sports, “Life in Abundance,” which described teamwork as a way of moving beyond one’s self-interest and toward a common goal. “Sporting competitions can also play an important role in fostering unity among people,” the pope wrote, adding that they provide an opportunity for teams to “strive together for excellence.” “In the time before or after the competition, there is usually an opportunity to meet and get to know one another,” Leo wrote. RELATED: AI and religion: A modest proposal

VVICAN CITY(RNS)——圣母和比利亚诺瓦本周末将面对罗马的男女大学生篮球赛季在第一个美国出生的教宗下开幕,为永恒之城带来了明显的美国体育和天主教自豪的组合. 教宗利奥十四于1977年从比利亚诺瓦毕业并分享其奥古斯丁式身份,但他生于芝加哥,距离印第安纳州南本德的圣母会校园不远. 教皇避免了在即将到来的比赛中站在一边,但他在9月告诉飞往法国的飞机上的记者,他听说比利亚诺瓦有更多的人前来观看比赛. 他说,“在维拉诺瓦一方,上帝人民的声音将非常强烈。” 这场史无前例的事件将展现两所天主教大学在朝廷内外的竞争,因为两者都扩大了他们的能见度并加深了他们在利奥领导下的梵蒂冈联系. “Pope Leo将会对比赛非常感兴趣”,维拉诺瓦神学教授、前篮球运动员Ed Hastings告诉RNS。 “我肯定他不会说希望谁赢, “但我们知道这是维拉诺瓦。” " 永恒之城"(Eternal City Tip-Off)将让学校男女队在双头人星期天(Nov. 1)于罗马的Palazzo dello体育会相会,男子比赛定于上午9:30进行,女子比赛定于中午进行。 最近从治疗右肺癌症的手术中康复的教皇不太可能亲自参加比赛, 但利奥将于星期六在梵蒂冈的保罗六世会堂(英语:Paul VI Hall (Oct. 31))与球队及其家属举行私人会面,之前在圣彼得巴西利卡举行由费城大主教纳尔逊·J·佩雷斯(英语:Nelson J. 罗马Spazio Novecento的预赛会、有希望的食物、饮料和大学“精神团体”都卖光了,而其他活动和学生聚会将在比赛前几天让城市充满活力。 粉丝会在校园观看会和校友观看全球活动时,从大西洋两岸欢呼. 对运动员来说,与教皇相遇并身处梵蒂冈的前景为开赛季的选手提供了更高的热情. 维拉诺瓦卫士凯尔西·约恩斯(Kelsey Joens)说她每天去上课时都会经过一幅大宗教宗的海报,这提醒了曾经在大学学习过的人现在是全球14亿天主教徒的领袖. 她对RNS说, “这只是给大家带来不同的氛围。 一位在中西部长大的天主教徒,圣母院警卫伊森·罗伯茨(Ethan Roberts)在10月22日的记者招待会上说,他从罗马的玩法前景中汲取了力量. “我的确认圣人是圣彼得, 天主教大学长期以来在篮球文化中占据了超大的地位. 圣克罗斯,拉萨勒,旧金山,洛约拉·芝加哥,马克特,乔治敦和比利亚诺瓦都获得了男子NCAA的冠军. 维拉诺瓦虽然是规模较小的大学,但并非被幼稚园所低估的篮球,曾于1985年,2016年和2018年获得男子团体冠军. 其2016年NCAA锦标赛的三名队员——贾伦·布伦森,乔什·哈特和米卡尔·布里奇斯——是纽约尼克斯队的队友,主力NBA冠军. 这个赛季的"野猫"(Wildcats)包括有前途的新生中心路易吉·苏伊戈(Luigi Suigo),被誉为潜在的NBA彩票选手,他将让自己的维拉诺瓦在家乡出道. 在圣母院男队失去3名主打分数后重建, 后卫汉娜·伊达尔戈被认为是WNBA在上个赛季破纪录的202起偷盗后获得的最高前景. 女子篮球比赛将标志着自2018年以来两队首次相会. 在篮球场外,各所大学给教宗法庭带来了不同的联系,在美国出生的庞蒂夫入选后,两所学校都吸引了知名度. 比利亚诺瓦分享了与利奥的个人联系,其神学家和校园部长描述了一位与宾夕法尼亚州相近的教宗. 维莱诺瓦的校园体育与精神部长David Walsh说, 但圣母院可以宣称与教廷有着广泛的机构关系. 利奥任命了两名圣母院教职员工和一名大学受托人,作为梵蒂冈综合人文发展饮食社的顾问,最近还任命神学家Khaled Anatolios为国际神学委员会顾问。 ”黑斯廷斯说, 乔恩斯证实了这种情绪,说玩弄另一所天主教大学会激起她的竞争力. 相关:芝加哥天主教徒起诉特朗普政府将移民被拘留者的故事带给教宗利奥·波普斯(Leo Popes), Leo X在观看家乡卡尔西奥·菲奥伦蒂诺(Calcio Fiorentino), 圣约翰-保罗二世成为了德国对手沙尔克和博鲁西亚·多特蒙德的荣誉成员,弗朗西斯在2013年意大利-阿根廷足球比赛前开玩笑说分出忠心. 当芝加哥棒球到达梵蒂冈时, 里奥本人几乎没有当选: 在他的兄弟确认对白袜的效忠后, 美国联盟野牌季后赛小组宣布, “HEY CHICAGO, HE's A SOX FAN!” Walsh说,大学的共同信仰决定了他们的运动员如何在法庭上相互接近。 他表示天主教和奥古斯丁精神都鼓励学生将对手视为“不是敌人,而是推动他们提高水平的人 ” 。 他将体育的更深层目的描述为球员发现与队友的联系,但也与神相通. 李奥在二月的信中提出了类似的情感,即“富足的生活 ” ( Life in Aboutance ) , 将团队合作描述为超越自我利益,实现共同目标的一种方式。 教皇写道, “体育比赛也可以在促进人们团结方面发挥重要作用 ” , 并补充说, 体育比赛为团队提供了一个“为卓越而努力”的机会。 Leo写道:“在比赛之前或之后,通常有机会见面和相互了解。” 相关:大赦国际和宗教:略微的建议

featured.summary: (RNS) — There was one thing that Houdini never tried to escape. And that was his Jewish identity.

featured.title_zh: 在他去世一百年后，胡迪尼仍然很重要
featured.content: Get RNS’ thoughtful, essential religion reporting every morning. Sign up for free! (RNS) — Tomorrow, on Halloween, magicians and ghost hunters around the world will mark Harry Houdini’s 100th yahrzeit. Yes — yahrzeit. Harry Houdini was Jewish. Why should that matter? Because his father was my colleague. The story begins with Rabbi Mayer Samuel Weiss (or Weisz). In 1878, Rabbi Weiss arrived from Budapest and took a post as Appleton, Wisconsin’s first rabbi . The rabbi helped plan the congregation’s new temple , but he never got to preach in it. Within a few years the congregation let him go. Houdini later explained that his father lost the pulpit because he spoke little English and never fit into American life . Others say that the German members wanted a German rabbi of their own , and to have a Hungarian rabbi was simply de classe. It is a classic story — the rabbi who smells too much of the old country, too traditional, “too Jewish,” and the congregation shows him the door. This plunged his family into poverty. So, a rabbi who could not escape the shackles of his past became the father of a man who turned escaping real shackles into an art form and a career, and became one of the first Jewish Americans to achieve worldwide celebrity. That’s Houdini as Jewish metaphor. And it continued. The boy reinvented himself, again and again. Erik became Ehrich, then “Erik the Great,” and finally Harry Houdini, a name he borrowed from the French conjurer Robert-Houdin . Jewish reinvention: It’s a thing. Remember how young Bobby Zimmerman became Bob Dylan. But no matter how tight the ropes and chains Houdini would encounter, his Jewish identity was never among them. In July 1918 he gathered some 20 performers, every one of them the son of a rabbi, into the Rabbis’ Sons Theatrical Benevolent Association to raise money for the Red Cross and other war charities. They elected Houdini president, Al Jolson vice president and Irving Berlin secretary. “It is surprising how many sons of Jewish clergymen there are on the stage,” Houdini told The New York Times. He married Bess Rahner, a Catholic, but he never repudiated his origins. When his mother died, he reportedly recited Kaddish for her every night for a year . When he died, his family buried him in Machpelah Cemetery in Queens, near his parents, with his head resting on his mother’s letters . Rabbi Bernard Drachman delivered a tribute. Every night, Houdini let strangers handcuff him, chain him, nail him into crates and lower him into water, and every night he escaped. RELATED: Halloween and a declining Christian tradition coexist on All Saints’ Day in Spain The Hebrew name for Egypt, Mitzrayim , carries within it the word meitzarim , the narrow straits. Each straitjacket act was a mini-Exodus. Except, unlike the ancient Israelites, Houdini chose, and welcomed, his bondage. Then, there was his body. Houdini was ripped. The ripped body is part of the Jewish story, though you would not know it; the traditional image of the Jewish man was stooped and frail. At the Second Zionist Congress in Basel in 1898, Max Nordau basically said “screw that,” and he called for “muscle Judaism.” In the words of Hans and Franz, Nordau wanted to pump Jews up. Within two months, Berlin students had founded a Jewish gymnastics club . That is also the origins of the Maccabiah games. Houdini did not need a Zionist ideologue to tell him that. He turned himself into the most physically commanding man in vaudeville, sporting a body that audiences on two continents paid to watch strain against steel. He was the personification of Nordau’s dream. Michael Chabon understood all of this. Houdini never walks onstage in “The Amazing Adventures of Kavalier & Clay,” but he presides over the entire novel. Joe Kavalier, a Jewish teenager in Prague, studies escape artistry with an old illusionist named Bernard Kornblum, and he gets out of Nazi-occupied Prague by hiding in the coffin that carries the golem to safety. In Brooklyn, Joe and his cousin Sammy invent a superhero called the Escapist. Chabon writes that Houdini was a hero to “little men, city boys and Jews,” and Sammy is all three. In Chabon’s hands, the escape artist becomes the emblem of 20-century Jewish survival. The heartbreak of the novel lies in the escapes that fail. Joe gets out. The family he leaves behind does not. Which brings us back to Halloween. Before he died, Houdini and Bess agreed on a code. If the dead could speak, he would send her two words, “Rosabelle, believe.” Rosabelle was the song Bess sang in her act when they met . For 10 years Bess held a séance every Halloween. In 1936, on the roof of the Knickerbocker Hotel in Hollywood, she held the last one, announced that Houdini had not come through , and put out the candle she had kept burning. His fans have kept the Halloween séances going ever since . He has yet to show up. The Torah would not have been surprised. Deuteronomy forbids the one who “doresh el ha-metim,” who inquires of the dead. King Saul broke that law. Abandoned by God and terrified of the Philistines, he found a woman at Endor who could bring up the prophet Samuel. Samuel came up angry, demanded to know why Saul had disturbed him and told the king that he and his sons would join him the next day. Houdini spent his last years exposing the mediums who preyed on grieving families, and his own grief set him on that path. At a séance conducted by the wife of Arthur Conan Doyle, a “message” from his late mother arrived in fluent English, with a cross drawn at the top of the page. Houdini knew that his German-speaking mother could not have written it and that a rabbi’s wife would never have marked her words with a cross. Perhaps Abraham, Isaac and Jacob were all, in their way, escape artists; especially Isaac, who needed to figure out how to untie himself on Mount Moriah, which just happens to show up in this week’s Torah portion. Perhaps synagogues will mention Harry Houdini this Shabbat. Perhaps they will remember the rabbi’s son from Appleton, who never sought to escape his essential identity. featured.content: Get RNS’ thoughtful, essential religion reporting every morning. Sign up for free! (The Conversation) — At a campaign rally , in Port Huron, Michigan, on Oct. 25, 2026, President Donald Trump accused U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed of being a “jihadist” who wants to impose Sharia law – Islamic law – in the United States. His comments reflect a broader pattern among Republican politicians of portraying Sharia as a threat to the American legal system. In March 2026, Texas legislators launched the Sharia Free Texas Caucus, a group dedicated to preventing what its members describe as the spread of Islamic law in Texas. Its founder, state Rep. Brent Money, has characterized Sharia as “an entire civilizational legal structure” that threatens American law and institutions. That same month, nearly 95% of Texas Republican primary voters backed a nonbinding proposition declaring that “ Texas should prohibit Sharia Law .” The movement extends beyond Texas. In Congress, the Sharia Free America Caucus , established in December 2025, grew to 68 Republican lawmakers from 25 states in just six months. These efforts reflect a long-standing claim , frequently invoked by anti-Sharia activists, that Muslims are seeking to establish a parallel legal system that will eventually replace American law. But this rhetoric raises a more basic question: What exactly is Sharia, and what does it actually mean for Muslims to follow it while living in the United States? I am a law professor who studies religious liberty . My 2019 book, “ When Islam Is Not a Religion ,” examined how ordinary Muslim religious practices come to be treated as political threats, and I recently documented that pattern in Texas . The Sharia controversy shows how this happens. Sharia is not a single legal code In Arabic, “sharia” means a path or way, literally “ the path to a watering place .” For Muslims, it refers to the divinely ordained way of living a moral and religious life, guided by the Quran and the teachings of the Prophet Muhammad. Sharia guides Muslims how to pray, when to fast, what to eat and how much to give to charity. It also addresses marriage and divorce. These rules span what Americans would sort into law, ethics, manners and worship, as law professor and an authority on Islamic law Asifa Quraishi-Landes has explained . This distinction matters because Americans often think of law as something established and enforced by the state. Sharia is broader than that. A Muslim who avoids pork or prays five times a day may see each practice as part of following Sharia, but neither requires a separate legal court or government enforcement. Rules governing marriage, divorce and inheritance, by contrast, may have legal consequences, though how they are interpreted and applied varies across Islamic traditions. Indeed, as Quraishi-Landes notes, Sharia itself obliges Muslims to follow the law of the land wherever they live. Who decides what Sharia requires? Muslims do not all agree on how Sharia should be interpreted. They distinguish between Sharia, which they regard as the divine ideal, and “ fiqh,” the human effort to understand and apply it . In other words, Muslims believe Sharia comes from God, but people must figure out what it requires in practice. Because people can disagree, interpretations can differ and change over time. For Muslims, Sharia is an expression of divine guidance. Bay Ismoyo/AFP via Getty Images Sunni Islam’s four major schools and Shiite Islam’s legal traditions sometimes reach different conclusions about matters such as marriage, divorce and financial transactions. For example, scholars differ on whether Muslims can take out conventional mortgages to buy homes, given Islamic prohibitions on interest, and on the conditions under which a marriage can be dissolved. They continue to debate newer questions, too, such as whether organ donation is permissible or how modern banking can comply with Islamic principles . No single institution speaks for all Muslims. Yet political debates often treat Sharia as a fixed rule book, when much of the Islamic legal tradition consists of ongoing disagreements about what its rules mean and how they should apply. How does Sharia work in the US? Muslims are subject to the same laws as everyone else in the United States. Their religious commitments may guide personal decisions about marriage, divorce, finances and everyday conduct, but Sharia has no independent legal authority. Muslims can follow religious rules voluntarily, but those rules cannot override American law. This is not unique to Islam. Religious communities across the country have long used their own procedures to resolve disputes. For example, many Orthodox Jewish couples sign prenuptial agreements committing them to appear before a Jewish religious court, known as a beth din, if their marriage breaks down. The court can then help facilitate a religious divorce, including addressing situations in which a husband refuses to grant his wife a religious divorce. Christian organizations likewise offer biblical mediation and arbitration to resolve conflicts according to religious principles. Muslims can similarly turn to religious scholars or mediators for guidance on family or financial disputes. These arrangements are generally voluntary, and any legally enforceable agreement must comply with American law. A religious ruling does not become binding simply because a religious authority issues it. Like other religious communities, Muslims may organize aspects of their personal lives around their faith, but they do so within the framework of American law. Can American courts enforce Sharia? Critics often claim Sharia is gaining a foothold in the courts. The concern usually arises when Muslims ask a court to recognize a religious contract or arbitration. Consider an Islamic marriage contract promising the wife a marriage gift, known as “mahr,” some or all of which may be payable if the couple divorces. A court asked to enforce it does not decide what Islamic theology requires. It asks whether the agreement meets ordinary contract law. In 2020, a Maryland appeals court held that a “mahr” could be enforced only under the same secular standards that apply to any agreement between spouses. In other words, the court’s job is to determine whether the couple’s agreement is legally enforceable, just as it would with any other contract. It is not enforcing Islamic religious law. Courts may apply what the Supreme Court calls “ neutral principles of law .” That simply means applying ordinary legal rules without deciding religious questions. A judge can determine whether two people entered into a valid contract, for example, but cannot decide which interpretation of Islam is religiously correct. As law professor Haider Ala Hamoudi has observed , courts can enforce a “mahr” agreement precisely because doing so does not require them to interpret Islamic law. Arbitration works the same way. Texas Gov. Greg Abbott has called Islamic panels “ Sharia tribunals masquerading as legal courts .” Yet the Beth Din of America also structures its proceedings so civil courts can enforce its rulings, as do Christian arbitrators. Courts can enforce voluntary arbitration awards and can also vacate them for fraud or overreach. For example, suppose a Muslim couple voluntarily agree to have a religious arbitrator resolve a financial dispute. If the arbitrator orders one spouse to pay the other US$10,000, a court may enforce that decision just as it would any other arbitration award. But if one spouse was coerced into participating or the arbitrator exceeded the authority the couple had agreed to give them, a court could set the decision aside. A religious arbitrator cannot override a statute or the Constitution. Why is Sharia so controversial? Protesters in Toronto, Canada, call for an end to Sharia law in Iran, on Sept. 20, 2018. (The Conversation) — — 在2026年10月25日密歇根州休伦港的一场竞选集会上,唐纳德·特朗普总统指责美国参议院候选人阿卜杜勒·赛义德(Abdul El-Sayed)是一位想在美国推行伊斯兰教法 — — 伊斯兰法的"犹太教主义者". 他的评论反映了共和党政治人物中将伊斯兰教法描绘为对美国法律制度的威胁的更宽泛模式. 2026年3月,德克萨斯州立法者发起了"伊斯兰教自由德克萨斯州核心小组",这个小组致力于防止其成员所说的"伊斯兰法在德克萨斯的传播". 其创始人布伦特·钱州将伊斯兰教说成是威胁美国法律和机构的“整个文明法律结构”。 同月,近95%的德克萨斯州共和党人支持一项不具约束力的主张,宣称“德克萨斯州应当禁止伊斯兰教法 ” 。 运动扩展到德克萨斯州以外. 在国会,2025年12月成立的"伊斯兰法自由美国核心小组"在短短6个月内从25个州发展到68名共和党议员. 这些努力反映了反沙里亚活动家经常援引的一个长期说法,即穆斯林正在寻求建立一个平行的法律制度,最终取而代之的是美国法律。 但这种言论提出了一个更基本的问题: 伊斯兰教教法究竟是什么,穆斯林在美国生活时遵循它到底意味着什么? 我是研究宗教自由的法学教授。 我的2019年著作“当伊斯兰教不是宗教时 ” 研究了普通穆斯林宗教实践如何被当作政治威胁对待, 伊斯兰教教法的争议说明了这种情况。 伊斯兰教教法并非单一的法典, 对于穆斯林来说,它指的是受《可兰经》和先知穆罕默德的教义指导的神圣的道德和宗教生活方式。 伊斯兰教法指导穆斯林如何祈祷、何时斋戒、吃什么和给慈善捐赠多少。 它还涉及婚姻和离婚。 正如法律教授和伊斯兰法权威Asifa Quraishi-Landes所解释的那样, 这种区分很重要,因为美国人常常认为法律是国家确立和执行的东西. 伊斯兰教教法比这更宽泛。 穆斯林如果每天避去猪肉或祈祷五次,可以将每种习俗视为遵循伊斯兰教法的一部分,但既不需要单独的法院,也不需要政府执行. 相反,关于婚姻、离婚和继承的规则可能会产生法律后果,尽管对这些规则的解释和适用方式因伊斯兰传统而异。 事实上,正如Quraishi-Landes所指出,伊斯兰教教法本身要求穆斯林在他们居住的地方遵守国家的法律。 谁决定伊斯兰教法要求什么? 穆斯林并不都同意如何解释伊斯兰教法。 他们将伊斯兰教教法(他们认为伊斯兰教教法是神圣的理想)与人类理解和应用伊斯兰教教法的努力区分开来。 换句话说,穆斯林认为伊斯兰教法来自上帝,但人们必须知道它在实践中需要什么. 因为人们可以不同意,解释可以不同,随时间而变化. 对穆斯林来说,伊斯兰教法是神通指引的体现. Bay Ismoyo/AFP通过逊尼派伊斯兰教的四所主要学校和什叶派伊斯兰教的法律传统, 例如,鉴于伊斯兰禁止利息,学者们在穆斯林能否拿出常规抵押贷款购买住房以及解除婚姻的条件方面意见不一。 他们继续争论新问题,例如器官捐赠是否允许,现代银行业如何遵守伊斯兰原则。 没有一个机构代表所有穆斯林。 然而,政治辩论往往把伊斯兰教教法视为固定的规则书,而伊斯兰法律传统大多是对其规则的含义和应如何适用存在分歧。 伊斯兰法在美国如何运作? 穆斯林与美国其他所有人一样受同法约束. 他们的宗教承诺可以指导个人对婚姻、离婚、财务和日常行为的决定,但伊斯兰教法没有独立的法律权威。 穆斯林可以自愿遵守宗教规则,但这些规则不能凌驾于美国法律之上。 这并非伊斯兰教所独有。 长期以来,全国各地的宗教团体都利用自己的程序解决争端。 例如,许多东正教犹太教夫妇签署婚前协议,承诺如果他们的婚姻破裂,他们必须到犹太宗教法庭(被称作beth din)出庭。 然后,法院可以帮助促进宗教离婚,包括处理丈夫拒绝准许妻子宗教离婚的情况。 基督教组织同样提供圣经调解和仲裁,以根据宗教原则解决冲突。 穆斯林同样可以求助于宗教学者或调解人,就家庭或经济纠纷提供指导。 这些安排一般是自愿的,任何可依法执行的协议都必须符合美国法律. 仅仅因为宗教当局发布宗教裁决,宗教裁决并不具有约束力。 和其他宗教团体一样,穆斯林可以围绕自己的信仰组织个人生活的各个方面,但他们在美国法律框架内这样做. 美国法院能否执行伊斯兰教法? 批评者常常声称伊斯兰教正在法院获得立足点。 当穆斯林要求法院承认一项宗教合同或仲裁时,通常会产生这种关切。 考虑签订伊斯兰婚姻合同,向妻子许诺结婚礼物,称为“马赫”,如果夫妇离婚,可以支付部分或全部。 要求执行的法院并不决定伊斯兰神学需要什么。 它询问协议是否符合普通合同法。 2020年,马里兰州的一个上诉法院认为,只有在适用于配偶之间任何协议的同样世俗标准下,才能执行“麻将”。 换句话说,法院的职责是确定夫妻双方的协议是否具有法律效力,就像它与任何其他合同一样。 它没有执行伊斯兰宗教法。 法院可适用最高法院所称的“中立法律原则”。 这仅仅意味着适用普通法律规则,而不决定宗教问题。 例如,法官可以确定两人是否签订了有效的合同,但不能决定对伊斯兰教的解释在宗教上是否正确。 正如Haider Ala Hamoudi教授所指出,法院可以执行“麻将”协定,因为这样做并不要求法院解释伊斯兰法。 仲裁同样有效。 德克萨斯州政府Greg Abbott将伊斯兰小组称为“伪装成法院的伊斯兰宗教法庭”。 然而,美国贝斯丁也安排其诉讼程序,以便民事法院能够执行其裁决,基督教仲裁员也是如此。 法院可以执行自愿仲裁裁决,也可以因欺诈或过度侵犯而撤职。 例如,如果穆斯林夫妇自愿同意由宗教仲裁员解决财务纠纷。 如果仲裁员命令配偶一方支付另外1万美元,法院可以执行该决定,如同任何其他仲裁裁决一样。 但是,如果配偶一方被强迫参加,或仲裁员超越了双方同意给予的权力,法院可以撤销裁决。 宗教仲裁员不能凌驾于法规或宪法之上。 为什么伊斯兰教法如此有争议? 加拿大多伦多的抗议者呼吁伊朗结束伊斯兰教法,2018年9月20日. 通过Getty图像的创意触摸成像有限公司/NurPhoto 有的担心来自Certa如何
